                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched in terms of the power of the President of India to make regulation for certain Union Territories under Article 240 of the Indian Constitution?240(1) (c) - Puducherry

                                              Art. 240 President's regulations: (a) Andaman and Nicobar, (b) Lakshadweep, (c) Dadra and Nagar Haveli, (d) Daman and Diu, (e) Puducherry; so 240(1)(c) is not Puducherry.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The President has power to make regulations regarding which of the following?1, 2, 4

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following statements is incorrect?Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under French colonial rule till 1954

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following statements about Sikkim are true? Select the correct answer from the code given below – I. It became an integral part of India in 1975. II. It is considered as a botanist’s paradise. III. Its population is mainly made up of the Lepchas.I, II and III

                                              Sikkim: integral part of India in 1975 (36th Amendment); botanist's paradise (Himalayan hotspot); natives Lepchas, Bhutias, Nepalis; all three true.

                                              • Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Union of India in:1975

                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              • Mizoram has been granted the status of a State by which of the following Constitutional Amendment?53rd

                                              • Consider the following pairs:Only two

                                              • A separate Vananchal State carved out of Bihar can be made possible by –None of these

                                              • Which of the following States of India was formed in 1948?—

                                              • One of the following statements is incorrect. Point out:The State of Mysore was renamed as Tamil Nadu

                                                    The Citizenship

                                                    13 facts · 16 questions · 3 Must know

                                                    Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                    The Citizenship: key facts from the book
                                                    • The Constitution deals with the citizenship from Articles 5 to 11 under Part II.
                                                    • India, like Britain, adopted the system of single citizenship.
                                                    • Article 11 empowers the Parliament to make laws regarding citizenship.
                                                    • The Indian Citizenship Act was passed by Parliament in 1955.
                                                    • It prescribes five ways ofacquiring citizenship – (1) By Birth,

                                                    (2) By Descent, (3) By Registration, (4) By Naturalisation and (5) By incorporation of territory.

                                                    • The Indian Citizenship Act 1955, prescribes three ways of losing citizenship, whether acquired under the Act or prior to it under the Constitution – (1) By Renunciation, (2) By Termination and (3) By Deprivation.
                                                    • Article 6 provides for the rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan.
                                                    • Article 7 provides for the rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan.
                                                    • Article 8 provides for the rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India.
                                                    • Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State are not to be citizens as mentioned in Article 9.
                                                    • As per the Section 5 (1) (a) of the Citizenship Act 1955, a person of Indian origin can acquire citizenship by registration if a person of Indian origin who has been a resident of India for 7 years before applying for registration. The Act has been amended: in 1957, 1985, 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005 and 2015, 2019.
                                                    • Under section 7A of The Citizenship Act, 1955 (inserted by 'The Citizenship Amendment Act, 2015) the Central government may, subject to such conditions, restrictions and manner as may be prescribed, on an application made on this behalf, register as an Overseas Citizen of India cardholder. Under this Amendment Act, it has been provided that no person, who or either of whose parents or grandparents or great grandparents is or has been a citizen of Pakistan, Bangladesh or such other country as the central government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify, shall be eligible for registration as an overseas citizen of India cardholder under this sub-section.
                                                    • The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 was passed by the Parliament of India on 11 December, 2019. It amended the Citizenship Act, 1955 by providing (section 6B) that illegal migrants of Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Parsi, Buddhist and Christian religious minorities who had come to India on or before 31 December, 2014 due to religious persecution from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan shall not be treated as illegal migrants for the purpose of this Act, and by enabling grant of citizenship via certificates of registration/naturalisation, but subject to conditions. (Muslims are not included in this Act). This Act came into force on 10 January, 2020. Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2024 have been notified on 11 March 2024, which are rules for implementing section 6B of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
                                                    • This Act does not apply to the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura, which are included in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.
                                                    • This Act does not apply even in the areas coming to the inner line under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873.
                                                    • In which Part of the Constitution of India we find the provisions relating to citizenship?PART II

                                                    Citizenship → Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11. Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                    • The citizenship provided by the Constitution of India is:Single citizenship

                                                    India → single citizenship for the whole country; USA → dual citizenship (of the federation and of a state). Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                    • Indian citizenship cannot be obtained by –Depositing money in Indian Banks

                                                    Citizenship Act 1955 → citizenship by Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation of territory; never by depositing money in Indian banks.

                                                    Memory aid Better Dads Raise Nice Indians = Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • A citizen of India will loose his or her citizenship if he or she1 and 2 only

                                                    Loss of citizenship (Citizenship Act 1955): renunciation, termination, deprivation. Renouncing or voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship ends it; marrying a foreigner or criticising government does not.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • With reference to India, consider the following statements:1 only

                                                    India: one citizenship and one domicile (from UK). Any citizen, by birth or naturalised, can become President; a naturalised citizen can be deprived of citizenship.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Who among the following is not eligible for registering as overseas citizen of India cardholder under the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2015?Indian who migrated to Pakistan after partition

                                                    OCI cardholder (Section 7A, Citizenship Act 1955): not for an Indian who migrated to Pakistan after Partition; minor child, foreign spouse, specified great-grandchild are eligible.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                    Articles 371A to 371I → special provisions for Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa. USA dual citizenship, India single; naturalised citizen can be deprived.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which country accepted the policy of Dual Citizenship?U.S.A.

                                                    Dual citizenship → USA: citizen of the USA and of the state where he resides. India has single citizenship.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Who/which of the following is competent to prescribe conditions for acquisition of citizenship?Parliament

                                                    Article 11 → Parliament regulates citizenship by law → Citizenship Act 1955; Central Government made Citizenship Rules 2009 under Section 18.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • How many years does a person of Indian origin need to reside in India to become a citizen of India under the Citizenship Act, 1955?7 years

                                                    Registration under Section 5(1)(a), Citizenship Act 1955 → a person of Indian origin must ordinarily reside in India for 7 years.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Who among the following has the exclusive power of determining the issue of citizenship in India?—

                                                    Only Parliament (Article 11) has exclusive power over citizenship; Central Government only frames rules under Section 18, Citizenship Act 1955.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • When was the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2019 passed by Parliament?11 December, 2019

                                                    Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2019: Lok Sabha 9 December; Rajya Sabha 11 December 2019 (passed by Parliament); President's assent 12 December 2019. Must know

                                                    Don't confuse 11 December (Parliament passed) with 12 December (President's assent).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                    • What is the purpose of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?To grant citizenship to presecuted minority groups of Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan

                                                    CAA 2019 → citizenship for persecuted Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan who entered India before end of December 2014.

                                                    Memory aid Three neighbours A-B-P: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan; six non-Muslim communities.

                                                          Fundamental Rights · part 1 of 4

                                                          37 facts · 41 questions · 7 Must know

                                                          Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                          Fundamental Rights: key facts from the book
                                                          • The first explicit Demand for the Fundamental Rights (FR) came in the form of the "Constitution of India Bill, 1895" which was inspired by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The Motilal Nehru Report of1928 demanded inalienable Fundamental Rights for the people of India.
                                                          • The Congress adopted a resolution on Fundamental Rights at the Karachi Session of 1931, presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
                                                          • The Fundamental rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution from Articles 12 to 35.
                                                          • Originally, the Constitution provided for seven fundamental rights – (1) Right to Equality, (2) Right to Freedom, (3) Right against Exploitation, (4) Right to Freedom of religion, (5) Cultural and Educational rights, (6) Right to Property and
                                                          • (7) Right to Constitutional remedies.
                                                          • However, the Right to Property was deleted from the list of fundamental rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
                                                          • Now, the right to property is a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII of the Constitution. Fundamental Rights are the guarantee against the arbitrary actions of the State.
                                                          • The enforcement of fundamental rights (except the rights under Articles 20 and 21) can be suspended during the operation of a national emergency, by an order of the president. These rights are justiciable.
                                                          • Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are often compared with the Bill of Rights in the Constitution of the U.S.A. Part III of the Indian Constitution is rightly regarded as the Magna Carta of India.
                                                          • The Fundamental Rights are defended and guaranteed by the Constitution.
                                                          • Article 14 provides for Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.
                                                          • The Right to equality is enshrined in the Constitution from Articles 14 to 18.
                                                          • Prohibition of discrimination only on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth (Article 15).
                                                          • Article 16- Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
                                                          • Article 17- Abolition of untouchability and prohibition of its practice.
                                                          • Article 18 – Abolition of titles except military and academic.
                                                          • The Right to freedom is described in Articles 19 to 22. Article 19 guarantees all citizens six rights.
                                                          • These are – Article 19(1) (a) – Right to freedom of speech and expression, Article 19 (1) (b) – Right to assemble peacefully and without arms, Article 19(1) (c) – Right to form associations or unions or cooperative societies, Article 19(1) (d) – Right to move freely throughout the territory of India, Article 19 (1)(e) – Right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India and Article 19(1) (g) – Right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade and business.
                                                          • Article 20 provides for protection in respect of conviction for offences.
                                                          • Protection of life and personal liberty is described in Article 21.
                                                          • Eighty
                                                          • – Sixth Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 made free and compulsory education (for all children of the age 6 to 14 years) a fundamental right and added Article 21A.
                                                          • Article 22 provides for protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. Right against exploitation is described in Articles 23 and 24.
                                                          • Article 23 provides for the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour.
                                                          • Article 24 provides for the prohibition of employment of children (below the age of 14 years) in factories, etc.
                                                          • The Right to freedom of religion is described in Articles 25 to 28.
                                                          • Articles 29 and 30 are related to the cultural and educational rights of minorities.
                                                          • Article 32 provides for Constitutional remedies.
                                                          • Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 as 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it/ "heart and soul".
                                                          • The Supreme Court (under Article 32) can issue writs only for the enforcement of fundamental rights, and the High Courts (under Article 226) can issue writs not only for the enforcement of fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
                                                          • Five kinds of writs are mentioned in Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution:
                                                          • (1) Habeas Corpus (to have the body of) – The writ of Habeas Corpus can be issued against both public authorities as well as private individuals who have detained another person to produce the body of the latter before it.
                                                          • If the detention is found to be illegal, the detained person would be set free.
                                                          • This writ is the bulwark of individual liberty against arbitrary detention.

                                                          (2) Mandamus (We command) – It is a command issued by the court against a public official, any public body, a corporation, an inferior court, a tribunal or a government, asking them to perform official duties that one has failed or refused to perform.

                                                          (3) Prohibition (to forbid) – It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent the latter from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction that it does not possess.

                                                          (4) Certiorari (to be certified) – It is issued on the grounds of excess of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction or error of law. It is issued by a higher court to a lower court to transfer a case pending with the latter to itselfor to quash the order of the latter in a case.

                                                          (5) Quo – Warranto (By what authority or warrant) – It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of the claim of a person to a public office.

                                                          • Article 358 provides for the suspension of provisions of Article 19, during emergencies.
                                                          • Article 359 provides for the suspension of the enforcement of fundamental rights except Articles 20 and 21 during emergencies (after the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act).
                                                          • The Supreme Court, in its judgment in the case of Bachan Singh Vs State of Punjab, held that the sentencing discretion inherent in section 302 of the IPC is not violative of Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Indian Constitution.
                                                          • Which one of the following factors constitutes the best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy?Separation of powers

                                                          Best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy → separation of powers (restrains power); not a committed judiciary or centralisation.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which Congress Session passed the resolution of Fundamental Rights in 1931?Karachi

                                                          Fundamental Rights resolution → Karachi Session 1931 (26-31 March, president Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel), with National Economic Programme; endorsed Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which of the following is correct?The Nehru Report (1928) had advocated the inclusion of Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India.

                                                          Nehru Report (1928) advocated including Fundamental Rights in the Constitution; not GoI Act 1935, August Offer 1940 or Cripps Mission 1942.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Who said the following words about Fundamental Rights: "A Fundamental Right should be looked upon, not from the point of view of any particular difficulty of that moment but as something that you want to make permanent in this Constitution"?Jawaharlal Nehru

                                                          Jawaharlal Nehru: a Fundamental Right should be seen not from any moment's difficulty but as something to make permanent in the Constitution.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Who among the following person said for the Fundamental Rights "a pledge to our people and a pact with the civilized world"?Dr. S. Radha Krishnan

                                                          Dr. S. Radhakrishnan: Fundamental Rights are 'a pledge to our people and a pact with the civilized world'.

                                                          Memory aid Pledge + Pact = Philosopher-king Radhakrishnan.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • ‘Fundamental Rights’ are:Justifiable

                                                          Fundamental Rights are justiciable: enforceable by courts, subject to certain restrictions.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • The rights are called Fundamental Rights becausei iv v

                                                          Called Fundamental because written in the Constitution, essential for personality development, and Parliament can't make laws against them (basic structure).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Fundamental Rights –Can be suspended during Emergency

                                                          Fundamental Rights can be suspended only during Emergency (Articles 358, 359); Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended.

                                                          Memory aid 20-21 never done: Articles 20 and 21 survive every Emergency.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights in India:1, 2 and 3 are correct

                                                          Fundamental Rights: guarantee against State action; listed in Part III; help ensure social, economic, political justice (mostly via DPSP, Part IV); they resemble the US Bill of Rights.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Under which Article of the Constitution of India, Fundamental Rights have been provided to citizens?Article 12 to 35

                                                          Fundamental Rights → Part III, Articles 12 to 35; six Fundamental Rights for citizens. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                          • Which Article of the Constitution gives precedence to Constitutional provisions over the laws made by the Union Parliament/State Legislatures?13

                                                          Article 13 → pre- or post-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void to that extent; secures paramountcy of the Constitution on Fundamental Rights. Must know

                                                          Don't confuse Article 245 = extent of laws by Parliament and States; Article 326 = elections to Lok Sabha.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                          • In the Indian Constitution, the right to equality is granted by five Articles, They are:Article 14 to Article 18

                                                          Right to Equality → Articles 14 to 18: 14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 public employment; 17 untouchability abolished; 18 titles abolished. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                          • The Right to Equality is given by-2,3 and 4

                                                          Right to Equality = Articles 14 to 18, so Articles 14, 15, 16 are included; Article 13 is not part of it.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution puts an absolute limitation on the legislative power:Article 14

                                                          Article 14 → equality before law and equal protection of laws for every person (citizen or foreigner); puts a limitation on legislative power. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                          • In which article of the constitution 'Equal Protection of Law' is provided?Article 14

                                                          Equal protection of laws → Article 14 (concept from the American Constitution); with equality before law; for citizens and foreigners.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • A legislation which confers on the executive or administrative authority an unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power in the matter of application of law violates which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?Article 14

                                                          A law giving the executive unguided, uncontrolled discretionary power → violates Article 14 (ultra vires).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • What is meant by 'Rule of Law'?One act for all and one judiciary for all

                                                          Rule of Law → one law for all and one judiciary for all; no one, however highly placed, is above the law.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Prohibition of discrimination on the ground of religion etc. (Article 15 of the Constitution of India) is a Fundamental Right classifiable under:The Right to Equality

                                                          Article 15 (no discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth) falls under Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following fundamental rights was amended as a result of the decision of the Supreme Court of India in ‘State of Madras Vs. Champakam Dorairajan’ case:Right against discrimination

                                                          State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan → First Amendment (1951) added Article 15(4): special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Under which article of the Constitution reservations in admission to educational institutions, including private and unaided, to OBCs/ST/SC is made?Article 15(5)

                                                          Article 15(5) → reservation in admission to educational institutions, including private aided or unaided ones (not minority institutions), for SC, ST and backward classes.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • The provisions of reservation of O.B.C. is made in the Constitution under which Articles?Article 15 (IV) & 16 (IV)

                                                          OBC reservation → Article 15(4) (special provisions for backward classes, SC, ST) and Article 16(4) (reservation in appointments or posts for backward classes).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • According to which Article of the Indian Constitution,Article 16 (2)

                                                          Article 16(2) → no citizen barred from State employment on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence.

                                                          Don't confuse Article 15 lists religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth only; 'descent' and 'residence' appear in Article 16(2).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality of opportunity to all citizens of India in matters relating to public employment?Article 16 (1) and 16(2)

                                                          Equality of opportunity in public employment for all citizens → Article 16(1) and 16(2).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following is not included in the fundamental right to equality as enshrined in the Indian Constitution?Economic equality

                                                          Right to Equality covers equality before law (Article 14), social equality (Article 15), equal opportunity (Article 16); not economic equality.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Assertion (A): The State can treat unequal differently with the objective of creating a level playing field in the social, economic and political spheres.Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                          Both A and R true, R explains A: Article 14 permits reasonable classification to treat unequals differently, but among equals law must be equal and equally administered.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Consider the following statements:Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

                                                          SC: reservation under Article 16(4) is limited by Article 335 (efficiency of administration); but Article 335 does not define 'efficiency of administration'.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Under which Amendment Act was the reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes ensured by inserting Clause '4A' in Article 16?77th Amendment Act, 1995

                                                          77th Amendment Act, 1995 → inserted Article 16(4A): reservation in promotion for SC and ST.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which of the following enabled the Supreme Court of India to deduce a fundamental right to equal pay for equal work:(a), (b) and (c) all read together

                                                          Equal pay for equal work → deduced by the Supreme Court from 'Socialist' in the Preamble read with Articles 14, 16 and 39(d).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which of the following Article/Articles read with the word ‘Socialist’ used in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution enabled the Supreme Court to deduce a fundamental right to Equal Pay for Equal Work?Articles 14 and 16

                                                          Randhir Singh v. Union of India → 'Equal pay for equal work' deduced from Articles 14 and 16 read with the Preamble ('Socialist') and Article 39(d). Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                          • Under what provision of the Constitution, untouchability has been abolished?Art. 17

                                                          Article 17 → untouchability abolished; its practice in any form forbidden; enforcing any disability arising from it is an offence punishable by law. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution abolished untouchability:Article 17

                                                          Untouchability abolished → Article 17 (not Articles 15, 16 or 18). Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                          • Under which Article Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have been granted fundamental, socio economic, political and cultural rights?Article 17

                                                          Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) is a 'statement of principle' to end humiliation of Dalits and secure their fundamental, socio-economic, political and cultural rights.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following categories of Fundamental Rights incorporates protection against untouchability as a form of discrimination?Right to Equality

                                                          Protection against untouchability (Article 17) is part of the Right to Equality, not the Right against Exploitation or Right to Freedom.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Prohibition and abolishment of untouchability may be achieved by1, 2, and 3

                                                          Untouchability is ended by laws, better education and public awareness, not by providing jobs; Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955 made it a punishable offence.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Following are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R):Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).

                                                          Both true, R explains A: untouchability is a worst form of structural violence (built into social structure), practised in the name of religious sanctions.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution belongs to a different category:—

                                                          Articles 14, 15, 16 → Right to Equality; Article 19 → Right to Freedom (speech, peaceful assembly, associations). By this grouping Article 19 is the odd one.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • In the Indian Constitution the ‘Right to Freedom’ is granted by four Articles which are –Article – 19 to Article – 22

                                                          Right to Freedom → Articles 19 to 22: 19 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence); 20 protection in conviction for offences; 21 life and personal liberty.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          Practise this hour: 40 questions

                                                            Spaced review: 9 questions from earlier hours

                                                              Your weak questions

                                                                Hour 12 →

                                                                Hour 12 of 72 · Learn

                                                                Fundamental Rights · part 2 of 4

                                                                36 facts · 43 questions · 7 Must know

                                                                Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                • Which of the follwing freedoms is not guaranteed by the Indian Constitution under Article 19?Freedom to own, acquire and dispose of property

                                                                Article 19(1) guarantees 6 freedoms (speech, assembly, associations, movement, residence, profession); freedom to own, acquire and dispose of property is not among them.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following rights is/are not included in the ‘Right to Freedom’ under Article 19(1)?Only 1

                                                                Article 19(1): speech and expression (a), assemble peaceably (b), practise any profession (g). Equal opportunity in public employment is Article 16 (Right to Equality), not Right to Freedom.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article of the Constitution of India is related with Freedom of the Press.Article 19

                                                                Freedom of the Press → not expressly in the Constitution; the Supreme Court held it is part of freedom of speech and expression, Article 19(1)(a). Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                • Indian Constitution does not give right to freedom of the Press, but it is included in-Article 19(1)(a)

                                                                Press freedom is not explicit in the Constitution; it is included in Article 19(1)(a), freedom of speech and expression. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Freedom of News Papers in India-Specially provided by Article 19(1)(a)

                                                                Freedom of newspapers → within Article 19(1)(a); Sakal Papers Ltd v. Union of India (1961): press freedom is part of freedom of speech and expression.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The Supreme Court has held that hoisting the National Flag atop the private buildings is a fundamental right of every citizen under:Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution

                                                                Supreme Court: hoisting the National Flag atop private buildings is every citizen's fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • As a part of the Right to Freedom, which one of the followings does not form part of“Freedom to Assemble Peaceably and Without Arms”?Gherao officials not performing their duties

                                                                Article 19(1)(b) → assemble peaceably and without arms; Article 19(3) → reasonable restrictions for public order. Gheraoing officials is not covered.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • By which of the following grounds, a citizen’s freedom of expression may not be subjected to restriction?Unbecoming criticism

                                                                Article 19(2) grounds: sovereignty and integrity, security of State, foreign relations, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to offence; not 'unbecoming criticism'.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Reasonable restrictions on 'Exercise of Freedom of Speech and Expression' under Article 19(2) are justified in the interest of which of the following conditions?Only I, II and IV

                                                                Article 19(2) restrictions on speech include security of State, defamation and public order; 'sedition' is not a listed ground.

                                                                Don't confuse Sedition is not an Article 19(2) ground; 'incitement to an offence' is.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The constitution of India provides for reasonable1 and 2 are correct

                                                                Reasonable restrictions (Articles 19(2) to 19(6)) must safeguard general public interest and may reflect prevailing social values and needs; Directive Principles cannot be bypassed.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article of the Constitution of Indian Republic relates to the Protection of'Life and Personal Liberty'?Article 21

                                                                Article 21 → protection of life and personal liberty. Article 19 → freedoms of speech etc.; 20 → conviction for offences; 22 → arrest and detention.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • In which Article of Indian Constitution Doctrine of Due Process of Law is included?21

                                                                Article 21: no person deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law; the question links due process to Article 21.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article of the Indian Constitution protects person’s right to travel abroad:21

                                                                Right to travel abroad → Article 21; Maneka Gandhi v. UOI (1978).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Identify the incorrect statement regarding Judicial Interpretation of Article 21 after Supreme Court’s verdict in Maneka Gandhi Case, 1978.The burden lies on the petitioner to prove that the procedure established by law which deprives him of his life or personal liberty is arbitrary.

                                                                Maneka Gandhi 1978 (7 judges): Articles 14, 19, 21 not mutually exclusive; life includes dignity; procedure close to US procedural due process. Petitioner-burden statement is wrong.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following has been recognized as a fundamental right by the Supreme Court of India?1, 2 and 3

                                                                SC-recognised Fundamental Rights: Right to Shelter (Chameli Singh v. State of U.P. 1995, Article 21), Right to Travel Abroad (Satwant Singh), Equal Pay for Equal Work.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following rights is available under Article 19(1)(d) read with Article 21:Right to privacy

                                                                Right to privacy → implicit in Article 21 (with 19(1)(d)); Govind v. State of M.P. (1975), Malak Singh v. State of Punjab (1980); 'right to be let alone'. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                • Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement?Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part III.

                                                                Right to Privacy → intrinsic part of Article 21 and the freedoms in Part III (Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy?Article 21

                                                                K.S. Puttaswamy case (nine-judge bench, 24 August 2017): Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21, part of the Part III freedoms.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one's right to marry the person of one's choice?Article 21

                                                                Right to marry a person of one's choice → Article 21 (Lata Singh v. State of U.P., 2006; Hadiya case: right to choose a partner).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following does not fall within the purview of article 21 of the Constitution?Capital punishment

                                                                Article 21 covers medical aid to the injured, safety from sexual harassment at work, pollution-free water; capital punishment is not barred by it (Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following rights cannot be suspended or restricted even during National Emergency?Right to life and personal liberty.

                                                                After 44th Amendment (1978), Article 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even in National Emergency; Article 19 rights auto-suspended if Emergency is on war or external aggression.

                                                                Memory aid 44 fixed 21: after the 44th Amendment, Article 21 never goes.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The scope of the Article 21 of the Constitution was expanded to include Right to Education, because of the decision of Supreme Court in the caseUnnikrishnan v/s Andhra Pradesh

                                                                Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) → Right to Education flows from Article 21; free education for children up to 14 years.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Right to education to all children between the age group of 6 to 14 years is -A Fundamental Right

                                                                Right to Education (6-14 years) is a Fundamental Right: Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act 2002 inserted Article 21A; RTE Act 2009; added from 1 April 2010. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Assertion (A): The state shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age group of six to fourteen years.Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                Article 21A: State gives free and compulsory education to children aged six to fourteen; education is indispensable to the right to development as a human right (R explains A).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India?2 and 3

                                                                Right against Exploitation → Article 23 (no human trafficking, begar, forced labour) and Article 24 (no child below fourteen in factory, mine, hazardous work). Untouchability (Article 17) is not. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Which provision of the fundamental rights is directly related to the exploitation of children?Art. 24

                                                                Article 24 → no child under 14 years employed in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Article 24 of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of child in factories related to hazardous works. Such prohibition isAbsolute prohibition

                                                                Article 24's ban on employing children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work is an absolute prohibition.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following is not a part of the Article 20 of the Constitution of India?Prohibition Against Torture

                                                                Article 20: no ex-post facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination. Protection from torture comes under Article 21, not 20. Child exploitation → Article 24. Must know

                                                                Memory aid Article 20 = three 'No's: ex-post facto, double jeopardy, self-incrimination.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                • Child Rights are protected in Article_______ofICCPR.24

                                                                Child rights → Article 24 of the ICCPR; Article 24 of the Indian Constitution also protects children.

                                                                Memory aid Same number twice: 24 in ICCPR and 24 in our Constitution.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article of the Constitution provides protection to the accused regarding conviction from double-bar and self-incrimination?Article 20

                                                                Article 20(2) → no one punished twice for the same offence (double jeopardy); Article 20(3) → no self-incrimination.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • An accused of any offence cannot be compelled to be a witness against himself, which Article of Indian Constitution provides for this?Article 20(3)

                                                                Article 20(3) → an accused cannot be compelled to be a witness against himself (self-incrimination); accused presumed innocent till guilt is proved.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • “No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.” Under which Article, the above preservation of conviction for crime is given?Article 20

                                                                Article 20(2) → no one prosecuted and punished twice for the same offence: Doctrine of Double Jeopardy (maxim: Nemo Debet Bis Vexari).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which Article gives safeguard to the Fundamental Rights of arrested person?Article 22

                                                                Article 22 → an arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest and may consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following is not correctly matched?Article 22.2 – Parliament may by law prescribe the circumstances under which a person may be detained for a period longer than three months.

                                                                Wrong pair: Article 22(2) is not about Parliament allowing detention beyond three months; 22(2) → arrested person produced before nearest magistrate within twenty-four hours.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Under the Preventive Detention Act, a person can be arrested without trial for –3 months

                                                                Article 22(4) → a preventive detention law cannot authorise detention for longer than 3 months.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Under Preventive Detention, a person can be detained without trial for –Three months

                                                                Preventive detention: a person can be detained without trial for at most three months (Article 22(4)).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                Practise this hour: 40 questions

                                                                  Spaced review: 9 questions from earlier hours

                                                                    Your weak questions

                                                                      Hour 13 →

                                                                      Hour 13 of 72 · Learn

                                                                      Fundamental Rights · part 3 of 4

                                                                      33 facts · 39 questions · 7 Must know

                                                                      Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                      • Consider the following statements:Only one

                                                                      Article 355 → Union must protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance (true). POTA 2002 made confession before police admissible; Article 22(5) lets detainee make representation.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • With reference to India, consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                      Parole is not a right in India (claim not absolute, even with a sufficient case); State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • The provision of ‘Right to Freedom of Religion’ includes-I, II and III

                                                                      Article 25 → freedom of conscience, profession, practice, propagation of religion; Sikhs may wear and carry Kirpans; State can legislate social reform. No right of religious bodies to convert people. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                      • The word ‘Hindu’ in Article 25 of the Constitution of India does not include –Parsis

                                                                      'Hindu' in Article 25 includes Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists; it does not include Parsis. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • According to Article 25 of the Constitution 'Right to Freedom of Religion' is not subjected to –Humanism

                                                                      Article 25 freedom of religion is subject to public order, morality and health; 'humanism' is not a limit.

                                                                      Memory aid Religion's limits = 'PMH': Public order, Morality, Health.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • What are the restrictions in the freedom to manage religious affairs in the Article 26 of the constitution?(i) (iv) (v)

                                                                      Article 26 (religious denominations manage own affairs, institutions, property) → subject to public order, morality and health only.

                                                                      Don't confuse National security, education and secularism are not Article 26 limits.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following is not correctly matched?Article 29 - Freedom of establishment and administration of educational institutions by minorities

                                                                      Wrong pair: Article 29 → protection of minorities' interests; minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions → Article 30. Articles 23, 24, 26 pairs are correct.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?Right of minorities to establish - Article 31 and administer educational institutions

                                                                      Wrong pair: minorities' educational institutions → Article 30, not 31. Article 31 (property acquisition) repealed by 44th Amendment 1978; property now a legal right, Article 300-A.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which Article of the Constitution protects the 'Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice'?30

                                                                      Article 30 → minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Article 29 → protection of minorities' interests; 26 → manage religious affairs. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                      Article 30 does not define 'minorities'; Constitution recognises only religious and linguistic minorities. Both true, but R does not explain A.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • The Constitution of India recognizes –Religious and linguistic minorities

                                                                      Constitution recognises religious and linguistic minorities (not ethnic). Article 29 → conserve distinct language, script, culture; Article 30 → minorities' educational institutions.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following is given the power to enforce the Fundamental Rights by the Constitution?The Supreme Court and High Courts

                                                                      Fundamental Rights enforced by the Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226); Article 13 gives them judicial review to void laws violating them.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • The Guardian of Fundamental Rights isJudiciary

                                                                      Guardian of Fundamental Rights → Judiciary (Supreme Court under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226). Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following is regarded as the protector of fundamental rights of citizens and Guardian of the Constitution of India?The Supreme Court

                                                                      Supreme Court → protector of citizens' Fundamental Rights and Guardian of the Constitution: enforces rights via Article 32 and interprets the Constitution.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following statements is not correct?The President of India is the Guardian of Fundamental Rights under the Constitution.

                                                                      Guardian of Fundamental Rights is the Judiciary, not the President. True: K.M. Munshi was in the Drafting Committee; Balwant Rai Mehta Committee 1957 recommended Panchayati Raj.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following rights can be enforced under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution?Fundamental Rights

                                                                      Article 32 enforces only Fundamental Rights (Part III) through writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following Article is called the "Heart and Soul" of the Indian Constitution?Article 32

                                                                      Article 32 → 'heart and soul' of the Constitution (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar): lets a person directly approach the Supreme Court when Fundamental Rights are violated.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following rights was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the ‘Heart and Soul of the Constitution’?Right to Constitutional Remedies

                                                                      Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) → 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' per Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; without it the Constitution would be a nullity. Must know

                                                                      Memory aid 32 teeth guard the mouth; Article 32 guards all Fundamental Rights.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                      • Consider the following statements:(A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

                                                                      Both true, R explains A: Ambedkar called Article 32 the very soul of the Constitution because it gives an effective remedy against violation of Fundamental Rights.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Consider the following statements concerning the powers of the Supreme Court to issue certain writs to stop violation of Fundamental Rights-Both (1) and (2)

                                                                      Article 32(2) → SC issues Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari; Article 32(3) → Parliament may by law empower any other court with these powers.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Under which of the following Article of the Constitution of India, the Supreme Court is empowered to issue different 'Writs' for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights of the citizens?Article 32

                                                                      Article 32 → Supreme Court issues five writs for Fundamental Rights; Article 226 → High Court issues them for Fundamental Rights and 'any other purpose'.

                                                                      Don't confuse High Court writ power (Article 226) is wider than the Supreme Court's (Article 32).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following writs is regarded as the greatest safeguard for the liberty of a person?Habeas Corpus

                                                                      Habeas Corpus → greatest safeguard of personal liberty: detainer must produce the detained person before court; freed if detention has no legal justification.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following writs can be issued by a High Court to secure the liberty of the individual?Habeas Corpus

                                                                      High Court (Article 226) secures individual liberty through Habeas Corpus → release of a person detained illegally.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • The writ which may be filed for protection of right to Personal Freedom is -Habeas Corpus

                                                                      Habeas Corpus = 'to have the body of': court has the detained person brought before it to check the grounds of detention → protects personal liberty.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Match it.iv iii v i ii

                                                                      Habeas Corpus → let us have the body; Mandamus → we command; Prohibition → writ to subordinate courts; Certiorari → be more fully informed; Quo-Warranto → by which authority.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?Prohibition 'To be certified'

                                                                      Wrong pair: 'To be certified' → Certiorari, not Prohibition. Certiorari: higher court takes over a pending case from a lower court or quashes its order.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following constitutional remedies is also known as 'postmortem'?Certiorari

                                                                      'Postmortem' writ → Certiorari (higher courts re-examine subordinate court decisions); Quo warranto (checks a claim to public office) also has a postmortem sense.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • In which petition, Judiciary orders Executives to perform their duty?Mandamus

                                                                      Mandamus ('we command') → superior court orders a lower court, government officer or institution to perform its duty. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Fundamental Rights): (Articles)Right to Freedom: Articles 23-24 of Religion

                                                                      Wrong pair: Articles 23-24 = Right against Exploitation, not Freedom of Religion (25-28). Equality 14-18; Freedom 19-22; Cultural and Educational 29-30.

                                                                      Memory aid Block sizes five-four-two-four-two: Equality, Freedom, Exploitation, Religion, Cultural-Educational.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Correctly match the following:(iv) (iii) (ii) (i)

                                                                      Cultural and Educational Rights → Articles 29-30; Constitutional Remedies → Article 32; Right against Exploitation → Articles 23-24; Right to Equality → Articles 14-18.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Match List-I (Article of Indian Constitution) with List II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:2 4 3 1

                                                                      16(2) → no discrimination in public appointment; 29(2) → no denial of admission to State-aided institutions; 30(1) → minorities' educational institutions; 31(1) → property deprived only by law.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?Protection against arrest and Art. 23 detention

                                                                      Wrong pair: protection against arrest and detention → Article 22, not 23. Correct: untouchability 17, freedom of religion 25, minorities' interests 29.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
