                                                                            Fundamental Rights · part 4 of 4

                                                                            31 facts · 45 questions · 7 Must know

                                                                            Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                            • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer by using the code given below the list:3 4 1 2

                                                                            Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment; Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights → Keshvanand Bharti case; Basic Structure → Minerva Mills case (per this key); trafficking ban → Article 23.

                                                                            Don't confuse Basic Structure was first propounded in Kesavananda Bharati and affirmed in Minerva Mills; this key pairs it with Minerva Mills.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following statement/s is/are incorrect? A. Part III on Fundamental Rights of the Constitution is based upon Bill of Rights of the U.S.A. B. "Right to Die" is a Fundamental Right under Article 21 of the Constitution. C. Indian Constitution is a complete Federal Constitution. D. Fundamental Rights can be removed under the Indian Constitution. Code:Only B, C and D

                                                                            Incorrect: Right to Die is not a Fundamental Right; Constitution is quasi-federal, not fully federal; FRs can be amended, not removed. Correct: Part III resembles US Bill of Rights.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India declare the prevalence of Fundamental rights over Directive Principles of the State Policy in case of conflict between the two?The State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)

                                                                            State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) → in a conflict, Fundamental Rights prevail over Directive Principles (case on community-based medical college seat reservation).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • By which of the following case Parliament got the right to amend Fundamental Rights?Keshvananda Bharati Case

                                                                            Keshvananda Bharati (1973) → Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights. Earlier: Shankari Prasad 1951, Sajjan Singh 1965 allowed it; Golaknath 1967 denied it.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Identify the correct chronological sequence of the following:1, 2, 3, 4

                                                                            Chronology: Shankari Prasad (1951) → Sajjan Singh (1965) → Golaknath (1967, reversed both) → Kesavananda Bharati.

                                                                            Memory aid S-S-G-K: Shankari, Sajjan, Golaknath, Kesavananda, in alphabet-like march.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The Supreme Court of India has propounded the ‘Doctrine of Basic Structure’ of the Constitution in which of the following cases?Keshavananda Bharati Vs. Kerala State

                                                                            Doctrine of Basic Structure → Keshvananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), majority judgment; approved in Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980). Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Select the correct chronological order of the following judgements dealing with Fundamental Rights: (A) Golaknath v/s State of Punjab (B) Keshvananda Bharati v/s State of Kerala (C) Minerva Mills v/s Union of India (D) A.K Gopalan v/s State of Madras Select the correct answer:(D), (A), (B),(C)

                                                                            Chronology: A.K. Gopalan (1950) → Golaknath (1967) → Keshvananda Bharati (1973) → Minerva Mills (1980).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • What is the position of the Right to Property in India?Legal right available to any person

                                                                            Right to Property → removed as a Fundamental Right by 44th Amendment Act 1978; now Article 300-A, a legal right available to any person (not citizens only). Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following statements –Only 2

                                                                            Right to Property: legal right, not Fundamental. Article 301 = freedom of trade, commerce, intercourse. 44th Amendment 1978 (Janta Party Government) omitted 19(1)(f), inserted Article 300-A. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                            • By which amendment the Right to Property was abolished?44th

                                                                            Right to Property removed from Fundamental Rights → 44th (Forty-fourth) Constitutional Amendment; now a legal right. Must know

                                                                            Memory aid 44th = 'forty-forfeit': property forfeited its fundamental status.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 10 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following is not among the six fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India?Right to protest

                                                                            The six Fundamental Rights do not include a 'Right to protest'; Equality, against Exploitation and Freedom of Religion are included.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Indian Constitution does not grant which of the following rights?Right of Equal Shelter

                                                                            Constitution grants Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Freedom (19-22), Freedom of Religion (25-28); there is no 'Right of Equal Shelter'.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following is not a fundamental right granted by the Indian Constitution to the citizens?Right to Information

                                                                            Right to Information is not expressly in the Constitution; the Supreme Court reads it into freedom of speech and expression, Article 19(1)(a).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following statements: No one can be compelled to sing the National Anthem since –1, 2 and 3 are correct

                                                                            Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala: no one can be compelled to sing the National Anthem; forcing it violates Articles 19(1)(a) and 25(1); no law obliges singing.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Choose the fundamental rights available to Indian Citizen but not to aliens: I. Freedom of Speech and Expression II. Equality Before the Law III. Right of Minorities IV. Protection of Life and LibertyI and III

                                                                            Citizens only, not aliens: freedom of speech and expression (Article 19) and minorities' cultural-educational rights (Article 29). Equality before law and life-liberty are for all.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Fundamental Rights provided by which of the following groups of Articles are granted only to 'Citizens' of India?Articles 15, 16, 19 and 30

                                                                            Citizens-only Fundamental Rights → Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30.

                                                                            Memory aid Two pairs plus one: 15-16, 29-30, and 19.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following fundamental rights is not available to foreign citizens?Right to Freedom of Expression

                                                                            Freedom of expression (Article 19) is citizens-only. Also for foreigners: equality before law (Article 14), Articles 20, 21, 21-A, right against exploitation, freedom of religion. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following rights is available to all persons under the Indian Constitution?Right to Equal Protection of the Law.

                                                                            Equal protection of laws (Article 14) → all persons; right against discrimination, speech (19(1)(a)) and cultural-educational rights (29-30) → citizens only.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following rights are not available to all persons in India? Select your answer by using the code given below:2, 3, 4

                                                                            Equality before law (Article 14) → every person. Citizens only: right against discrimination, free movement (19(1)(d)), right to contest elections.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following rights conferred by the Constitution of India is also available to non-citizens?Right to Constitutional Remedies

                                                                            Right to Constitutional Remedies → for citizens and non-citizens; freedom of speech, free movement and acquiring property → citizens only.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • A British citizen staying in India cannot claim right to –Freedom of Trade and Profession

                                                                            A British citizen in India cannot claim freedom of trade and profession (Article 19(1)(g), citizens only); can claim equality before law, life and liberty, religious freedom.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following rights is not enjoyed by a British Citizen residing in India?Freedom of Trade and Profession

                                                                            Citizens-only rights: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, 30; so a British citizen in India lacks freedom of trade and profession (Article 19).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • In India, if a religious sect/community is given the status of a national minority, what special advantages is it entitled to?1 and 3

                                                                            National minority status → can run own educational institutions and benefit from PM's 15-Point Programme; no automatic Lok Sabha nomination by the President.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Bonded Labour was abolished in India, by an Act of Parliament enacted in the year –1976

                                                                            Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act 1976 replaced the Ordinance of 25 October 1975; Article 23(1) bans traffic in human beings and forced labour. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • The child labour was prohibited in hazardous employment by–All of the above

                                                                            Child labour in hazardous work banned by all: Article 24 (no child under fourteen), UN Charter (childhood needs special assistance), and Supreme Court judgment of December 10, 1996. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Fill in the blank: _________without duties are like men without shadows.’Rights

                                                                            Sir Ernest Barker: 'Rights without duties are like men without shadows'.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • In the context of India, which one the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties?Rights are correlative with Duties

                                                                            In India, rights and duties are correlative (two faces of the same thing); Holland: every right implies forbearance (a duty) by others.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following statements is correct?Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.

                                                                            Rights are claims of citizens against the State; they restrict State power and guard against State action.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Arrange the following states chronologically with respect to enactment of ‘Right to Service Act’:(i), (ii), (iv), (iii)

                                                                            Right to Service Act, by Official Gazette dates: Punjab → Assam → Gujarat → Maharashtra.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The concept of 'Right to Service' originated inGreat Britain

                                                                            'Right to Service' (time-bound delivery of public services) originated in Great Britain; India's 2011 Bill on time-bound delivery and grievance redressal was not passed.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The aim of citizen's charter is not -To create effective hearing system of public demands

                                                                            Citizen's Charter aims: quality, time-bound service delivery, citizen-friendly and accountable governance; creating a hearing system for public demands is not its aim.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  Directive Principles of State Policy: key facts from the book
                                                                                  • The Directive Principles of State Policy are mentioned in Part IV of the Indian Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
                                                                                  • The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy is borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
                                                                                  • Article 37 deals with the application of the principles contained in this part.
                                                                                  • The Directive Principles are non – justiciable.
                                                                                  • The Constitution (Article 37) itself says that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
                                                                                  • They embody the concept of a ‘Welfare State’.
                                                                                  • Article 38 says, the State is to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
                                                                                  • Article 39A, added by the 42nd Amendment, provides for the equal justice and free legal aid to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
                                                                                  • Organisation of Village Panchayats (Article 40).
                                                                                  • Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases (Article 41).
                                                                                  • According to the Article 42, the State shall make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief. According to Article 43, the State shall endeavour to secure, for all workers, work and living wage, and to promote the cottage industry.
                                                                                  • Participation of workers in the management of industries (Article 43 A).
                                                                                  • Promotion of cooperative societies (Article 43 B).
                                                                                  • Uniform Civil Code for the citizens (Article 44).
                                                                                  • The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years (Article 45).
                                                                                  • Promotion of educational and economic interests of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes and other weaker sections (Article 46).
                                                                                  • It is the duty of the State to raise the level of the nutrition and the Standard of living and to improve public health (Article 47).
                                                                                  • Organisation of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry (Article 48).
                                                                                  • Article 48A provides for the protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life.
                                                                                  • Article 49 provides for the protection of monuments, and places and objects of national importance.
                                                                                  • Separation of judiciary from executive (Article 50).
                                                                                  • Promotion of international peace and security (Article 51). Difference between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles

                                                                                  i.e. they are legallyi.e. they are not legally

                                                                                  enforceable by the courts enforceable by the courts in case of their violation. for their violation.

                                                                                  2. These are mostly negative These are positive in nature. in nature.

                                                                                  3. These have legalThese have moral and
                                                                                  sanctions.political sanctions.
                                                                                  4. They aim to establishThey aim to establish social
                                                                                  political democracy.and economic democracy.
                                                                                  5. Promotes welfare of thePromotes community
                                                                                  individual.welfare.
                                                                                  6. They are automaticallyThey require legislation for
                                                                                  enforced.their implementation.

                                                                                  • The purpose of the inclusion of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution is to establish:Social and Economic Democracy

                                                                                  Purpose of Directive Principles → establish social and economic democracy, helping India grow as a welfare State.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not the objective of the Directive Principles of State Policy?To establish a Religious State

                                                                                  DPSP (Articles 36 to 51) aim at a welfare, secular, democratic State with socio-economic justice; not a religious State. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) Directive Principles are important for economic, social and political functions in a Modern Democratic State.Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                  Both true, R explains A: DPSP aim at economic and social democracy; Article 38(1) → social order with social, economic, political justice; Article 37 → not court-enforceable.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • How are the Directive Principles of State Policy different from Fundamental Rights?Directive Principles are not enforceable whereas Fundamental Right can be enforced.

                                                                                  DPSP are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced in any court); Fundamental Rights are enforceable.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The ‘Directive Principles’ are………..Non-justifiable

                                                                                  Directive Principles are non-justiciable; Fundamental Rights are justiciable.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Consider the following statements: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principle of State Policy constitute limitations uponNeither 1 nor 2

                                                                                  DPSP are instructions to Legislature and Executive on how to use their powers; they are not limitations on legislative or executive functions and are not court-enforceable.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • With reference to the provisions contained in Part IV of the Constitution of India, which of the following statements is/are correct?2 and 3 only

                                                                                  Article 37: Part IV is not enforceable by any court, but is fundamental in governance; State must apply these principles in making laws.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which Article of the Indian constitution says that Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court?Article 37

                                                                                  Article 37 → Directive Principles (Part IV) are not enforceable by any court.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Consider the following statements with respect to Directive Principles of State Policy:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                  DPSP: not enforceable by courts, yet fundamental in governance; State's duty to apply them in making laws (both statements true).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                  DPSP spell out socio-economic democracy; not enforceable by any court; 'fundamental in the governance of the country'.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy, which one of the following statements is not correct?They impose a legal duty on the State.

                                                                                  DPSP do not impose a legal duty on the State (non-enforceable, moral ideals), but are fundamental in governance and the State must apply them in law-making.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The concept of welfare state is included in the Constitution of India in the:Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Welfare State concept → Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36 to 51). Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The idea of India as Welfare State is found in-Both (a) and (c)

                                                                                  Idea of India as a welfare State → found in both the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The Directive principles of State Policy may be classified in to which of the following parts for the sake of convenient study?All of the above

                                                                                  Constitution does not classify DPSP; by content they fall into three groups: Socialistic, Gandhian, Liberal-intellectual.

                                                                                  Memory aid S-G-L: Socialist, Gandhian, Liberal.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The Directive Principles of State Policy of the Constitution of India is taken from the Constitution of which country?Ireland

                                                                                  Directive Principles of State Policy → borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Ireland). Must know

                                                                                  Memory aid Directives from Dublin: DPSP came from Ireland.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following Directive Principles do not follow Gandhian Principles?2 and 4

                                                                                  Gandhian DPSP: village panchayats, rural cottage industries. Not Gandhian: Uniform Civil Code (liberal-intellectual), right to work (socialist).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Directive Principles of State Policy are-Non-Justiciable

                                                                                  Directive Principles are non-justiciable: not enforceable in any court of law in India. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • According to the Constitution of India, which of the following are fundamental to the governance of the country?Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Article 37 → Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, though not enforceable in courts.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Under the Indian Constitution, concentration ofwealth violatesthe Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Concentration of wealth violates DPSP: Article 39 directs equal right to livelihood for men and women and distribution of community's material resources for common good.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • ‘Equal Pay for Equal Work’ has been ensured in the Indian Constitution as one of the:Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Equal pay for equal work for men and women → Article 39(d), a DPSP, not a Fundamental Right; SC read it with Articles 14, 16 (Randhir Singh, 1982). Must know

                                                                                  Don't confuse Don't call it a Fundamental Right: the text is in DPSP; the Supreme Court only deduced it through Articles 14 and 16.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Panchayati Raj System in India is laid down under-Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Panchayati Raj → DPSP, Article 40: State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following Articles directs the State Governments to organize the Panchayats?Article 40

                                                                                  Article 40 → State organises village panchayats (a DPSP). Article 48 → ban cow slaughter; Article 33 → Parliament modifies Fundamental Rights for forces. Must know

                                                                                  Don't confuse Article 33 is in Part III (Fundamental Rights), not a Directive Principle.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Match List -I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists:None of the above / More than one of the above

                                                                                  Village Panchayat → Article 40; Uniform Civil Code → 44; Agriculture and Animal Husbandry → 48; Separation of Judiciary → 50; International Peace → 51.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer using the code given below:1 2 3 4

                                                                                  Article 40 → village panchayats; 41 → right to work, education, public assistance; 44 → Uniform Civil Code; 48 → agriculture and animal husbandry. Must know

                                                                                  Memory aid Gaon (40) → Kaam (41) → Kanoon (44) → Kheti (48).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?Article 48 - Separation of Judiciary from Executive

                                                                                  Wrong pair: Article 48 → organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, not separation of judiciary. Correct: 39A free legal aid; 40 village panchayats; 44 Uniform Civil Code.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Identify the correct pair mentioning the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India-That there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women – Article 39

                                                                                  Article 39(d) → equal pay for equal work for men and women. Others: free legal aid 39A; agriculture and animal husbandry 48; village panchayat 40.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Match the following List - P (Directive Principles) with List - R (Articles):II I III IV

                                                                                  Equal justice and free legal aid → Article 39A; Protection of environment → 48A; Right to Work → 41; Protection of monuments → 49.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?The promotion of Co-operative -Article 43A Societies

                                                                                  Wrong pair: co-operative societies → Article 43B, not 43A; Article 43A → workers' participation in management. Article 50 separation of judiciary; 46 SC/ST interests; 40 panchayats.

                                                                                  Memory aid A before B: 43A workers, 43B co-operatives.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):(A) is true, but (R) is false.

                                                                                  MGNREGA → at least 100 days' employment a year to a rural household (A true); right to work is a DPSP, not in Part III (R false).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • MANREGA scheme has been launched as a part of implementing which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?Article 43

                                                                                  MGNREGA implements Article 43 (DPSP): State to secure a living wage, decent working conditions and leisure for all workers.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following Article was inserted by the 42nd Constitution Amendment to provide for participation of workers in management?Article 43A

                                                                                  Article 43A (workers' participation in management of industries) → inserted by the 42nd Amendment. Uniform Civil Code → Article 44. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                  • In India, separation of judiciary from the executive is enjoined by:a Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  Separation of judiciary from executive → Article 50, a Directive Principle (Part IV).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following Articles of the Directive Principles of State Policy deals with the promotion of international peace and security?51

                                                                                  Article 51 → promotion of international peace and security. 41 → right to work, education, public assistance; 43A → workers in management; 48A → environment, forests, wildlife.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • In the Constitution of India, Promotion of International Peace and Security is included in the –Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                  International peace and security → DPSP, Article 51 (linked to foreign policy): just and honourable relations, respect for international law, settle disputes by arbitration. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following was not added to the Directive Principles by the 42nd Amendment of the Constitution?Uniform civil code

                                                                                  Added by 42nd Amendment: 39(f) protection of children and youth, 39A free legal aid, 43A workers' participation. Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) was not added by it. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The Constitution grants right against exploitation to –1, 2 and 3 only

                                                                                  Constitution grants the right against exploitation to children, women and tribals; the word 'Dalit' is not in the Constitution.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not a Directive Principle of State Policy?Free Education to children up to the age of fourteen (14)

                                                                                  Free education for children up to 14 (old Article 45) is no longer a DPSP (changed 2002). DPSPs: prohibition of intoxicating drinks (47), cow protection (48), environment (48A). Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following is/are included in the Directive Principles of State Policy?2 only

                                                                                  Prohibition of intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs (except medicinal) → DPSP, Article 47; ban on trafficking and forced labour → Fundamental Right, Article 23(1).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Consider the following provisions under the Directive Principles of State Policy as enshrined in the Constitution of India –2 and 3

                                                                                  Gandhian DPSPs: village panchayats (Article 40), rural cottage industries, nutrition and public health (47), cow protection (48). Uniform Civil Code and workers' leisure are not Gandhian.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • In which of the following 'the provisions for the protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife' are found in the Constitution of India?Both (a) and (b)

                                                                                  Environment, forests and wildlife → both DPSP (Article 48A) and Fundamental Duty (Article 51A(g)).

                                                                                  Memory aid State protects (48A), citizen protects (51A g); g for green.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following Provision is a part of both Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties?Protection of environment

                                                                                  Protection of environment → part of both DPSP (Article 48A, State's duty) and Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A(g), citizen's duty).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is a Directive Principle of State Policy?The State shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment.

                                                                                  'State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment' → DPSP, Article 48A. Equality before law and non-discrimination are Fundamental Rights.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • The Constitution is silent in the Directive Principles of State Policy about –Adult education

                                                                                  DPSP are silent on adult education. Included: living wage (Article 43), free legal aid (39A), early childhood care and education below six (45).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy was added to the Constitution at a later date?Free Legal Aid

                                                                                  Free legal aid (Article 39A) → added later by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976; panchayats, cow slaughter ban and Uniform Civil Code were not later additions.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • In Which year it was inserted in the Constitution of India that the State shall secure free legal aid to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities?1976

                                                                                  Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid) → inserted by 42nd Amendment Act 1976 (in force 3 January 1977).

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • With reference to National Legal Services Authority, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                  NALSA (Legal Services Authorities Act 1987): free, competent legal services to weaker sections on equal opportunity; organises Lok Adalats; guides State legal services authorities.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • In India, Legal Services Authorities provide free legal services to which of the following type of citizens?1 and 2 only

                                                                                  Free legal aid (Section 12, Legal Services Authorities Act): SC/ST, trafficking victims, women, children, disabled, industrial workmen, low-income persons; not all OBCs or all senior citizens.

                                                                                  Don't confuse Senior citizens get free aid only within State income ceilings (Delhi: 2 lakh), not automatically.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following is not included in the Directive Principles of State Policy?Right to Information

                                                                                  Right to Information is a legal right (RTI Act 2005), not a DPSP. DPSPs: equal pay (39(d)), adequate livelihood (39(a)), prohibition of liquor, right to work. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which one of the following is a Directive Principle of the State Policy?Uniform Civil Code

                                                                                  Uniform Civil Code → DPSP, Article 44 (State shall endeavour to secure it throughout India). Press freedom, religious freedom, equality before law are Fundamental Rights. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Identify the items included in the Directive Principles of State Policy.Only 1

                                                                                  Only prohibition of liquor is a DPSP (Article 47). Bans on child labour in factories, begar or forced labour, and untouchability are Fundamental Rights. Must know

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                  • “The Directive Principles of State Policy is a cheque which is paid on Bank’s Convenience," Who said it?K.T. Shah

                                                                                  K.T. Shah: Directive Principles are 'a cheque payable at the bank's convenience'.

                                                                                  Memory aid Shah sounds like 'Sahukar' (moneylender): the cheque remark is his.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following.Only 3

                                                                                  National Social Assistance Programme (15 August 1995) → fulfils DPSP on right to work, education, public assistance; includes old age pension, family benefit, maternity benefit schemes.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                  • Which of the following is/are listed among the Directive Principles in Part-IV of the Constitution of India? I. Equal Pay for Equal Work II. Uniform Civil Code III. Small family norm IV. Education through mother tongue at primary level.I and II

                                                                                  In Part IV: equal pay for equal work (39(d)), Uniform Civil Code (44). Not DPSP: small family norm; mother-tongue primary education → Article 350A.

                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        25 facts · 41 questions · 8 Must know

                                                                                        Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                        Fundamental Duties: key facts from the book
                                                                                        • The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
                                                                                        • These were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
                                                                                        • This amendment added a new part (Part IV A) which consists of only one article, that is, Article 51 A.
                                                                                        • Presently, the number of Fundamental Duties, as per the Article 51 A, is 11, whereas originally, at the time of its inclusion in the Constitution, the number was 10. The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
                                                                                        • According to Article 51 A, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India –

                                                                                        (a) To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;

                                                                                        (b) To cherish and follow the noble ideas which inspired our national struggle for freedom;

                                                                                        (c) To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India;

                                                                                        (d) To defend the Country and render national service when called upon to do so;

                                                                                        (e) To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women;

                                                                                        (f) To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;

                                                                                        (g) To protect and improve the natural environment- including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures;

                                                                                        (h) To develop the scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry and reform;

                                                                                        (i) To safeguard public property and to abjure violence; (j) To Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective Activity.

                                                                                        (k) Who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years (added by 86 Amendment Act, 2002).

                                                                                        • Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen?Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                        Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A, Part IV-A; 42nd Amendment 1976, Swaran Singh Committee) are non-justiciable: no legal process to enforce them; not correlative to legal duties.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • The provisions relating to Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India were added on the recommendation of:Swaran Singh Committee

                                                                                        Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A, Article 51A, added by 42nd Amendment 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation; originally 10, now 11. Must know

                                                                                        Memory aid Swaran = gold: Swaran Singh gave the golden duties.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Constitution on the recommendation of -Swaran Singh Committee

                                                                                        Swaran Singh Committee recommended (1976) Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment Act 1976 inserted Article 51A (Part IV-A), in force 3 January 1977; 11th duty (k) added later. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                        • The Fundamental Duty to uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India is mentioned at number –three

                                                                                        Article 51A(c), the third duty → uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. Duties came via the 42nd Amendment.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Under which Articles of Indian Constitution, provision for Fundamental Duties has been made by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act?Article 51A

                                                                                        42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 51A in new Part IV-A → Fundamental Duties of citizens. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which of the following were members of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976)?(A), (B) and (D)

                                                                                        Swaran Singh Committee (1976): 12 members incl. A.R. Antulay, S.S. Ray, C.M. Stephen; Haridev Joshi (Rajasthan CM) was not a member. 42nd Amendment added ten duties. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 11 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which of the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties is not true:They can be enforced by writs

                                                                                        Fundamental Duties cannot be enforced by writs; they are moral obligations (patriotism, unity of India), promoted by constitutional methods and usable to interpret ambiguous statutes. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Under the Constitution of India which of the following is not Fundamental Duty?To vote in General Election

                                                                                        Voting in elections is not a Fundamental Duty; Article 51A has 11 duties incl. scientific temper, safeguarding public property, abiding by the Constitution. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                        • The word 'To Abide and Respect' under the Provisions of Article 51A of Constitution of India is concerned to-Constitution

                                                                                        Article 51A(a) → abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is a Fundamental Duty in India?To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture

                                                                                        Value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture → Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(f); separation of judiciary, free education, abolition of untouchability are not duties.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • The Fundamental Duties of a citizen do not include duty –To strive towards abolition of untouchability

                                                                                        Striving to abolish untouchability is not a Fundamental Duty; untouchability is dealt with by Article 17, a Fundamental Right (Part III).

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is not a part of Fundamental Duties under Indian Constitution?To help in organizing Village Panchayats.

                                                                                        Organising village panchayats is a DPSP (Article 40), not a Fundamental Duty. Duties: defend country and render national service (51-A(d)), composite culture, public property, abjure violence. Must know

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which of the following is/are among the Fundamental Duties of citizens laid down in the Indian Constitution?1, 3 and 4

                                                                                        Fundamental Duties include preserving composite culture, scientific temper and inquiry, striving towards excellence; 'protect weaker sections from social injustice' is not a duty.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Protection of which one of the following is a Fundamental Duty of an Indian citizen?Wild Life

                                                                                        Article 51A(g) → protect and improve natural environment incl. forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife; compassion for living creatures. 51A(a) → respect the National Flag.

                                                                                        Don't confuse The duty is to respect the National Flag, not 'protect' it; protection of wildlife is the duty asked.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • “It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment”?. The above statement refers to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?Article 51-A

                                                                                        Citizen's duty to protect and improve the natural environment → Article 51A(g), Part IV-A. (Article 48-A is the State's DPSP on environment.)

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is incorrect?Fundamental Duties are the part of the Fundamental Rights.

                                                                                        Fundamental Duties are not part of Fundamental Rights; they form Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by 42nd Amendment 1976; now 11 duties.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is not a Fundamental Duty?To protect monuments and places of public importance

                                                                                        Protecting monuments and places of public importance is not in Article 51A; duties include respecting the National Anthem, safeguarding public property, protecting environment.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which of the following is not a fundamental duty?To protect monuments and places of national importance

                                                                                        Protecting monuments and places of national importance → DPSP, Article 49, not a Fundamental Duty.

                                                                                        Don't confuse 'safeguard public property' (duty) with 'protect monuments' (DPSP, Article 49).

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is NOT provided in part IV A (Fundamental Duties) of the Indian Constitution?To respect our parents and teachers

                                                                                        Respecting parents and teachers is not among the eleven Fundamental Duties; respecting the National Flag, brotherhood and composite culture are.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Under the Constitution of India, which one of the following is not a Fundamental Duty?To vote in public elections

                                                                                        Voting in public elections is not a Fundamental Duty. Scientific temper → 51A(h); safeguard public property → 51A(i); abide by Constitution → 51A(a).

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Which one of the following is not correctly matched?Part V - Fundamental Duties

                                                                                        Wrong pair: Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A (42nd Amendment), not Part V; Part V = Union Executive. Part II Citizenship, III Fundamental Rights, IV DPSP.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Consider the following pairs:All the three

                                                                                        All three correct: separation of judiciary → DPSP (Article 50); preserving composite culture → Fundamental Duty (51A(f)); child employment ban → Fundamental Right (Article 24).

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • “To uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India” is a provision made in the –Fundamental Duties

                                                                                        Uphold and protect sovereignty, unity and integrity of India → Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(c). Duties added by 42nd and 86th Amendments; now 11.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                        • How many Fundamental Duties are there in the Indian Constitution?Eleven

                                                                                        Eleven Fundamental Duties; originally 10; 11th (51A(k): parents/guardians give education opportunity to children aged 6 to 14) added by 86th Amendment Act 2002. Must know

                                                                                        Memory aid 86th gave the 11th: the education duty.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                        • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists:2 4 1 3

                                                                                        Respect for international law → Article 51(c) (DPSP); compassion for living creatures → 51A(g); spirit of inquiry and reform → 51A(h); separate judiciary → Article 50.

                                                                                        Don't confuse Article 51 (DPSP) and Article 51A (Duties) differ by one letter; don't mix them.

                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
