                                                                                              30 facts · 49 questions · 6 Must know

                                                                                              Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                              The President: key facts from the book
                                                                                              • The President of India is the head of the Indian State, the first citizen, and acts as the symbol of unity, integrity and solidarity of the nation.
                                                                                              • According to Article 52, ‘There shall be a President of India’.
                                                                                              • According to Article 53, the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with this Constitution.
                                                                                              • According to Article 54, the President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the States.
                                                                                              • 70th Amendment Act, 1992 (effective from 01- 06-1995) provided for the inclusion of the elected members of legislative assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union territory of Puducherry in the electoral college for the election of the President.
                                                                                              • Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not participate in the election of the President.
                                                                                              • According to Article 55(3), the election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is done by secret ballot.
                                                                                              • All doubts and disputes in connection with the election of the President are enquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final.
                                                                                              • The Election of the President cannot be challenged on the grounds that the electoral college was incomplete. (due to any vacancy of members)
                                                                                              • Article 58 describes the eligibility criteria (a citizen of India, has completed the age of 35 years and is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People, and is not ineligible due to holding any office of profit under Article 58(2)) for election as President.
                                                                                              • Further, the nomination of a candidate for election to the office of President must be subscribed by at least 50 electors as proposers and 50 electors as seconders.
                                                                                              • Every candidate has to make a security deposit of Rs. 15000. The security deposit is liable to be forfeited in case the candidates are not elected and the number of valid votes polled by such candidates does not exceed one-sixth of the number of votes necessary to secure the return of a candidate at such election.
                                                                                              • The President's term of office is five years from the date on which he enters his office (Article 56).
                                                                                              • According to Article 56 (1)(a), the President submits his resignation in writing under his hand addressed to the Vice- President of India. The Vice-President shall immediately inform, about the resignation, to the speaker of the Lok Sabha (Under Article 56(2)).
                                                                                              • Further under Article 56(1)
                                                                                              • (b) he can also be removed from the office by the process of Impeachment (mentioned under Article 61)
                                                                                              • The Article 57 defines the eligibility of re-election, to the post of the President, for a person. The only ground for impeachment specified in the Art. 61(1) is the violation of the Constitution.
                                                                                              • No President has so far been impeached.
                                                                                              • When a vacancy occurs in the office of the President due to his resignation, removal, death or otherwise, the Vice–President acts as the President until a new President is elected.
                                                                                              • Further, when the sitting President is unable to discharge his functions due to absence, illness or any other cause, the Vice–President discharges his functions until the President resumes his office.
                                                                                              • In case the office of the Vice–President is vacant, the Chief Justice of India (or if his office is also vacant, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available) acts as the President or discharges the functions of the President.
                                                                                              • According to Article 59(1), if any person who is a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the State legislature is elected as President, he is deemed to have vacated his seat in that house on the date on which he enters upon his office as President.
                                                                                              • The oath of office to the President is administered by the Chief Justice of India (Art. 60).
                                                                                              • Currently, the salary of the President is 5 Lakh per month. It is paid from the Consolidated Fund of India.
                                                                                              • According to Article 77, the conduct of businesses of the Government of India is formally done in the President's name.
                                                                                              • He can summon a joint sitting of both the houses of Parliament (Art.108).
                                                                                              • When a bill is sent to the President after it has been passed by the Parliament, he can give his assent to the bill or withhold his assent to the bill, or return the bill (if it is not a money bill) for reconsideration by the Parliament. However, if the bill is passed again by the Parliament, with or without amendments, the President has to give his assent to the bill.
                                                                                              • A bill becomes an Act after the assent of the President.
                                                                                              • The President cannot return a money bill for reconsideration.
                                                                                              • Money bill is introduced in the Parliament, that too in Lok Sabha only with his prior recommendation.
                                                                                              • He can promulgate ordinances when the Parliament is not in Session (Art.123).
                                                                                              • These ordinances must be approved by the Parliament within six weeks from its reassembly.
                                                                                              • He can also withdraw an ordinance at any time.
                                                                                              • Article 72 of the Constitution empowers the President to grant pardons to persons and to suspend, remit, respite, reprieve or commute sentences in certain cases.
                                                                                              • He has the power to consult the Supreme Court (Art. 143).
                                                                                              • He can declare any area as a scheduled area and has powers with respect to the administration of scheduled areas and tribal areas. He is the supreme commander of defence forces (Army, Navy and Air-force) of India.
                                                                                              • The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 made a provision that made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
                                                                                              • The 44thAmendmentAct, 1978 (enacted by the Janta Party Government) authorized the President to require the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice either generally or otherwise. However, he shall act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.
                                                                                              • Who amongst the following is the head of Indian Republic?President of India

                                                                                              Head of the Indian Republic (Head of State) → President of India; first President Dr. Rajendra Prasad (26 Jan 1950 to 13 May 1962). Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Consider the following statements(A) is true but (R) is false.

                                                                                              A true, R false: India's President is indirectly elected, unlike the hereditary British King; but not similar to the US President, who has more power.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Given below are two statements:(A) is true, but (R) is false.

                                                                                              Article 53 → Union executive power vested in the President (A true); R false: he acts directly or through subordinate officers as per the Constitution, so his power is limited.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • President of India exercises his powerseither directly or through officers subordinate to him

                                                                                              Article 53(1) → President exercises Union executive power directly or through officers subordinate to him, per the Constitution. Article 52 → there shall be a President.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Who is the Executive Head of State in India?President

                                                                                              Executive Head of State → President; Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President. Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                              Both true, R explains A: Article 53 vests Union executive power in the President, who is the constitutional head of the State.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Given below are two statements:Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                              Both true, R does not explain A: Article 53 vests executive power in the President; Article 77 → all executive action of Government of India taken in the President's name.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Given below are two statements:(A) is true, but (R) is false.

                                                                                              Article 53(2) → supreme command of the Defence Forces vested in the President, but its exercise is regulated by law (not free of legislative control). Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                              • “He represents the nation but does not lead the nation”—this dictum applies to whom of the following?President

                                                                                              'Represents the nation but does not lead it' → President (Head of State); the Prime Minister holds real executive power and leads the nation.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • How is the President elected in India?By Indirect Election

                                                                                              President elected indirectly (Article 54) by an electoral college, through proportional representation by single transferable vote, by secret ballot. Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 12 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Which one of the following is not correct regarding Presidential election?President’selection may be postponed on the ground that the electoral college is incomplete.

                                                                                              Presidential election cannot be postponed because the electoral college is incomplete (e.g. a dissolved Assembly). Term five years; incumbent continues till successor enters office.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Minimum number of electors needed to be proposer of the presidential candidate is -—

                                                                                              Presidential nomination needs at least 50 electors as proposers and another 50 as seconders.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Consider the following statements: In the electoral college for Presidential Election in India,Only 2

                                                                                              MLA vote value = State population ÷ elected MLAs ÷ one thousand (not ×100); MP vote value = total value of all MLAs' votes ÷ total elected MPs (Article 55).

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                              MLA vote value varies by State (Arunachal Pradesh 8, Uttar Pradesh 208); every MP of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha has the same vote value.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the election of the President of India?Every elected member of the Legislative Assembly of a State shall have as many votes as there are multiples of one hundred in the quotient obtained by dividing the population of the State by the total number of the elected members of the Assembly.

                                                                                              Incorrect: MLA votes = multiples of one thousand, not one hundred. Correct: 1971 census basis till first census after 2026 (84th Amendment 2001); PR by single transferable vote.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • In the Presidential Election, 2022, the vote value of each member of Rajasthan Legislative Assembly was:129

                                                                                              2022 Presidential election: Rajasthan MLA vote value = 129 (1971 population 2,57,65,800 ÷ 200 MLAs ÷ 1000 = 128.82). Droupadi Murmu became 15th President.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India:Only one

                                                                                              Only one correct: nominated members excluded from electoral college; more Assembly seats → lower MLA vote value; values: Madhya Pradesh 131, Kerala 152, Arunachal 8, Puducherry 16.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • The Chief Minister of a State in India is not eligible to vote in the Presidential election if-He is a member of the Upper House of the State Legislature.

                                                                                              A Chief Minister who is a member of the State Legislative Council (Upper House) cannot vote for President; electoral college = elected MPs and elected MLAs of States, Delhi, Puducherry.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • In the Presidential election in India, every elected member of the Legislative Assembly of a State shall have as many votes as there are multiples of one thousand in the quotient obtained by dividing the population of the State by the total number of the elected members of the Assembly. As at present (1997), the expression “population” here means the population as ascertained by the1971 Census

                                                                                              'Population' for Presidential vote value = 1971 Census, until figures of the first census after 2026 are published (Article 81(3) proviso).

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Which of the following is not an essential qualification for the candidature of President?Educated

                                                                                              President eligibility (Article 58(1)): citizen of India, age 35 completed, qualified for election to Lok Sabha; no educational qualification.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Consider the following statements about the President of India-Only 2

                                                                                              President needs (Article 58(1)): citizenship (not necessarily by birth), age 35, and qualification for election to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

                                                                                              Don't confuse Qualification is for the House of the People (Lok Sabha), not just 'Parliament'; citizenship need not be by birth.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • A Member of Parliament or a State Legislature can be elected as President butHe will have to relinquish his seat as soon as he is elected

                                                                                              Article 59(1): an MP or MLA elected President is deemed to vacate the seat on the date he enters upon office as President.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • The Indian President is eligible for re-election for how many times?Any number of times

                                                                                              Article 57 → President is eligible for re-election any number of times.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Which article of the Indian Constitution prescribes eligibility conditions for re-election to the post of the President of India?Article 57

                                                                                              Eligibility for re-election of the President → Article 57.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • If there is any dispute regarding the Presidential election, it can be referred to –Supreme Court of India

                                                                                              Disputes about Presidential election → decided by the Supreme Court (Article 71); its decision is final.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • Consider the following statements:None

                                                                                              All three false: acts of a President whose election is voided by SC remain valid (Article 71(2)); election not postponed for Electoral College vacancies; no time limit for assent.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • The President holds office for a term of 5 years from date on –Which he enters upon his office/hold his office

                                                                                              Article 56(1) → President's term is 5 years from the date he enters upon his office.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                              • To whom does the President of India address his resignation?Vice-President of India

                                                                                              President addresses resignation to the Vice-President (Article 56(1)(a)), who at once informs the Lok Sabha Speaker (Article 56(2)).

                                                                                              Memory aid Resignation relay: President → Vice-President → Speaker.

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                              • The President of India can be removed from his post by –Parliament

                                                                                              President removed by Parliament through impeachment for violation of the Constitution (Article 56(1)(b), procedure Article 61); either House can start it. Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                              • What is not true in relation to election of President?None of the above

                                                                                              All true: PR by single transferable vote, secret ballot (Article 55); nomination needs 50 proposers and 50 seconders; MLA vote value on 1971 census. Impeachment → Article 61. Must know

                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                    The President · part 2 of 3

                                                                                                    26 facts · 40 questions · 8 Must know

                                                                                                    Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                    • Which among the following Article speaks about impeachment of the President of India?Article 61

                                                                                                    Impeachment of President → Article 61: charge preferred by either House; the other House investigates; President may appear and be represented.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which Article of the Indian constitution provides the Provisions related to the impeachment of the President?Article 61

                                                                                                    Article 61 → impeachment of President for 'violation of the Constitution' (not defined); quasi-judicial procedure in Parliament; either House can initiate. Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • At least how many days of prior notice is required for the impeachment of the President of India?14 days

                                                                                                    Impeachment needs at least 14 days' written notice signed by at least one-fourth of total members of the House (Article 61(2)(a)).

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is a part of the electoral college of the President but not of the process of impeachment?State Legislative Assemblies

                                                                                                    State Legislative Assemblies elect the President but take no part in impeachment (only Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha do); Legislative Councils take part in neither.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is electoral college for the President but not forum for his impeachment?State Legislative Assemblies

                                                                                                    Impeachment of President is a quasi-judicial process in Parliament only (Article 61); State Legislative Assemblies are in the electoral college (Article 54(b)) but not in impeachment.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • The vacant post of the President is to be filled within –Six months

                                                                                                    Vacancy in President's office (death, resignation, removal) must be filled within six months (Article 62(2)). Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • For how long can the Vice-President act as President when the President cannot perform his duties for reasons of death resignation, removal or otherwise?6 months

                                                                                                    Vice-President can act as President for at most 6 months, since a President's vacancy must be filled within 6 months.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • In case the post of the President of India falls vacant due to his death, resignation or removal from office, who will occupy that post?Vice-President

                                                                                                    Vacancy by death, resignation or removal → Vice-President acts as President until the new President enters office (Article 65(1)).

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • In case the post of President of India falls vacant, and there is no Vice-President also, who among the following would be the acting President?Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

                                                                                                    Both President and Vice-President offices vacant → Chief Justice of India acts as President; if absent, senior-most SC judge (President (Discharge of Functions) Act 1969). Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Assertion (A): During the term of office no litigation can be instituted in any court of law against the President of India.—

                                                                                                    Article 361(2): no criminal proceedings against President or Governor during term; Article 361(4): civil proceedings allowed after two months' written notice. President is not above the Constitution.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • The President can dissolve Lok Sabha on –Recommendation of the Union Cabinet

                                                                                                    President dissolves Lok Sabha (Article 85(2)(b)) on the advice of the Union Cabinet / Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Article 74(1)).

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:2 and 3

                                                                                                    Prorogation needs Council of Ministers' advice (statement 1 false); a House can be prorogued even in session; President dissolves Lok Sabha (Article 85(2)(b)), usually on Ministers' advice.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • The joint sitting of the House of People and the Council of States is summoned by –The President

                                                                                                    Joint sitting of both Houses → summoned by the President (Article 108); presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker (Article 118(4)). Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which of the following expression is appropriate regarding the message to call joint sitting of both houses under Article 108 of the Constitution of India?Intention of President

                                                                                                    Article 108: President notifies his 'intention' to summon a joint sitting when a Bill is rejected, amendments are disagreed, or six months pass without passing.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which one of the following statements about the President of India is not correct?He participates in the discussions in the both Houses.

                                                                                                    President is a constituent part of Parliament (Article 79), addresses a joint meeting every year, issues ordinances (Article 123); he does not take part in House discussions.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Given below are two statements:Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                    Both true, R explains A: Parliament = President + both Houses (Article 79); a Bill becomes law only with the President's assent (Article 111). Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • A Bill presented in Parliament becomes an Act after –The President has given his Assent.

                                                                                                    A Bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act only after the President's assent (Article 111).

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • The only instance when the President of India exercised his power of veto, is related to-The Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill

                                                                                                    Absolute veto (on Ministers' advice): Rajendra Prasad, PEPSU Appropriation Bill 1954. Pocket veto (at discretion): Gyani Zail Singh, Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill 1986.

                                                                                                    Don't confuse The PEPSU Bill also saw a veto, but on Ministers' advice; the Post Office Bill pocket veto is the discretionary one the key wants.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Who among the following Presidents exercised a power which is ‘Pocket veto’ in Constitutional terminology?Gyani Zail Singh

                                                                                                    Pocket veto (taking no action on a Bill) used only once: President Gyani Zail Singh, 1986, Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill.

                                                                                                    Memory aid Zail Singh kept the 'Post' in his pocket.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution, the President of India enjoys the power to withhold his assent to any Bill passed by both the Houses of the Parliament?Article 111

                                                                                                    Article 111 → President declares assent to, or withholds assent from, a Bill passed by both Houses. Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which of the following are the discretionary powers of the President?(ii) (iii) (vi)

                                                                                                    Discretionary: return a Bill with objections, withhold a Bill, send messages to Parliament (Article 86(2)). Appointing Ministers and judges = executive; summoning joint session = legislative power.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • On which matter, it is not essential for the President to take advice from the Council of Ministers?To assent to Bills

                                                                                                    Per book, giving assent to Bills (Article 111) does not need Council of Ministers' advice; dissolving Lok Sabha, appointing ambassadors and other options do.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which of this is the legislative power of the President according to constitution?To promulgate ordinance

                                                                                                    Promulgating ordinances (when Parliament is not in session) is the President's legislative power; Parliament must approve within six weeks of reassembly; President can withdraw it anytime.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which of the following is the discretionary powers of President?iii vi vii viii

                                                                                                    President's discretion: return a Bill with objections, detain a Bill, seek information from the PM, ask Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice.

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President give his assent to the Ordinance on electoral reforms when it was sent back to him by the Union Cabinet without making any changes (in the year 2002)?Article 123

                                                                                                    2002 electoral reforms ordinance: President assented under Article 123 (ordinance power during Parliament's recess) after the Cabinet sent it back unchanged; ordinance has force of an Act. Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                    • Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the issuance of Ordinance by the President?President can never repeal it.

                                                                                                    Article 123 ordinances: same force as an Act of Parliament; must be approved within six weeks of reassembly; President can withdraw them any time ('can never repeal' is false). Must know

                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                          The President · part 3 of 3

                                                                                                          39 facts · 42 questions · 6 Must know

                                                                                                          Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                          • An ordinance promulgated by the President must be placed before the Parliament within what time frame after the start of its session?6 weeks

                                                                                                          President's ordinance must be laid before both Houses and ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles (Article 123(2)).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: I. An Ordinance can amend any Central Act. II. An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right. III. An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date. Which of the statements given above are correct?I and II only

                                                                                                          An ordinance can amend any Central Act (not the Constitution) and can be retrospective; it cannot abridge Fundamental Rights any more than an Act can.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which among the following is/are appointed by the President of India?1 and 3 are correct

                                                                                                          President appoints Finance Commission Chairman (Article 280(1)) and UT Chief Ministers (Article 239AA(5)); Planning Commission Vice-Chairman was appointed by the PM (now NITI Aayog). Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who among the following is appointed by the President:All of the above

                                                                                                          President appoints the Attorney General (Article 76), CAG (Article 148) and State Governors (Article 155).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is not appointed by the President of India:Vice- President

                                                                                                          Vice-President is elected (Article 66), not appointed by the President; PM, Governor and CEC are appointed by the President.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The Constitution authorizes the President to make provisions for discharge of duties of Governors in extraordinary circumstances underArticle 160

                                                                                                          Article 160 → President may provide for discharge of a Governor's duties in any contingency.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Indian Constitution doesn’t empower the President of India with the right ofAppointment of Chief Minister in states

                                                                                                          A State's Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor (Article 164(1)), not by the President.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to consult the Supreme Court?Article 143

                                                                                                          Article 143 → President may consult the Supreme Court on a question of law or fact; its advice is not binding on him. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • According to the Constitution, which among the following is literally not a ‘Power’ of the President of India?To send messages to Houses of Parliament

                                                                                                          Sending messages to Houses of Parliament (Article 86(2)) is a right of the President, not a 'power'; ordinances, consulting SC, pardon are powers.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The President of India does not have the right to –Remove a judge of Supreme Court

                                                                                                          President cannot remove a Supreme Court judge on his own: removal needs an address by each House with the required majority, then the President's order (Article 124(4)).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Power of the President to grant pardons etc. is a :-Judicial Power

                                                                                                          Pardoning power (Article 72: pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, suspend, remit, commute sentence) is a judicial power of the President.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following doesn't consists in the power 'To Pardon' of President?vi vii

                                                                                                          Article 72 pardoning power: pardon, commutation, remission, respite, reprieve (also court-martial sentences); 'detention' and 'continuation' are not part of it.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • From which Article does the President of India derive his/her pardoning power?Article 72

                                                                                                          Article 72 → President pardons for offences against Union law, court-martial sentences and all death sentences.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India: I. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review. II. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?I only

                                                                                                          Pardoning power (Article 72) is open to limited judicial review; the President cannot use it without aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following types of authority are attributed to the President of the India?2 and 4

                                                                                                          President has titular (formal), de jure, constitutional and nominal authority, not real, popular or political authority.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • According to the Constitution of India, it is the duty of the President of India to cause to be laid before the Parliament which of the following?1, 3 and 4

                                                                                                          President lays before Parliament: Finance Commission recommendations (Article 281), CAG report (151(1)), National Commission for SCs report (338(6)); not PAC report (a parliamentary committee).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is not Constitutional Prerogative of the President of India?Returning a financial bill for reconsideration

                                                                                                          President cannot return a Finance Bill for reconsideration (it needs his recommendation; not introduced in Rajya Sabha). Returning ordinary Bills, dissolving Lok Sabha, appointing PM are prerogatives.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who has the Constitutional Power to declare a geographical area as a ‘’Scheduled Area’’?President

                                                                                                          President declares an area a 'Scheduled Area' (Fifth Schedule); he can also end or enlarge it after consulting the Governor.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who prepares the President’s address to Parliament?Central Cabinet

                                                                                                          President's address to Parliament is prepared by the Union (Central) Cabinet, which holds real executive power.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The first President of India Rajendra Prasad belonged to which State?Bihar

                                                                                                          First President Dr. Rajendra Prasad → from Bihar; born 3 December 1884 in a village of Siwan district.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The First President of Independent India hailed from-Bihar

                                                                                                          First President of independent India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, hailed from Bihar.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which President of India completed two successive terms?Dr. Rajendra Prasad

                                                                                                          Dr. Rajendra Prasad → only one among options to complete successive terms: 1950-1952, 1952-1957, 1957-1962.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The fourth President of India was:Sri V.V. Giri

                                                                                                          V.V. Giri → 4th President as an individual (1969-1974); 6th by tenure order (after Rajendra Prasad's three terms, Radhakrishnan, Zakir Hussain).

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Individual order and tenure order differ: Giri is the 4th person but 6th tenure.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who of the following was elected President of India unanimously?N. Sanjiva Reddy

                                                                                                          Neelam Sanjiva Reddy → the only President elected unanimously (unopposed); tenure 1977 to 1982. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the list:2 3 4 1

                                                                                                          Zakir Husain 1967-1969; V.V. Giri 1969-1974; Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed 1974-1977; Neelam Sanjiva Reddy 1977-1982.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the tenure of the following Presidents of India and arrange them in correct chronological order starting from earliest to the last.1, 4, 2, 3

                                                                                                          Order: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1977-1982) → R. Venkataraman (1987-1992) → K.R. Narayanan (1997-2002) → A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (2002-2007).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who of the following before becoming the President of India did not hold the office of Vice-President?Neelam Sanjiva Reddy

                                                                                                          Neelam Sanjiva Reddy did not serve as Vice-President before becoming President; Radhakrishnan, Zakir Hussain and R. Venkataraman did. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following Indian President also served as Speaker of Lok Sabha?Neelam Sanjiva Reddy

                                                                                                          Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (sixth President) was twice Lok Sabha Speaker: 17 March 1967 to 19 July 1969, and 26 March to 13 July 1977.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Among the following who has been Speaker of Lok Sabha prior to his Election as President of India?Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy

                                                                                                          Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was Lok Sabha Speaker twice before becoming President (elected unopposed, 1977 to 1982).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Among the following Presidents of India, who is known as the Philosopher King or the Philosopher Ruler?Dr. Radhakrishnan

                                                                                                          Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, second President (1962-1967) → called the 'Philosopher King' or 'Philosopher Ruler'.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who among the following Presidents of India was associated with Trade Union Movement?V. V. Giri

                                                                                                          V.V. Giri (fourth President, 1969-1974) → linked to the trade union movement; twice chairman of the All India Trade Union Congress.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which President of India was called the ‘Missile Man’?Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam

                                                                                                          'Missile Man' → Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (11th President, 2002-2007), for work on ballistic missile and satellite launch vehicle technology.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who among the following Chief Justices of India also acted as the President of India?Justice M. Hidayatullah

                                                                                                          Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah served as acting President from 20 July 1969 to 24 August 1969. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Choose the odd one-Jawaharlal Nehru

                                                                                                          Odd one: Jawaharlal Nehru was Prime Minister; Rajendra Prasad, Radhakrishnan and Zakir Husain were Presidents.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • What is the sequence number of Ms. Pratibha Patil as the President of the Republic of India?12t

                                                                                                          Pratibha Patil → 12th President (25 July 2007 to 25 July 2012), first woman President; 14th by tenure order. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who was the candidate of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) in 15th Presidential Election in India?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                          UPA candidate in the 15th Presidential election → Meira Kumar (not in options). In the 16th: NDA's Droupadi Murmu vs opposition-backed Yashwant Sinha.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following President of India has been the Governor of Bihar?Dr. Zakir Hussain

                                                                                                          Dr. Zakir Husain: Governor of Bihar (1957-1962), Vice-President (1962-1967), President (13 May 1967 to 3 May 1969, died in office).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following President was appeared before Supreme Court, when Supreme Court was hearing election dispute of the President?V.V. Giri

                                                                                                          V.V. Giri appeared in person before the Supreme Court (bench under Justice S.M. Sikri) in his election dispute; petition dismissed; he won on second preference votes.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Rashtrapati Bhavan was designed by:Edwin Lutyens

                                                                                                          Rashtrapati Bhavan designed by Edwin Lutyens; Viceroy House till 1947, then Government House; C. Rajagopalachari first Indian resident (21 June 1948).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                The Vice-President

                                                                                                                18 facts · 23 questions · 2 Must know

                                                                                                                Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                The Vice-President: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                • The post of the Vice–President of India is modelled on the lines of the American Vice–President.
                                                                                                                • Vice–President is next to the President in the official order of precedence.
                                                                                                                • According to Article 63, there shall be a Vice–President of India.
                                                                                                                • According to Article 64, the Vice–President is the ex–officio Chairman of the Council of States.
                                                                                                                • While acting as the President or discharging the functions of the President, the Vice– President does not perform the duties of the office of the chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64, proviso) and he is not entitled to the salary or allowance payable to the Chairman of Rajya Sabha but the salary and allowances of the President.
                                                                                                                • He is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of the Members (both elected and nominated) of both houses of Parliament.
                                                                                                                • According to Article 66 (1), the election of Vice-President is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is done by secret ballot.
                                                                                                                • The eligibility for election as Vice-President (a citizen of India, should have completed 35 years of age, and should be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha) is mentioned in Article 66 (3).
                                                                                                                • The Vice-President draws his salary (4 lakh per month) in his capacity as the ex–officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
                                                                                                                • The constitution has not fixed any emoluments for the Vice–President in that capacity.
                                                                                                                • According to Article 67, the Vice–President holds office for a term of five years. According to Article 67(a), a vice president may, by writing under his hand addressed to the president, resign his office.
                                                                                                                • According to Article 67 (b) he can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an absolute majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, but no resolution for this purpose shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.
                                                                                                                • The Vice – President of India and their terms of office is as follows
