                                                                                                                2.Dr. Zakir Hussain1962-1967
                                                                                                                3.V.V. Giri1967-1969
                                                                                                                4.G.S. Pathak1969-1974
                                                                                                                5.B. D. Jatti1974-1979
                                                                                                                6.M. Hidaytullah (Justice)1979-1984
                                                                                                                7.R. Venkataraman1984-1987
                                                                                                                Dr. Shankar Dayal Sharma1987-1992

                                                                                                                8.

                                                                                                                9.K. R. Narayanan1992-1997
                                                                                                                10.Dr. K.Krishnakant1997-2002
                                                                                                                11.Bhairon Singh Shekhawat2002-2007
                                                                                                                12.Mohd. Hamid Ansari2007-2017
                                                                                                                Venkaiah Naidu2017- 2022

                                                                                                                13.

                                                                                                                14. Jagdeep Dhankhar2022-2025
                                                                                                                15. C.P. Radhakrishnan2025- Incumbent
                                                                                                                • The Vice-President of India is elected by the members of an electoral college comprising –All the members of both the Houses of Parliament.

                                                                                                                Vice-President elected (Article 66(1)) by all members of both Houses of Parliament, by proportional representation through single transferable vote.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • According to Article 66, who among the following participates in the election of Vice-President of India?All the members of both the Houses of Parliament

                                                                                                                Article 66: all members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) elect the Vice-President; State Legislatures have no role.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • How is Vice-President of India elected?through election by the MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

                                                                                                                Vice-President → elected by MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Article 66(1)); not directly, not nominated. Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Electoral College for the 16th Vice Presidential Election of India for 2022 consists of how many members?788

                                                                                                                16th Vice-Presidential election (2022) electoral college = 788: 233 elected + 12 nominated Rajya Sabha members + 543 elected Lok Sabha members.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements. Which of these statements is/are correct?1 only

                                                                                                                Both President and Vice-President are elected indirectly; but State Legislature members vote only for the President (Article 54), not the Vice-President (Article 66).

                                                                                                                Don't confuse MLAs vote for President, not Vice-President; nominated MPs vote for Vice-President, not President.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Given below are two statements, Assertion (A) and Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is an acceptable explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                Vice-President must be qualified for election to the Council of States (Article 66(3)) because he is its ex-officio Chairman (Article 64); also citizen, age 35.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements about Vice-President of India.Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                Vice-President: ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64); elected by members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66(1)).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?The Vice-President

                                                                                                                Rajya Sabha Chairman → Vice-President (ex officio); he presides over it but is not its member.

                                                                                                                Memory aid Rajya Sabha is chaired by an outsider: the Vice-President.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following statements is not correct?Vice-President is appointed by the President of India

                                                                                                                Vice-President is elected by MPs via proportional representation and single transferable vote (Article 66), not appointed by the President. Other statements true.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India are not correct?1 and 4

                                                                                                                Vice-President must qualify for Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha (Article 66(3)(c)); removal: Rajya Sabha resolution by majority of all members, agreed by Lok Sabha, 14 days' notice (67(b)).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference of the election of the Vice-President of India, which is declared void by the Supreme Court of India, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Only (1)

                                                                                                                If the SC voids a Vice-President's election, his acts on or before the date of the decision stay valid (Article 71(2)); so only statement 1 is correct.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The Vice-President of India:All the four

                                                                                                                Vice-President: second-highest constitutional office (Article 63); no formal functions as VP as such; acts as President in his absence or on death, resignation, removal.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • IfVice-President of India has to discharge the duties of President of India in his absence due to some reasons, then what is/are true for such duration?(ii) and (iii)

                                                                                                                While acting as President, the Vice-President does not act as Rajya Sabha Chairman (Article 64), gets President's emoluments (Article 65(3)); if he resigns, CJI discharges President's duties.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The Vice-President may be removed from his office by a resolution of –Council of States

                                                                                                                Vice-President removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution (majority of all members) agreed to by Lok Sabha, after 14 days' notice (Article 67(b)); it starts only in Rajya Sabha. Must know

                                                                                                                Memory aid VP removal starts in his own House, the Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Among the four pairs given below which one consists of a correct-combination of dignitaries who became Vice-President after having held diplomatic posts of Ambassador and High Commissioners?Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and V.V. Giri

                                                                                                                Vice-Presidents with diplomatic posts: S. Radhakrishnan (Ambassador to USSR, 1949-1952) and V.V. Giri (High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, 1947-1951); K.R. Narayanan was Ambassador to China.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Who among the following has held the office of the Vice-President of India?1 and 4

                                                                                                                Held Vice-President's office: M. Hidayatullah (1979-84) and Shankar Dayal Sharma (1987-92); Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy were only Presidents.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which one of the following statements is not correct?Zakir Hussain was the first Vice-President of India.

                                                                                                                First Vice-President → Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1952-1962), not Zakir Hussain (second, 1962-1967). Also true: amendment Bills need special majority; constitutional cases need five judges.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The serial number of Mr. Mohammad Ansari as Vice President of India is12th

                                                                                                                Mohammad Hamid Ansari → 12th Vice-President, took office 2007, re-elected July 2012. First VP: S. Radhakrishnan (1952-1962).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      The Council of Ministers: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • The Central Council of Ministers includes Prime Minister, Cabinet ministers, Ministers of State and Minister of State (independent).
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 74(1), there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice. However, the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice, and the President shall act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration (added through the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978).
                                                                                                                      • The advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court [Article 74 (2)].
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 75
                                                                                                                      • (1), the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 75 (1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. This provision was added by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003.
                                                                                                                      • As per Article 75(2), the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
                                                                                                                      • The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                      • The term ‘Cabinet’ was mentioned only in clause
                                                                                                                      • (3) of the Article 352 of the Constitution and it was inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act. It did not find a place in the original content of the Constitution.
                                                                                                                      • Cabinet includes Cabinet Ministers and the Prime Minister.
                                                                                                                      • Due to the Ministerial Responsibility, for every act of the bureaucrats, the concerned Minister is answerable to the Parliament.
                                                                                                                      • The Central Cabinet Secretariat is directly under the control of Prime Minister. Its administrative head is the Cabinet Secretary, who is the ex-officio chairman of the Civil Services Board.
                                                                                                                      • A person who is not a member of either house of the Parliament can also be appointed as a minister, but within six months, he must become a member (either by election or by nomination) of either house of the Parliament, otherwise he ceases to be a minister.
                                                                                                                      • The President administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Prime Minister and other ministers.
                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister is the Chairman of Union Cabinet meetings.
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 78, it shall be the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers and to furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation as the President may call for. The Prime Minister submits his resignation to the President. The ministries of departments are created by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961, which are rules made by the President under Article 77 of the Constitution. There are 53 ministries at present in the Government of India.
                                                                                                                      • The number of Ministries at the centre on 15 August 1947 was 18.
                                                                                                                      The Council of Ministers: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • The Central Council of Ministers includes Prime Minister, Cabinet ministers, Ministers of State and Minister of State (independent).
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 74(1), there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice. However, the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice, and the President shall act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration (added through the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978).
                                                                                                                      • The advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court [Article 74 (2)].
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 75
                                                                                                                      • (1), the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 75 (1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. This provision was added by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003.
                                                                                                                      • As per Article 75(2), the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
                                                                                                                      • The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                      • (3) of the Article 352 of the Constitution and it was inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act. It did not find a place in the original content of the Constitution.
                                                                                                                      • Cabinet includes Cabinet Ministers and the Prime Minister.
                                                                                                                      • Due to the Ministerial Responsibility, for every act of the bureaucrats, the concerned Minister is answerable to the Parliament.
                                                                                                                      • The Central Cabinet Secretariat is directly under the control of Prime Minister. Its administrative head is the Cabinet Secretary, who is the ex-officio chairman of the Civil Services Board.
                                                                                                                      • A person who is not a member of either house of the Parliament can also be appointed as a minister, but within six months, he must become a member (either by election or by nomination) of either house of the Parliament, otherwise he ceases to be a minister.
                                                                                                                      • The President administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Prime Minister and other ministers.
                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister is the Chairman of Union Cabinet meetings.
                                                                                                                      • According to Article 78, it shall be the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers and to furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation as the President may call for. The Prime Minister submits his resignation to the President. The ministries of departments are created by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961, which are rules made by the President under Article 77 of the Constitution. There are 53 ministries at present in the Government of India.

                                                                                                                      • As per Article 300 of the Constitution of India, the legal name of the Government of India is–The Union of India

                                                                                                                      Article 300 → the legal name of the Government of India is 'The Union of India'.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:Only 2, 3 and 4 are correct.

                                                                                                                      PM is appointed by the President, heads the Council of Ministers, and need not be an MP at appointment; Union executive power vests in the President (Article 53(1)), not PM.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following statements is correct about Prime Minister of India?Prime Minister is the real head of the Council of Ministers.

                                                                                                                      PM is the real head of the Council of Ministers: Article 74(1) → Council headed by PM aids and advises the President, who acts on that advice.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Prime Minister of India is –Appointed

                                                                                                                      Prime Minister is appointed by the President; other Ministers are appointed by the President on the PM's advice (Article 75(1)).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister of India is the head of the –Central Government

                                                                                                                      PM heads the Central Government (Head of Government); the President is Head of State (Article 74(1)).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Article 78 of the Constitution of India lays down the duties of the –Prime Minister

                                                                                                                      Article 78 → PM's duties to the President: furnish information on Union administration; place a minister's decision before the Council if the President requires.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                      Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks (British convention). Article 75(1A) (91st Amendment, 2003): total ministers incl. PM not above 15% of Lok Sabha strength.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Size of Council of Ministers has been restricted to 15 percent of membership of Lok Sabha by which Constitutional Amendment?91st Amendment

                                                                                                                      91st Amendment (2003) → ministers incl. PM limited to 15% of Lok Sabha members (Article 75); same for States incl. CM (Article 164).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Cabinet means –Ministers with Cabinet Rank

                                                                                                                      Cabinet = PM plus Cabinet-rank ministers only; a senior body within the Council of Ministers and the supreme decision-making body. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The word ‘mantrimandal’ (cabinet) is mentioned only once in Constitution, and that is in–Article 352

                                                                                                                      The word 'Cabinet' appears only in Article 352(3): President issues an Emergency Proclamation only when the Union Cabinet communicates it in writing.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                      Both false: Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report (1950) proposed grouping ministries, not a dedicated reforms minister; Department of Personnel (1 August 1970) was under Cabinet Secretariat, later Home Ministry.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • With reference to Union Government, consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                      Ministries are allotted to Ministers by the President on the PM's advice; Ministries are NOT created by the PM on the Cabinet Secretary's advice.

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Cabinet Secretary heads the Cabinet Secretariat and chairs the Civil Services Board; he does not create Ministries.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements about Central Government:Only 2 is correct

                                                                                                                      Art 77(3) → President makes rules of business and allocates portfolios among ministers on the PM's advice; PM and Cabinet Secretary do not 'form' Ministries.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who exercises the actual/executive power under the parliamentary form of Government?Prime Minister

                                                                                                                      Parliamentary form of government → actual/real executive power exercised by the Prime Minister (Article 75).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                      Art 77(1) → all executive action taken in the name of the President (not PM); Art 77(3) → President makes rules for business and its allocation among Ministers.

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Don't pick 'in the name of the Prime Minister'; executive action is always in the President's name.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • If the Prime Minister of India belongs to the Upper House of Parliament:He will not be able to vote in his favour in the event of a no-confidence motion

                                                                                                                      PM from Rajya Sabha can speak in Lok Sabha but cannot vote there → cannot vote in his own favour in a no-confidence motion.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Speak in both Houses, vote only in your own House.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which Article of the Indian Constitution describes the appointment and disqualification of the Council of Ministers.Article 75

                                                                                                                      Article 75 → appointment of PM and Ministers (75(1)); Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (75(2)).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Prime Minister of India is generally-Member of Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                      PM is generally a Lok Sabha member, but not compulsorily; can be from Rajya Sabha; Indira Gandhi → first PM from Rajya Sabha at appointment.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister of India, at the time of his/her appointmentNeed not necessarily be a member of one of the Houses of the Parliament but must become a member of one of the Houses within six months.

                                                                                                                      Art 75(5) → PM need not be an MP at appointment, but must become a member of either House (LS or RS) within 6 months.

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Don't pick 'must join Lok Sabha'; any one House of Parliament is enough.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • What is the minimum age requirement to become the Prime Minister of India?25 years

                                                                                                                      Minimum age to become Prime Minister → 25 years (same as for a Lok Sabha member).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister is –Appointed by the President

                                                                                                                      Art 75(1) → PM appointed by the President; other Ministers appointed by President on PM's advice; not elected by Lok Sabha or Parliament.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following statements is correct about the Prime Minister of India?He has full discretion in the choice of persons who are to serve as ministers in his cabinet.

                                                                                                                      PM has full discretion in choosing ministers (Art 75(1)); a non-member minister must enter either House within 6 consecutive months, else ceases (Art 75(5)). Must know

                                                                                                                      Memory aid 75(5) → '5' looks like 'S' for Six months.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following statements is not true regarding the Parliament of India.The membership of the cabinet is restricted to the Lower House.

                                                                                                                      Cabinet membership is NOT restricted to the Lower House; a non-member can be minister for 6 months (Art 75(5)); cabinet needs Lok Sabha majority confidence.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Prime Minister of India is responsible to whom?The Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                      Prime Minister (with Council of Ministers) → collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)), not to the President or Cabinet.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible:1, 2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                      Collective responsibility → to the House of the People; a constitutional obligation under Article 75(3); Article 74(3) does not exist.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Council of Ministers is responsible to the –—

                                                                                                                      Council of Ministers → collectively responsible to Lok Sabha; when Lok Sabha is not an option, the nearest answer is Parliament. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to–Only to Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                      Union Council of Ministers → collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Don't pick 'Parliament' when 'Only to Lok Sabha' is offered; Rajya Sabha cannot remove the ministry.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Assertion (A): The Council of Ministers in the Union of India is collectively responsible both to the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.(A) is false, but (R) is true.

                                                                                                                      (A) false: Council responsible only to Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)); (R) true: members of either House can be Union Ministers, but vote only in own House. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:2 and 3

                                                                                                                      Council responsible to Lok Sabha, not 'Parliament' (Art 75(3)); Ministers hold office at President's pleasure (75(2)); PM communicates legislative proposals to President (Art 78(a)).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not explicitly stated in the Constitution of India but followed as a convention?The Prime Minister has to resign if he loses the majority in the Lower House.

                                                                                                                      PM resigning on losing majority in Lok Sabha → a convention, not written in the Constitution (flows from collective responsibility, Art 75(3)).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • In Indian Polity, the executive is subordinate to the-Legislature

                                                                                                                      In Indian polity, the Executive is subordinate to the Legislature; Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following motions, the Council of Ministers in India can move?Confidence Motion

                                                                                                                      Council of Ministers can move a Confidence Motion; No-Confidence Motion only in Lok Sabha; if passed by Lok Sabha majority → Council must resign. Must know

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Confidence Motion (moved by the government) with No-Confidence/Censure Motion (moved against it).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • After resigning, whose permission does a minister require to give a statement in Lok Sabha?Speaker

                                                                                                                      A minister who resigns may make a statement on his resignation in Lok Sabha with the Speaker's permission; he cannot be compelled to do so.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The number of Lok Sabha members required to table a ‘No Confidence Motion’ against the Council of Ministers is50

                                                                                                                      No-Confidence Motion against the Council of Ministers in Lok Sabha → needs at least 50 members to table it. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements regarding a ‘No Confidence Motion’ in India:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                      No-Confidence Motion: not mentioned in the Constitution; introduced only in Lok Sabha; procedure in Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure (Rule 198).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following statement is not correct regarding “No-Confidence Motion”?—

                                                                                                                      No-Confidence Motion: only in Lok Sabha (Rule 198); notice to Secretary-General, not Speaker; 28 such motions and 11 confidence motions till 15 August 2023; first by J.B. Kripalani (1963).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not a correct situation arising after the resignation of the Council of Ministers?President’s Rule will be imposed.

                                                                                                                      Resignation of Council of Ministers does NOT bring President's Rule; President asks it to continue till an alternative arrangement (new government or early election).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which leader of Madhya Pradesh became the Defence Minister first and later Home Minister in Nehru’s Cabinet?Kailash Nath Katju

                                                                                                                      Kailash Nath Katju (Madhya Pradesh) → in Nehru's Cabinet: Law Minister and Home Minister 1951, Defence Minister 1955; CM of Madhya Pradesh 1957-1962.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who was the First Finance Minister of Independent India?—

                                                                                                                      First Finance Minister of independent India → R.K. Shanmukham Chetty (1947-1948), in Nehru's Cabinet.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who was the Law Minister in the first Cabinet of post independence India?B.R. Ambedkar

                                                                                                                      First Law Minister of independent India → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; Law Minister in the 1946 Interim Government → Jogendra Nath Mandal.

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse The first Cabinet (Ambedkar) with the Interim Government of 1946 (Jogendra Nath Mandal).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Among the following given names, whose portfolio in the first cabinet of India (1947) was different from his portfolio in the Interim Government (1946)?Only (iii)

                                                                                                                      C.H. Bhabha → Works, Mines and Power (Interim Govt 1946) → Commerce (first Cabinet 1947); Rajendra Prasad, Jagjivan Ram, Baldev Singh kept same portfolios.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who was the 12th Prime Minister of India?Deve Gowda

                                                                                                                      12th Prime Minister of India → H.D. Deve Gowda (counting acting PM Gulzari Lal Nanda); Narendra Modi → 15th PM.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Match the Prime Ministers with their tenure.(iv) (iii) (i) (v) (ii)

                                                                                                                      PM tenures: V.P. Singh 1989-90; Chandra Shekhar 1990-91; Deve Gowda 1996-97; I.K. Gujral 1997-98; Atal Bihari Vajpayee 1999-2004.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Order VP → Chandra Shekhar → Deve Gowda → Gujral → Vajpayee follows the years 1989 to 1999.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who among the following held the office of the Prime Minister of India more than once?All of above

                                                                                                                      PM more than once → Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Gulzari Lal Nanda (acting PM twice), Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who among the following occupied the office of the Prime Minister of India more than once with gaps in between their political career?3, 4 and 5 only

                                                                                                                      PM more than once with gaps → Gulzari Lal Nanda (1964, 1966), Indira Gandhi (1966-1977, 1980-1984), Vajpayee (1996, 1998-2004); not Nehru or Shastri.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which Prime Minister died outside India?Lal Bahadur Shashtri

                                                                                                                      PM who died outside India → Lal Bahadur Shastri (second PM), in Tashkent (capital of Uzbekistan), 11 January 1966.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Match the following States and their respective Chief Ministers, who became Prime Minister of India.ii v iv i iii

                                                                                                                      CMs who became PM: Narasimha Rao → undivided Andhra Pradesh; Morarji Desai → Bombay; Deve Gowda → Karnataka; Charan Singh → undivided Uttar Pradesh; Modi → Gujarat.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who amongst the following had never been the Chief Minister of any State before becoming the Prime Minister of India?Chandra Shekhar

                                                                                                                      Never a Chief Minister before becoming PM → Chandra Shekhar; Deve Gowda, Narasimha Rao and Morarji Desai were CMs earlier.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following person was not a Chief Minister of any state before holding the office of Prime Minister?Chandra Shekhar

                                                                                                                            The Attorney-General and the C.A.G. + Order of Precedence

                                                                                                                            The Attorney-General and the C.A.G.: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                            • The Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Attorney General for India.
                                                                                                                            • He is the highest law officer in the country.
                                                                                                                            • The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court to be the Attorney General for India [Article 76 (1)].
                                                                                                                            • It shall be the duty of the Attorney-General to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred or assigned to him by the President [Article 76(2)].
                                                                                                                            • In the performance of his duties, the Attorney-General shall have the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India [Article 76(3)].
                                                                                                                            • The Attorney-General shall hold office during the pleasure of the President, and shall receive such remuneration as the President may determine [Article 76 (4)].
                                                                                                                            • He has the right to speak and to take part in the proceedings of both the houses of the Parliament or their joint sitting but without the right to vote.
                                                                                                                            • He enjoys all the privileges and immunities that are available to a member of Parliament.
                                                                                                                            • According to Article 165 (1), the Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of a High Court to be Advocate-General for the State. He advises the State Governments on legal matters.
                                                                                                                            • He is the first legal adviser to the State Government.
                                                                                                                            • He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
                                                                                                                            • According to Article 148(1), there shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India who shall be appointed by the President and shall only be removed from office in like manner or on the like grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                            • The Comptroller and Auditor-General shall not be eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State after he has ceased to hold his office [Article 148(4)].
                                                                                                                            • He holds office for a period of 6 years or up to the age of 65 years.
                                                                                                                            • He can be removed by the President on the basis of a resolution passed to that effect by both the Houses of Parliament with special majority, either on the grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
                                                                                                                            • He is the guardian of the public purse and audits the entire financial system of the country at both the levels – the Centre and the State.
                                                                                                                            • He is called as the ‘friend, philosopher and guide’ of the Public Accounts Committee.
                                                                                                                            • He submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of the centre to the President who shall, in turn, causes them to be laid before both the houses of the Parliament [Article 151(1)].
                                                                                                                            • He submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of a State to the Governor who shall, in turn, place them before the State Legislature [ Article 151(2)].
                                                                                                                            • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said that the CAG is probably the most important officer under the Constitution of India.
                                                                                                                            • The Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act came into effect in 1971. This Act was amended in 1976 for the separation of accounts from audit.
                                                                                                                            • The CAG submits three audit reports to the President, an audit report on appropriation accounts, an audit report on finance accounts, and an audit report on public undertakings. The President causes these reports to be laid before both the Houses of the Parliament. After this, the Public Accounts Committee examines them and reports its findings to the Parliament.
                                                                                                                            Order of Precedence: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                            • The order of precedence is a protocol list in which the functionaries and authorities are recorded by the rank in the Central and State Governments, including foreign diplomats and awardees.
                                                                                                                            • It is meant for state and ceremonial occasions and has no application in the day-to-day functioning of the Government.
                                                                                                                            • The notification regarding this was released on 26 July, 1979. The current order of precedence is as follows

                                                                                                                            • Who advises the Government of India on legal matters?Attorney General

                                                                                                                            Art 76 → Attorney General advises Government of India on legal matters; first law officer; appointed by President, holds office during President's pleasure. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Attorney General of India is appointed bythe President of India

                                                                                                                            Attorney General (Art 76) → appointed by the President, holds office at his pleasure (no security of tenure); highest/first law officer of India. Must know

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Not appointed by the Law Minister or PM; only the President appoints and removes him.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The chief legal advisor to government of india is:Attorney General of India

                                                                                                                            Chief legal adviser to Government of India → Attorney General (Art 76), part of Union Executive; has right of audience in all courts of India. Must know

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse With Solicitor General (second law officer) or Advocate General (State).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Who is the government's chief legal advisor and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India?None of the above

                                                                                                                            Government's chief legal adviser and main lawyer in Supreme Court → Attorney General (Art 76); not Solicitor General, CJI or CAG → 'None of the above'.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • As per Article 76 of the Indian Constitution, the President shall appoint a person to be Attorney General for India:who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.

                                                                                                                            Art 76(1) → AG must be qualified to be appointed a Supreme Court Judge; Art 76(4) → holds office during the pleasure of the President.

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Not 'qualified as a High Court Judge'; that is the Advocate General of a State.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            AG → qualified to be SC judge (Art 76(1)); remuneration determined by the President, not Parliament (Art 76(4)); holds office at President's pleasure.

                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements with reference to Attorney General of India:Only 2

                                                                                                                            Attorney General (Art 76) → holds office at President's pleasure, not PM's; speaks in both Houses but cannot vote; Constitution doesn't require him to resign with the government. Must know

                                                                                                                            AG: advises on legal matters referred by President; audience in all courts (Art 76(3)); speaks in Parliament, no vote (Art 88); not full-time counsel, may practise privately.

                                                                                                                            Non-members in Parliament's proceedings → Attorney General (both Houses) and Vice-President (Rajya Sabha only) → 'more than one'; for 'both Houses' the answer is AG. Must know

                                                                                                                            Solicitor General → legal adviser; second law officer, subordinate to and assists the Attorney General; helped by Additional Solicitor Generals. Must know

Advisory jurisdiction → Supreme Court (Art 143), not High Courts.
