                                                                                                                            • The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by-President

                                                                                                                            CAG → appointed by President by warrant (Art 148(1)); removed like SC judge; Union audit reports → President; State audit reports → Governor. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Where are the salary and service conditions of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India specified?Second Schedule of the Constitution of India

                                                                                                                            CAG salary and service conditions → Part E of the Second Schedule; CAG appointed under Art 148; head of Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The tenure of Comptroller and Auditor General of India is –6 Years

                                                                                                                            CAG term → 6 years or age 65, whichever earlier (CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971); service conditions set by Parliament (Art 148(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                            Memory aid CAG: '6 or 65', whichever comes first.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is not true about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?He can be removed by the President.

                                                                                                                            Not true: 'CAG removed by the President' at will; removed only like an SC judge (Art 148(1)); salary equals SC judge; no further government office (148(4)). Must know

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Removal order is signed by the President, but only after Parliament's address, as for an SC judge.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Assertion (A): The Duty of Comptroller and AuditorBoth (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

                                                                                                                            CAG checks not just legality but also propriety of expenditure, as he upholds the Constitution and Parliament's laws in financial administration; he does NOT control issue of public money. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In India, other than ensuring that public funds are used efficiently and for the intended purpose, what is the importance of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?2 and 3

                                                                                                                            CAG reports → discussed by Public Accounts Committee; investigating agencies can press charges using them; CAG has no exchequer control in emergency and no judicial powers.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The ultimate responsibility of taking due action on the comments of the Comptroller and Auditor General vests withParliament

                                                                                                                            Final action on CAG's comments → Parliament (via Public Accounts Committee); Art 151(1): Union audit reports go to President, then laid before Parliament.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Who amongst the following attends the meetings of the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament?Comptroller and Auditor General of India

                                                                                                                            CAG attends meetings of Parliament's Public Accounts Committee; CAG's duties and powers → Article 149. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Match the following List - P (CAG) with List - R (Articles):I III IV II

                                                                                                                            CAG Articles: 148 → appointment; 149 → duties and powers; 150 → form of accounts of Union and States; 151 → audit reports.

                                                                                                                            Memory aid 148-151 in order: Appoint, Duties, Form, Reports.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed by the President. He can be removed –—

                                                                                                                            CAG removed like an SC judge (Art 148(1), 124(4)) → by President after an address by both Houses (special majority) for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which among the following is not true about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India? I. The adminstrative expenses of his office are subject to vote of Parliament. II. He is not eligible for further office under the Government of India or of any State after he quits office. III. The CAG can be removed from office on the ground of proven incapactiy or misbehaviour after an address by both the houses of Parliament. Select the correct answer:Only I

                                                                                                                            Not true: CAG office expenses 'voted' → they are charged on Consolidated Fund of India (Art 148(6)); CAG barred from later government office (148(4)); removed like SC judge.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is a friend and guide of:Public Accounts Committee

                                                                                                                            CAG → 'Friend, Philosopher and Guide' of the Public Accounts Committee; attends PAC sittings and assists its deliberations.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The power to grant or refuse leave to the Comptroller and Auditor General shall vest in thePresident

                                                                                                                            Power to grant or refuse leave to CAG → President; CAG's salary and service conditions determined by Parliament by law (Art 148(3)).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In which year was accounting separated from auditing and Comptroller and Auditor General's task only remained confined to auditing the Government Accounts?1976

                                                                                                                            CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Amendment Act, 1976 (in force 1 March 1976) → accounting separated from audit; CAG confined to auditing Government accounts.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Amendment to (CAG Duties, Power and Condition of Service Act) 1971 separates Accounts from Audit and relieves the CAG of his responsibility in the matters of preparation of Accounts. The amendments were made in the year.1976

                                                                                                                            Amendment to the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 → made in 1976; separated Accounts from Audit, relieving CAG of preparing accounts.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Accounts of the States are controlled by the:None of these

                                                                                                                            Accounts of the States (and the Union) → controlled by the CAG; not Governor, CM or State Finance Secretary → 'None of these'.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Who is called the Guardian of Public Purse?Comptroller and Auditor General

                                                                                                                            Guardian of the Public Purse → Comptroller and Auditor General (Art 148); head of Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • C.A.G. (Comptroller and Auditor General) of India acts asThe Guardian of Public Finance.

                                                                                                                            CAG → guardian of public finance; ensures no money from Consolidated Fund of India or of a State is spent without the Legislature's authorisation.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Girish Chandra Murmu has become India's:14th Comptroller & Auditor General

                                                                                                                            Girish Chandra Murmu → 14th CAG of India; K. Sanjay Murthy → 15th CAG (appointed 2024).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.3 1 4 2

                                                                                                                            Vice-President → Rajya Sabha; CAG → Public Accounts Committee; Solicitor General → Supreme Court; Attorney General → meetings of Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following options is not correct? Public Finance Studies financial activities of the Government. It consists of ………Functioning of Commercial Bank

                                                                                                                            Public Finance → studies Government revenue, public expenditure and financial administration; NOT the functioning of commercial banks.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Arrange the following words in a logical and meaningful order -2, 1, 4, 3, 5

                                                                                                                            Order of precedence: President → Vice-President → Prime Minister → Speaker (Lok Sabha) → Members of Parliament.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Consider the following functionaries:4, 3, 2, 1

                                                                                                                            Precedence: Chief Justice of India → Union Cabinet Minister → Chief Election Commissioner → Cabinet Secretary.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In the order of precedure of the government of India which of the following come/comes above the Chief Justice of India?Former President

                                                                                                                            Precedence: President; Vice-President; PM; Governors (within own State); Former Presidents; Deputy PM (5A); then CJI and Lok Sabha Speaker (equal).

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Former President ranks ABOVE the Chief Justice; Attorney General and Service Chiefs rank below.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In the Indian Order of Precedence, who amongst the following comes first?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                            Precedence 9A → UPSC Chairman, Chief Election Commissioner and CAG (equal); High Court Chief Justice → 14; so 'more than one' comes first.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Who is the topmost civilian officer in Government of India?Cabinet Secretary

                                                                                                                            Topmost civilian officer of Government of India → Cabinet Secretary; ex-officio head of Civil Services Board, Cabinet Secretariat, IAS and all Civil Services.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  The Parliament (1) · part 1 of 2

                                                                                                                                  The Parliament (1): key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Parliament is the legislative organ of the Union Government.
                                                                                                                                  • Articles 79 to 122 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of the President and the two houses - House of the People and the Council of States.
                                                                                                                                  • Lok Sabha is also known as the "House of the People".
                                                                                                                                  • Its maximum strength is 550. At present, it has 543 (States-524, UTs-19) members.
                                                                                                                                  • Out of 550 members, at most 530 members are representative of states, 20 members are representative of Union territories. If, in the opinion of the President, there is not enough representation of the Anglo-Indian Community in the Lok Sabha, then he could nominate two members of that community to the Lok Sabha. In this regard, the arrangements related to the Anglo-Indian Community have not been extended beyond the stipulated date (25 January, 2020) by 'The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019' [The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Sixth Amendment) Bill, 2019]. Thus, the arrangements for the nomination of two members of the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha have ended.
                                                                                                                                  • The allocation of state-wise seats in the Lok Sabha is based on the Census of 1971.
                                                                                                                                  • According to the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001, the next assessment shall be held after the year 2026.
                                                                                                                                  • In Lok Sabha seats are allotted on the basis of the population.
                                                                                                                                  • The normal tenure of Lok Sabha is 5 years from the date of its first meeting after the general elections but it can be dissolved by the President in between.
                                                                                                                                  • Under the Article 83(2) Proviso, Lok Sabha can be extended during the time of National Emergency for one year at a time.
                                                                                                                                  • In any case of extension, it can't continue beyond the period of 6 months after the emergency has ceased to operate.
                                                                                                                                  • The qualifications of a person in order to be elected a member of Lok Sabha are (a) He must be a citizen of India and (b) He must not be less than 25 years. (c) He must make and subscribe to an oath (d) He must possess other qualifications prescribed by the Parliament by law.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 93, the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are elected by Lok Sabha from among its members.
                                                                                                                                  • Suspension of Lok Sabha (Adjournment/Adjournment Sine die of Lok Sabha sitting) is called up by the Speaker, whereas prorogation and dissolution of Loksabha is called up by the President of India.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 94 (b), the Speaker of Lok Sabha addresses his resignation in writing to the Deputy Speaker and vice-versa.
                                                                                                                                  • The speaker of Lok Sabha is removed from his Post by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of Lok Sabha and such resolution shall not be moved until and unless a 14-day advance notice is given.
                                                                                                                                  • While a resolution of removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker/Deputy Speaker concerned can not preside but both have the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the house.
                                                                                                                                  • While the proposal of removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is in process, the Speaker or Deputy Speaker (as the case may be) have the right to vote in first instance but not in the case of equality of votes.
                                                                                                                                  • The Speaker of Lok Sabha uses his casting vote only in case of a tie.
                                                                                                                                  • Lok Sabha Secretariat directly functions under the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                                  • After the general elections, the Protem Speaker administers the oath to the newly elected members of Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                                  • As provided by the Constitution, the Speaker of the last Lok Sabha vacates his office immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha. Therefore, the President appoints a senior member of the Lok Sabha as the Pro-tem Speaker.
                                                                                                                                  • Article 85(1) empowers the President to summon each house of the Parliament if he thinks fit.
                                                                                                                                  • In any case, the interval between the two consecutive sessions of the houses cannot be more than six months. (
                                                                                                                                  • Thus as per the Constitution, it is mandatory for Lok Sabha to meet at least twice a year.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 100(3), the quorum of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha shall be 1/10th of the total members of the respective houses.
                                                                                                                                  • Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of Lok Sabha seats
                                                                                                                                  • (80) followed by Maharashtra (48) and West Bengal (42). In January, 2022 the Election Commission of India (ECI) has increased the expenditure limits for candidates, contesting in the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly polls. The ECI hiked the poll expenditure limit upto Rs. 95 lakh from the existing Rs. 70 Lakhs for the Lok Sabha election. For the state assembly elections, the expenditure limit has been enhanced to Rs. 40 lakh from Rs. 28 lakh. For small states, revised expenditure for the Loksabha is increased by Rs. 75 Lakhs from Rs. 54 Lakhs. While, in the case of small state assembly it is increased to Rs. 28 Lakhs from the previous limit of Rs. 20 Lakhs.
                                                                                                                                  • First Lok Sabha elections were held from 25 October, 1951 to 21 February, 1952.
                                                                                                                                  • The elections were conducted for 489 seats.
                                                                                                                                  • First Meeting of Lok Sabha took place on 13th May, 1952.
                                                                                                                                  • Ganesh Vasudev Mavlankar became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha and remained in this post till his death on 27 February, 1956. M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar was the speaker for the remaining tenure of the first Lok Sabha. In 1954, the first resolution/motion for removal of the speaker was brought against the first Speaker of Lok Sabha, G.V. Mavlankar, by Vigneshwar Missir (Socialist Party M.P. from Bihar), J.B. Kriplani and some other members of Opposition in the Lok Sabha which was rejected by the Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                                  • First Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha was M.A. Ayyangar.
                                                                                                                                  • The First woman speaker of Lok Sabha was Meira Kumar.
                                                                                                                                  • The Speaker of the present (18th) Lok Sabha is Om Birla.
                                                                                                                                  • What is the minimum age laid down for a person to seek election to the Lok Sabha?25 years

                                                                                                                                  Minimum age: Lok Sabha member → 25 years; Rajya Sabha (Council of States) → 30 years (Article 84(b)). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Upper House, older members: Lok 25, Rajya 30.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not correct with regard to the elections to the Lok Sabha?The electoral rolls are prepared under the direction and control of the President of India.

                                                                                                                                  Not correct: rolls under President → electoral rolls prepared under Election Commission's control (Art 324(1)); Lok Sabha elections on adult suffrage (Art 326).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed byany citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency.

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha nomination paper → any citizen of India whose name is on the electoral roll of any parliamentary constituency (Section 4(d), RP Act, 1951).

                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Need not be a resident of the constituency he contests from.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The state wise seat allocation in Lok Sabha is based on -Population

                                                                                                                                  State-wise Lok Sabha seats → allotted by Population (Art 81), on the 1971 Census; equal-ratio rule not applied to States with population up to six million. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The state-wise allocation of seats in Lok Sabha is based on the 1971 Census. Up to which year does this remain intact?2026

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha seat allocation on 1971 Census → frozen till 2026 by 84th Amendment Act, 2001 (Art 81(3) proviso); delimitation of constituencies also frozen. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 1971 census, frozen till 2026.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Maximum strength of Lok Sabha as stipulated in the Constitution of India is -None of these

                                                                                                                                  Constitutional maximum of Lok Sabha → 550 (530 States + 20 UTs); earlier 552 with 2 Anglo-Indians (Art 331), whose nomination ended 25 January 2020.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following Constitutional Amendments is related to raising the number of Members of Lok Sabha to be elected from the States?7th and 31st

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha seats raised by 7th Amendment, 1956 (520) and 31st Amendment, 1973 (525 → 545); present maximum 550 (530 States + 20 UTs).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The Strength of the Lok Sabha was increased from 525 to 545 through which Amendment?31st

                                                                                                                                  31st Amendment Act, 1973 → Lok Sabha strength 525 → 545; State seats 500 → 525; UT seats 25 → 20.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The maximum number of members in Lok Sabha can be -550

                                                                                                                                  Maximum Lok Sabha strength (Art 81) → 550 (530 States + 20 UTs); present strength → 543 (524 States + 19 UTs). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Don't mix 550 (maximum) with 543 (present); 2 Anglo-Indian nominations ended 25 January 2020.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • What can be the maximum representation from the Union Territories to the Lok Sabha??20

                                                                                                                                  Art 81 → not more than 530 members from States and not more than 20 from Union Territories; of 543 seats in 2009, 530 were from States. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • How many seats are reserved for UTs in Lok Sabha?20

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha seats for UTs → up to 20 (Art 81); now 19 (Delhi 7, J&K 5, Dadra-Daman 2, others 1 each); UT seats in Rajya Sabha → 8. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • In which Article of the Constitution of India was the provision for reservation of scheduled castes in the Lok Sabha made?Article 330

                                                                                                                                  Art 330 → SC/ST reservation in Lok Sabha; Art 331 → Anglo-Indian nomination (ended January 2020, 104th Amendment, 2019); Art 332 → SC/ST in State Assemblies.

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 330 = Lok Sabha, 332 = State Assemblies (Centre before State).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha does not exist in the states of:Kerala and Tamil Nadu

                                                                                                                                  No ST reservation in Lok Sabha → Kerala and Tamil Nadu; Karnataka and Meghalaya got ST seats (2 each) after 2008 delimitation.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • There is no reservation for SC and ST for Lok Sabha in:Arunachal Pradesh; Jammu & Kashmir

                                                                                                                                  No SC/ST Lok Sabha reservation → Arunachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir; after 2008 both Meghalaya seats reserved for STs.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • How many seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes in the Lok Sabha?84

                                                                                                                                  After 2008 delimitation: SC seats in Lok Sabha → 84 (earlier 79); ST → 47 (earlier 41); general → 412; all voters elect reserved seats.

                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse No separate electorate: reserved SC/ST seats are voted on by all voters of the constituency.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • If the number of seats allocated to a state in the Lok Sabha is 42, then the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Castes in that state will be:—

                                                                                                                                  SC/ST seats in a State (Art 330(2)) → in proportion to their population share; e.g. 42-seat West Bengal SC 8 → 10, Andhra 6 → 7 after 2008. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following States has the highest number of reserve seats for the Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?Madhya Pradesh

                                                                                                                                  Most ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats → Madhya Pradesh (6); Jharkhand, Odisha 5 each; Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra 4 each; none in UP and Bihar. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Who holds power to appoint the nominees from Anglo Indian Community in the Lok Sabha?—

                                                                                                                                  Anglo-Indian nominees to Lok Sabha → President could nominate up to 2 (Art 331); provision not extended beyond 25 January 2020 (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment, 2019). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Before completing its term, the Lok Sabha can be dissolved-By the President on the recommendation of Prime Minister

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha dissolved before its term → by President on recommendation of PM/Council of Ministers (Art 85(2)(b)); not at President's or Speaker's discretion.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                  Art 85(1): President summons Parliament at any time and place he thinks fit; gap between sessions max six months; no minimum sitting days and no 'three sessions' rule.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Generally how many sessions are there in the Lok Sabha?3

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha usually holds 3 sessions: Budget (February-May), Monsoon (July-August), Winter (November-December); Art 85 requires at least two a year.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The sitting of House of the People may be terminated by:All of the above

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha sitting ends by Adjournment (by Speaker), Prorogation or Dissolution (both by President, Art 85(2)).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:Only 4

                                                                                                                                  Summoning = convocation; Prorogation ends a session; Dissolution ends the House; prorogation is by the President (Art 85(2)), not the leader of the House. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The term of the Lok Sabha:Can be extended by one year at a time during the proclamation of emergency

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha term → five years (Art 83(2)); in Emergency Parliament may extend it by law one year at a time, not beyond six months after Emergency ends.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Session of Lok Sabha is called for at least-Two times in a year

                                                                                                                                  Art 85(1): gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months → Lok Sabha must meet at least two times a year.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • What is the quorum of Lok Sabha in relation to its strength?1/10

                                                                                                                                  Quorum of Lok Sabha (and Rajya Sabha) → 1/10 of total members of the House (Art 100(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which State sends the largest number of members in Lok Sabha?Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                  Largest number of Lok Sabha members → Uttar Pradesh (80); West Bengal 42, Bihar 40, Madhya Pradesh 29.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • In India which State has the largest representation in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                  Largest representation in both Houses → Uttar Pradesh: 80 Lok Sabha seats, 31 Rajya Sabha seats. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid UP = 80 + 31.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • So long as the representation in Lok Sabha is concerned, which states rank second and third?—

                                                                                                                                  Lok Sabha seats now: UP 80, Maharashtra 48 (second), West Bengal 42 (third), Bihar 40, Tamil Nadu 39, Madhya Pradesh 29. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • How many Lok Sabha seats are allocated to the State of Rajasthan?25

                                                                                                                                  Rajasthan → 25 Lok Sabha seats (4 SC, 3 ST).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • How many Lok Sabha members are elected from Uttarakhand?5

                                                                                                                                  Uttarakhand → 5 Lok Sabha members.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Seats allocated to Bihar in the House of People is the total of seats allocated to:—

                                                                                                                                  Before 2000: Bihar's 54 Lok Sabha seats = Madhya Pradesh 40 + Assam 14; after Jharkhand split, Bihar 40, Jharkhand 14; MP now 29.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following pair of States has equal seats in Lok Sabha?—

                                                                                                                                  Equal Lok Sabha seats (before 2014) → Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal, 42 each; Telangana took 17, Andhra now 25; Punjab 13, Assam 14, Gujarat 26, Rajasthan 25. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which among the following group of States/Union Territories has only one seat in the Lok Sabha?Chandigarh, Sikkim, Mizoram

                                                                                                                                        One Lok Sabha seat each → Chandigarh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Andaman and Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Nagaland, Puducherry.

                                                                                                                                        • From which of the following States two members of the Lok Sabha are elected?Tripura

                                                                                                                                        Two Lok Sabha seats each → Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya.

                                                                                                                                        • After delimitation the largest Lok Sabha Constituency in terms of number of voters in U.P. is –Unnao

                                                                                                                                        Among the options, largest UP Lok Sabha constituency by voters → Unnao; largest in the whole State → Ghaziabad.

                                                                                                                                        • 'Malogam', the polling station with only one voter during 2024 Lok Sabha elections falls in which state?Arunachal Pradesh

                                                                                                                                        Malogam (Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh) → polling station for a lone woman voter in 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Arunachal East seat, Hayuliang Assembly seat.

                                                                                                                                        • In which Lok Sabha seat, one of India’s Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), Shompen tribe, for the first time exercised their democratic right to vote in April 2024?Andaman and Nicobar

                                                                                                                                        Shompen tribe (PVTG, Great Nicobar) → voted for the first time on 19 April 2024, for the Andaman and Nicobar Lok Sabha seat.

                                                                                                                                        • What is the maximum expenditure limit for the Parliamentary Elections of a Constituency?—

                                                                                                                                        Lok Sabha poll expenditure limit → raised to Rs 95 lakh by Election Commission (January 2022); Assembly limit Rs 40 lakh (earlier Rs 28 lakh).

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • In the case of election to the Lok Sabha, the amount of Security deposited by general category candidates and SC/ST category candidates respectively is:—

                                                                                                                                        Lok Sabha security deposit: earlier Rs 10,000 (general) / Rs 5,000 (SC/ST); since 2010 → Rs 25,000 / Rs 12,500; Assembly → Rs 10,000 / Rs 5,000.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • A candidate of Lok Sabha Poll loses his security amount if he/she does not get –None of the above

                                                                                                                                        Candidate loses security deposit if he fails to get more than one-sixth (1/6) of valid votes polled in the constituency.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • First General Election of Lok Sabha was held in-1952

                                                                                                                                        First Lok Sabha general election → 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952, for 489 seats; first session began 13 May 1952. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • The tenure of which Lok Sabha was about 6 years?5th Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                        5th Lok Sabha → tenure about 6 years (15 March 1971 to 18 January 1977).

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • 9th Lok Sabha was dissolved on –13 March,1991

                                                                                                                                        9th Lok Sabha → constituted 2 December 1989, dissolved 13 March 1991.

                                                                                                                                        • In India Lok Sabha Speaker is -Chosen

                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following doesn't take the oath of the office?Speaker

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Who among the following doesn't take oath of the office?Speaker

                                                                                                                                        Speaker and Deputy Speaker take no oath of office (Arts 93-95); President (Art 60), VP (Art 69), PM and Ministers (Art 75(4)), SC Judges (Art 124(6)) do.

                                                                                                                                        • Who does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha submits his resignation to?The Deputy Speaker

                                                                                                                                        • How can the speaker of the Lok Sabha be removed?By a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a majority of all the members of the House.

                                                                                                                                        Speaker removed by a Lok Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all the then members (Art 94(c)), after at least 14 days' notice. Must know

Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                              The Parliament (2): key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                              • The Upper House of the Parliament is also known as the Rajya Sabha. It is also known as the 'Council of States'.
                                                                                                                                              • The Maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. According to Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than 238 members from the States and Union Territories (elected indirectly) and 12 other members are nominated by the President from amongst the persons having special knowledge or practical experience in the field of literature, science, art and social service (Present Strength is 245, out of which 12 are nominated members).
                                                                                                                                              • Representatives of each state shall be elected by the elected members of the legislative assembly of the state in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
                                                                                                                                              • Only 3 Union territories (Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir) out of 8 have representatives in Rajya Sabha.
                                                                                                                                              • Rajya Sabha is a Permanent house. Hence it is not subject to dissolution.
                                                                                                                                              • As nearly as possible 1/3rd members of the Rajya Sabha retire at the end of every second year.
                                                                                                                                              • The term of its members is 6 years.
                                                                                                                                              • A Person to be elected as a member of Rajya Sabha must fulfil two criteria- (1) he must be a citizen of India and
                                                                                                                                              • (2) he must not be less than 30 years of age. In addition to the prior two conditions, he must be an elector for a parliamentary constituency in India.
                                                                                                                                              • The Vice-President of India is the ex officio chairman of the Council of States/Upper House of Parliament.
                                                                                                                                              • When the Vice-President acts as the President he shall not be entitled to get the salary and allowances of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha. For this period, he receives salary and allowances of the President.
                                                                                                                                              • Rajya Sabha elects a deputy chairman from amongst its members.
                                                                                                                                              • The Deputy Chairman gives his resignation in writing to the Chairman.
                                                                                                                                              • Rajya Sabha has the power to remove the Deputy Chairman from his post, by a resolution passed by the absolute majority of the total members of Rajya Sabha. Such resolution can be moved only after giving at least 14 days' notice.
                                                                                                                                              • When the post of Chairman is vacant, the deputy chairman will perform the duties of the chairman.
                                                                                                                                              • While presiding over the Rajya Sabha, the Deputy Chairman can't vote in general, he can only exercise a casting vote in case of a tie.
                                                                                                                                              • When a resolution to remove the Vice President from his office is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Chairman and when a resolution of removal of the Deputy Chairman is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Deputy Chairman.
                                                                                                                                              • The representation of states in Rajya Sabha is given in proportion to their population.
                                                                                                                                              • For a quorum, there must be the presence of one-tenth of the total number of members in the Rajya Sabha.
                                                                                                                                              • The Representation of People Act 1951 (through an amendment in 2003) made a provision that any person can contest from anywhere for Rajya Sabha even ifhe is a resident of any other state. Now for contesting Rajya Sabha elections, a person must be an elector in a parliamentary constituency anywhere in India.
                                                                                                                                              • The 4th Schedule of the Indian Constitution enumerates the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats for states and union territories.
                                                                                                                                              • Article 249 states that if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with a 2/3 majority of its members present and voting, the Parliament can make laws in the national interest regarding the subjects of the state list, which are specified in the resolution.
                                                                                                                                              • It is valid for a period of1 year, but it can be extended by passing a resolution.
                                                                                                                                              • Article 250 empowers the Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the state list if the proclamation of emergency is in operation but, six months after the emergency ceases to operate, it automatically expires.
                                                                                                                                              • Article 252 empowers the Parliament to legislate for two or more states by consent and adoption of such legislation by any other state.
                                                                                                                                              • According to Article 253, Parliament has the power to make any law for the whole or part of the territory of India for implementing international agreements or conventions with any other country or any decision made at any international conference.
                                                                                                                                              • What is the fixed strength of Rajya Sabha?250

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha maximum strength → 250 (238 States/UTs + 12 nominated, Art 80); present 245 (225 States, 8 UTs, 12 nominated).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The representation in the Rajya Sabha includes:More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha → up to 238 members elected for States/UTs plus 12 nominated by President → 'more than one'; permanent body; members serve six years.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The Rajya Sabha consists of-250 members of which 12 members are nominated by the President of India.

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha → maximum 250 members, of which 12 nominated by the President; not more than 238 from States and UTs (Art 80).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The Representation of States in Council of States is based on –Ratio of their Population

                                                                                                                                              States' seats in Rajya Sabha → in ratio of their population (not equal); seats allotted in the Fourth Schedule.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements:None of these

                                                                                                                                              UTs ARE represented in Rajya Sabha (Delhi 3, Puducherry 1, J&K 4); election disputes → judiciary via election petition; Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha (Art 79).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The members of Council of States are elected by -Members of Legislative Assembly of States.

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha members → elected by elected MLAs of the State Legislative Assembly, by proportional representation through Single Transferable Vote (Art 80(4)).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following are correct about the Rajya Sabha?1 and 3

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha: never dissolved; one-third members retire every second year; member's term 6 years (not five); minimum age 30 (not 25). Must know

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • What is the tenure of a member of Council of State?6 years

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha member's tenure → 6 years; House is permanent (Art 83(1)); one-third retire every second year.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Rajya Sabha?One-third of its members retire every two years.

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha → permanent House, cannot be dissolved (Art 83(1)); one-third members retire every two years; each member elected for six years. Must know

                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Six-two-third: six-year term; every two years, one-third retire.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • Which one of the following statements about Rajya Sabha is correct?It is not subject to dissolution.

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha → not subject to dissolution; members elected by elected MLAs (Art 80(4)); Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman; Attorney General can speak in both Houses. Must know

                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse Rajya Sabha does not choose its Chairman from its members; it elects only the Deputy Chairman.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The number of members nominated by the President in Rajya Sabha is–12

                                                                                                                                              President nominates 12 members to Rajya Sabha (Art 80), from Literature, Science, Art and Social Services. Must know

                                                                                                                                              Memory aid 12 nominees from 'LSAS': Literature, Science, Art, Social service.

All-India Judicial Service.

                                                                                                                                              • The Council of States has exclusive powers in relation to which of the following?To recommend creation of a new All India Service
