                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements:Only 2

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha Chairman (Vice-President) is not a member, but the Deputy Chairman is; nominated MPs vote in Vice-President's election, not in President's.

                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse President: only elected MPs and MLAs vote; Vice-President: all MPs, elected and nominated.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • The Chairman of Council of States (Rajya Sabha) isVice-President is ex-officio Chairman

                                                                                                                                              Chairman of Rajya Sabha → Vice-President, ex officio (Arts 64, 89(1)); VP elected by members of both Houses of Parliament (Art 66(1)).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • With reference to ‘Vice-President of India’, which of the following statements is/are correct?Only l

                                                                                                                                              Vice-President → ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Arts 64, 89(1)) but not a member of either House; an MP elected VP loses his seat.

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • In which House is the presiding officer not a member of that House?Rajya-Sabha

                                                                                                                                              House presided over by a non-member → Rajya Sabha (Chairman = Vice-President, elected by members of both Houses). Must know

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • Present Chairman of Rajya Sabha is -—

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha Chairman = Vice-President (ex officio); at question time → Hamid Ansari; now → C.P. Radhakrishnan.

                                                                                                                                              Incorrect: S. Radhakrishnan not the only two-term Chairman; Hamid Ansari too (2007-2017); 1st Amendment (1951) predated Rajya Sabha; 8 UT members; 3 joint sittings.

                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Joint sittings 'D-B-P': Dowry (1962), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), Prevention of Terrorism (2002).

                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                              • In which year was Rajya Sabha constituted for the first time?1952

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha first constituted → 3 April 1952; maximum 250 (12 nominated), present 245; one-third retire every two years.

                                                                                                                                              Rajya Sabha member who can take part in Lok Sabha deliberations → a Minister (not an ordinary nominated member or the Deputy Chairman).

                                                                                                                                                    The Parliament (3) Conduct of Business and Legislative Procedure: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                    • The Parliament of India is the supreme legislative body.
                                                                                                                                                    • India has a parliamentary system of Government based on the Westminster model.
                                                                                                                                                    • The Right to amend the constitution is vested in the Parliament under Article 368.
                                                                                                                                                    • Maximum time gap between the two sessions of parliament is 6 months.
                                                                                                                                                    • Lok Sabha speaker, Deputy speaker, Secretary General, Rajya Sabha chairman, Deputy chairman etc. are called officials of parliament.
                                                                                                                                                    • There are usually three sessions in a year, i.e. Budget session, Monsoon session and Winter session.
                                                                                                                                                    • If any member of Parliament remains absent for 60 days from all meetings without informing to the respective house, then the House may declare his seat vacant.
                                                                                                                                                    • Article 105 of the Indian Constitution lays down the privileges and immunities of the members of Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                    • For making International treaties effective, the Parliament can make laws in the state list without the consent of the state.
                                                                                                                                                    • Speaker or chairman of the House can prohibit any member and allow any other member to speak. This is called Yielding the floor.
                                                                                                                                                    • When a member of parliament changes party allegiance, leaving one political party and joining another political party in the Parliament, it is called Crossing the floor.
                                                                                                                                                    • Zero Hour is a unique feature of the Parliamentary system of India. It can be a maximum of one hour, which is around 12 noon to 1:00 pm in Lok Sabha (its duration is not fixed in the Rules).
                                                                                                                                                    • A money bill can only be introduced in Lok Sabha and that too on the recommendation of the President of India. It cannot be introduced in Rajya Sabha.
                                                                                                                                                    • Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a money bill and must return it within 14 days, after which, Lok Sabha may accept or reject its recommendations. If the money bill is not returned within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                                                    • According to Article 108, the President summons both the Houses for ajoint sitting to resolve the deadlock between the two houses over the passage of a bill.
                                                                                                                                                    • According to Article 118(4) the speaker shall preside over a joint sitting of two houses of parliament.
                                                                                                                                                    • The Joint sitting of two Houses of Parliament is called up only for ordinary bills or non-money financial bills. The Joint sitting of two houses of Parliament is not called for Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills.
                                                                                                                                                    • Since 26 January, 1950 joint sitting of two Houses has been invoked only for three bills- the first one was in 1961 for the Dowry prohibition bill, second one was for the Banking service commission (repeal) Bill in 1978 and third one in 2002 for the prevention of terrorism Bill.
                                                                                                                                                    • Any ordinary bill can be introduced in any house of parliament.
                                                                                                                                                    • The Speaker has power to decide whether a bill is a money bill or not.
                                                                                                                                                    • To withdraw the funds from the Consolidated Fund of India, the government needs to pass appropriation bills.
                                                                                                                                                    • According to Article 116 of the Indian Constitution, when an appropriation bill is not passed and the government needs funds then Lok Sabha has the power to withdraw funds from the consolidated fund of India through a Vote on Account, for a fixed period of time.
                                                                                                                                                    • The Estimates Committee is the largest among the Financial committes of Parliament. It consists of 30 members (all from the Lok Sabha). There is no Rajya Sabha member in the Estimates Committee.
                                                                                                                                                    • The Secretariat of the Indian Parliament is free from the Government.
                                                                                                                                                    • Indian Parliament established control over administration through parliamentary committees.
                                                                                                                                                    • Consider the table given below: Parliament (Council of States) (House of the People)Not more than 20 representatives of Union Territories

                                                                                                                                                    Lok Sabha (Art 81): up to 530 State members + up to 20 UT members (the 'X') + 2 Anglo-Indians earlier (ended 25 January 2020); Rajya Sabha: 250 (238 + 12).

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The President of India addresses the Parliament under Article 87 of the Indian Constitutionboth Houses of Parliament assembled together.

                                                                                                                                                    Art 87 special address → President addresses both Houses of Parliament 'assembled together' (Constitution's words, not 'joint sitting').

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • With reference to the special address of the President of India, which of the following/statements is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                    Art 87(1): President addresses both Houses at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year; tells Parliament the causes of its summons.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which of the following are/is stated in the Constitution of India?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                    Art 59(1) → President is not a member of either House; Art 79 → Parliament = President + two Houses; both are written in the Constitution. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The Presidentis a part of the Parliament

                                                                                                                                                    President → integral part of Parliament (Parliament = President + Council of States + House of the People), though not a member and does not sit in it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 12 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Who/which of the following is not an integral part of Parliament?Vice-President

                                                                                                                                                    Not part of Parliament → Vice-President; Parliament = President + Council of States + House of the People (Art 79, Part V).

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Minimum how many times the Parliament has to meet in a year:Twice

                                                                                                                                                    Parliament must meet at least twice a year; gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months (Art 85(1)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The Officers of the Parliament include –All the four

                                                                                                                                                    Officers of Parliament → Lok Sabha Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Secretary-General of Lok Sabha and Chairman of Rajya Sabha. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The membership of a Parliament/Legislative Assembly’s membership may be terminated if he remains absent without informing to respective House for a term of -60 days

                                                                                                                                                    MP absent from all meetings for 60 days without permission → House may declare seat vacant (Art 101(4)); prorogation/adjournment over four days not counted.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • A seat of a M.P. can be declared vacant if he absents himself from the house for a continuous period ofTwo months

                                                                                                                                                    MP absent without permission from all meetings for sixty days (two months) → House may declare his seat vacant (Art 101(4)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • For the first time, a MP/MLA was disqualified from the membership on the ground of remaining absent from sixty consecutive meetings of the House without the permission. He was a member of –Council of States

                                                                                                                                                    First MP disqualified for 60 days' absence → Barjinder Singh Hamdard, Independent Rajya Sabha member from Punjab, in 2000.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • If any member of Parliament is elected for any State Legislature, within how many days he has to resign from the State Legislature, otherwise his membership of Parliament will become void?14 days

                                                                                                                                                    MP elected to a State Legislature must resign the State seat within 14 days, else his seat in Parliament becomes vacant (Art 101(2); 1950 rules).

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Privilege motion can be raised against a Minister when he –Withholds facts of a case or gives distorted versions of facts.

                                                                                                                                                    Privilege motion against a Minister → when he withholds facts of a case or gives a distorted version of facts.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which Article of the Constitution restrict a Member of Parliament to hold the office of profit?Article 102 (1) (a)

                                                                                                                                                    Office of profit bar on MPs → Article 102(1)(a): office under Union or State Government disqualifies, unless exempted by Parliament's law.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Consider the following statements:1 and 2 only

                                                                                                                                                    'Office of profit' is not defined in the Constitution or RP Act, 1951; Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts posts; amended five times.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Who will decide the Office of Profit?President and Governor; Union Parliament

                                                                                                                                                    Office of profit: declared by law by Parliament (Art 102(1)(a)) or State Legislature (Art 191(1)(a)); disqualification decided by President/Governor on Election Commission's advice (Arts 103, 192). Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following provisions deals with the privileges and immunities of the Members of Parlia ment under the Constitution of India?Article 105

                                                                                                                                                    Powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament, its members and committees → Article 105.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is not a collective privilege of the members of Parliament?Freedom from attendance as Witness.

                                                                                                                                                    Collective privileges: freedom of debates, excluding strangers, regulating own procedure, punishing breach; freedom from attending as witness → an individual privilege.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Under which Article of the Constitution the Courts have been prohibited from inquiring the proceedings of the Parliament?Article 122

                                                                                                                                                    Courts barred from inquiring into the proceedings of Parliament → Article 122.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Who among the following has the right to vote in the elections to both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?Elected members of the Lower House of the state Legislature

                                                                                                                                                    Elected MLAs (State Lower House) → vote in Lok Sabha elections (as citizens), Rajya Sabha elections and the Presidential election.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following statement is correct?—

                                                                                                                                                    Earlier, a Rajya Sabha candidate had to be a voter of that State; RP Act amended in 2003 removed this; Supreme Court upheld it in 2006.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following statements is correct?Only the Rajya Sabha and not the Lok Sabha can have nominated members; There is no Constitutional bar for nominated members to be appointed as a Union Minister

                                                                                                                                                    Nominated members: 12 in Rajya Sabha; Lok Sabha's 2 Anglo-Indian seats ended 25 January 2020, so only Rajya Sabha has them; nominated member may be Minister; no vote for President.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The Parliament of India has the 'Power to Legislate' for the following–1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                    Parliament can legislate for the Union of India, the Territory of India, and Indian subjects and their property anywhere in the world. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Union Parliament may legislate on any subject of State List –All of above

                                                                                                                                                    Parliament may legislate on State List: to implement international agreements (Art 253); by consent of two or more States (Art 252); Rajya Sabha 2/3 resolution (Art 249); during Emergency. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Memory aid 249-252-253 = Rajya resolution, States' request, Treaties.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The Parliament can make law for the whole or any part of India for implementing International Treaties –Without the consent of any state

                                                                                                                                                    Art 253 → Parliament can make law for whole or any part of India to implement international treaties/agreements, even on State List, without any State's consent. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Who can legislate on the subjects which are not included in any of the lists of subjects given in the Constitution?Parliament

                                                                                                                                                    Residuary subjects (not in State or Concurrent List) → Parliament has exclusive power to legislate (Art 248).

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Under which Article(s), the Speaker can allow any member of the House to speak in his/her mother tongue?Article 120 (1)

                                                                                                                                                    Art 120(1) → Parliament's business in Hindi or English; Speaker/Chairman may let a member who cannot express himself in either speak in his mother tongue.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • The Speaker can ask a member of the House to stop speaking and let another member speak. This phenomenon is known as:Yielding the floor

                                                                                                                                                    Yielding the floor → Speaker stops a member and lets another speak; Crossing the floor → changing party; Interpellation → asking Government to explain an act or policy.

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                    • Time of zero-hour in Parliament is:11 am to 12 noon; 12 noon to 1.00 pm

                                                                                                                                                    Zero Hour (Indian innovation): Lok Sabha 12 noon-1 pm, after Question Hour (11-12); Rajya Sabha 11 am-12 noon; maximum one hour. Must know

                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          The Parliament (3) Conduct of Business and Legislative Procedure · part 2 of 3

                                                                                                                                                          37 facts · 47 questions · 6 Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                          • Zero Hour in political jargon refers to-Question-answer session

                                                                                                                                                          Zero Hour → members raise important matters that cannot be delayed; the book equates it with a question-answer session.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • At which of the following stages general discussion on a Bill takes place in the Lok Sabha?During second reading

                                                                                                                                                          General discussion on a Bill → second reading (first stage of consideration), then clause-by-clause; first reading = introduction; third reading = passing.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • When a bill is referred to a joint sitting of both the Houses of the Parliament, it has to be passed by –A simple majority of members present and voting

                                                                                                                                                          Bill at a joint sitting (Art 108(4)) → passed by a simple majority of total members of both Houses present and voting.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • What will be happened if President summons for the joint session of Parliament and in the meantime Lok Sabha dissolved?Joint session will be held in scheduled time

                                                                                                                                                          If Lok Sabha is dissolved after President notifies a joint sitting, the joint sitting is still held as scheduled (bill does not lapse); a lapsed bill cannot go to one.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the joint sitting of Parliament, which statement/s is/are correct?Only (2)

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting → Article 108 (not 109, which covers Money Bills); presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the Joint Sitting of Parliament’, which of the following statements is/are correct?Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting → Article 108, not 109 (Money Bill procedure); no joint sitting for a Constitution Amendment Bill, which each House passes by special majority (Art 368).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Who among the following presides over a joint sitting of two houses of the Parliament?Speaker of the Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting of the two Houses → presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Who presides over the joint session of both the Houses of the Parliament?Speaker

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting presided by Lok Sabha Speaker (Art 118(4)); if absent → Deputy Speaker → Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha → person chosen by members present. Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Not the President or Vice-President; the Rajya Sabha Chairman never presides over a joint sitting.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 10 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting (Art 108): 1st in 1961 (Dowry Prohibition Bill); 2nd in 1978 (Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill, 1977); 3rd in March 2002 (POTA). Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid D-B-P order: Dowry, Banking, POTA.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Joint Session of both the Houses of Parliament is concernedonly 4

                                                                                                                                                          Joint session (Art 108) → only to pass a Bill on which the two Houses disagree; not for President/VP elections or Constitution amendment; first on Dowry Bill. Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following statements is/are true in reference to the joint sitting of Parliament for passage of bill?None of these

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting: only ordinary bills (not Money or Constitution Amendment bills); Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman can preside if Speaker and Deputy Speaker absent; quorum 1/10, not 1/6.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • A deadlock between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha calls for a joint sitting of the Parliament during the passage ofOnly 1

                                                                                                                                                          Joint sitting (Art 108) → only for ordinary legislation; Money Bill needs none (Rajya Sabha must return it in 14 days); Constitution Amendment passed by each House (Art 368). Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Joint sitting is never for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • A legislative bill may be introduced in which House of Parliament?Either House of Parliament

                                                                                                                                                          An ordinary legislative Bill → can be introduced in either House of Parliament; a Money Bill only in Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                          Lapse on Lok Sabha dissolution (Art 107(5)): bill pending in LS, and LS-passed bill pending in RS; NOT a bill notified for joint sitting (108(5)) or RS bill unpassed by LS (107(4)).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following statements is/are correct?2 only

                                                                                                                                                          Bills do not lapse on prorogation (Art 107(3)); a bill pending in Rajya Sabha not yet passed by Lok Sabha does not lapse on Lok Sabha's dissolution (Art 107(4)).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the Constitutional Provision lays down that taxes can neither be levied nor collected without the authority of law?Article 265

                                                                                                                                                          No tax levied or collected except by authority of law → Article 265; Art 266 → Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts; Art 300 → suits; Art 368 → amendment.

                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid 265 = 'No taxation without law'.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Who has the right to issue money from the Consolidated Fund of India?None of the above

                                                                                                                                                          No one (CAG, Finance Minister or any Minister) can issue money from Consolidated Fund of India (Art 266) without Parliament's authorisation by appropriation (Art 114).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • All revenues received by the Union Government by way of taxes and other receipts for the conduct of Government business are credited to theConsolidated Fund of India

                                                                                                                                                          All Union Government revenues, taxes and other receipts → credited to the Consolidated Fund of India (Art 266).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • The authorization for the withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India must come from –The Parliament of India

                                                                                                                                                          Withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India → must be authorised by Parliament (Art 114).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is not a mandatory expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?Salary and Pension of the members of the Election Commission of India.

                                                                                                                                                          Charged on Consolidated Fund: President's emoluments; RS Chairman/Deputy and LS Speaker/Deputy salaries; debt charges; SC judges; HC judges' pensions; CAG. Not listed: Election Commission members' salary.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following expenditures is not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?Salary and allowances of the Vice-President of India

                                                                                                                                                          Not charged on Consolidated Fund → Vice-President's salary as VP (Art 112); he is paid as Rajya Sabha Chairman, whose salary is charged.

                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Chairman of Rajya Sabha's salary is charged; there is no separate charged salary for the Vice-President.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following expenditure is not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?Salary and allowances of the Prime Minister of India.

                                                                                                                                                          Not charged → Prime Minister's salary; charged (Art 112(3)): President, CJI, HC judges' pensions, CAG, RS Chairman/Deputy, LS Speaker/Deputy; charged items discussed, not voted.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related to Contingency Fund?Article 267

                                                                                                                                                          Contingency Fund of India → Article 267; placed at President's disposal for advances to meet unforeseen expenditure.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • How can the President spend from Contingency Fund?Before Authorisation of Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                          Contingency Fund (Art 267(1)) → President can advance money for unforeseen expenditure before Parliament's authorisation; no prior approval needed.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                          Union Budget prepared by Ministry of Finance (not Department of Revenue); Consolidated Fund withdrawal needs Parliament's authorisation (Art 114(3)); Public Account disbursements do not.

                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Public Account is controlled by the Executive; no Parliament vote needed.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is responsible for preparation and presentation of union budget in the Parliament?Department of Economic Affairs

                                                                                                                                                          Preparation and presentation of the Union Budget → Department of Economic Affairs (not Department of Revenue or Expenditure).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to Union Budget, consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                          Annual Financial Statement (Art 112(1)) laid by Finance Minister on behalf of the President, not PM; no demand for grant except on President's recommendation (Art 113(3)).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 0 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • How many (number) 'Demands for Grants' are put before the Parliament as a part of the Annual Budget in pursuance to Article 113 of the Constitution?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                          Demands for Grants (Art 113) → presented to Lok Sabha, usually one per ministry; budget 2025-26 had 102, 2021-22 had 101 → 'none of the above'.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Money Bill has been defined by the Constitution under Article:110

                                                                                                                                                          Article 110 → definition of Money Bill; Art 109 → special procedure for Money Bills; Art 111 → assent to Bills. Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse 109 (procedure) with 110 (definition).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • A Bill is deemed to be a Money Bill (as per Article 110), ifit contains provisions dealing with matters relating to:All the above

                                                                                                                                                          Money Bill (Art 110): only matters of tax, Government borrowing, custody of Consolidated/Contingency Funds, appropriation, charged expenditure, receipts and audit of Union/State accounts.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following subject is not included in the provisions of the Money Bills?Provision for imposition of fines or penalties

                                                                                                                                                          NOT a Money Bill matter → imposition of fines or penalties; Money Bill covers taxes, borrowings, custody of Consolidated and Contingency Funds (Art 110).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is not correct?v vi

                                                                                                                                                          Wrong: 'Rajya Sabha can detain Finance Bill 14 days' (that is Money Bill) and 'President cannot refuse Finance Bill' (he can return it); Rajya Sabha can amend Finance Bill.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following statements about a Money Bill is not correct?A Money Bill can be tabled in either House of Parliament

                                                                                                                                                          Not correct: 'Money Bill in either House' → only Lok Sabha; Speaker decides if a bill is a Money Bill; Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to Finance Bill and Money Bill in the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:Only two

                                                                                                                                                          Rajya Sabha can amend or reject a Financial Bill (I), but only recommend on a Money Bill within 14 days; joint sitting possible (not necessary) for Financial Bills, never for Money Bills.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Who among the following decides whether a particular Bill is a Money Bill?Speaker of Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                                          Whether a Bill is a Money Bill → decided by the Lok Sabha Speaker; his decision is final (Art 110(3)).

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Who certifies the money bill?Speaker

                                                                                                                                                          Money Bill certified by Lok Sabha Speaker; his decision is final, not questioned by courts, Parliament or President; endorsed when sent to Rajya Sabha and to President. Must know

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following statements is correct regarding submission of Money bill?It is presented in Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                          Money Bill → presented only in Lok Sabha (Art 109(1)); UPPSC's Hindi paper said 'Finance Bill' but meant Money Bill.

                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
