Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                • The Finance Bill of Indian Government is presented in -Lower House

                                                                                                                                                                Finance Bill (Art 117(1)) → introduced only in the Lower House (Lok Sabha), on the President's recommendation; never in Council of States.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following statements are correct in respect of a Money Bill in the Parliament?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                Money Bill: special procedure Art 109; not introduced in Rajya Sabha; RS may only recommend within fourteen days; Lok Sabha may accept or reject them; deemed passed if not returned.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following statements is correct?A Money Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                Money Bill → introduced only in Lok Sabha; Speaker's decision final; no joint session; Rajya Sabha can hold it at most 14 days (Art 109(2)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Of the following statements, which one is not correct?Money Bill is introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                Not correct: 'Money Bill introduced in Rajya Sabha' → only in Lok Sabha (Art 109(1)); Rajya Sabha returns it, with or without recommendations, within 14 days. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Rajya Sabha can delay the Finance Bill sent for its consideration by Lok Sabha for a maximum period of-Fourteen days

                                                                                                                                                                Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill (treated here as 'Finance Bill') for at most fourteen days; an ordinary bill has no time limit. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following procedures will enable the adoption of a Money Bill that was once passed by the Lok Sabha but was amended by the Rajya Sabha?It will be deemed to have been passed if the Lok Sabha passes it again either by accepting or rejecting the amendments.

                                                                                                                                                                Money Bill amended by Rajya Sabha → deemed passed once Lok Sabha passes it again, accepting or rejecting the changes (Art 109); no joint session, no special majority.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • A Bill which merely involves expenditure and does not include any of the matters specified in Article 110 can be:Initiated in either House of Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                Bill merely involving expenditure from Consolidated Fund (Financial Bill, Art 117(3)) → can be introduced in either House; President's recommendation needed for its consideration.

                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse Financial Bill under Art 117(1) (Art 110 matters) is Lok Sabha-only; 117(3) expenditure bill can start in either House.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the Annual Financial Statement?Article 112

                                                                                                                                                                Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) → Article 112; financial year 1 April to 31 March; budget passes through six stages in Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is necessary to be laid before the Parliament?Article 112

                                                                                                                                                                Art 112 → President causes the Annual Financial Statement (Budget), estimated receipts and expenditure, to be laid before both Houses each financial year.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following terms does not appear in the Constitution of India?Budget

                                                                                                                                                                'Budget' does not appear in the Constitution; it uses 'Annual Financial Statement' (Art 112); Appropriation Bill and Consolidated Fund of India do appear.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following statements is not correct with regard to control of Parliament on a budget?Parliament has the power to move on the charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund.

                                                                                                                                                                Not correct: 'Parliament votes on charged expenditure' → charged expenditure on Consolidated Fund (Art 112(3)) is only discussed, never voted.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following are the methods of Parliamentary control over public finance in India?1, 2, 3 and 5

                                                                                                                                                                Parliamentary control over finance: Annual Financial Statement, Appropriation Bill before withdrawal (Art 114), supplementary grants and vote on account (Arts 115, 116), Finance Bill; no Budget Office review.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • If the annual Union Budget is not passed by the Lok Sabha…The Prime Minister submits the resignation of Council of Ministers

                                                                                                                                                                If Lok Sabha does not pass the Union Budget → PM submits resignation of the Council of Ministers (government has lost its majority).

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                Private member's Bill → by any MP other than a Minister (not only nominated MPs); about a dozen passed since independence, so not a recent first.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Economic Survey is presented in Parliament every yearBefore presentation of the Budget for the coming year

                                                                                                                                                                Economic Survey → presented in Parliament every year before the Budget; reviews progress and fiscal details of economic sectors for the current year.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • ‘Votes on Account’ permits Union Government to:Withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund of India for specific period

                                                                                                                                                                Vote on Account (Art 116) → lets Union Government withdraw money from Consolidated Fund for a specific period when Appropriation Bill is not yet passed.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Vote on Account is meant forAppropriating funds pending passing of budget

                                                                                                                                                                Vote on Account (Art 116(1)(a)) → funds to run the administration pending passage of the full budget, e.g. near elections or before new financial year. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • What is the difference between ‘Vote-on-Account’ and ‘interim budget’?2 only

                                                                                                                                                                Vote on Account covers only expenditure; Interim Budget covers both receipts and expenditure; the 'stable vs caretaker government' distinction is false.

                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse Don't treat Vote on Account and Interim Budget as same: only Interim Budget shows receipts.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Estimates of expenditure are submitted to the Parliament of India in the form of –Demands for Grants

                                                                                                                                                                Estimates of expenditure → submitted to Lok Sabha as Demands for Grants (Art 113(2)); Lok Sabha may assent, refuse or reduce them.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • The stages in the normal financial legislation include –1, 2, 3 and 5

                                                                                                                                                                Normal financial legislation: Budget presentation → discussion → Appropriation Bill → Finance Bill; Vote on Account, vote of credit, exceptional grants (Art 116) are outside it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Prior sanction of the President of India is required before introducing a Bill in the Parliament on –All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                President's prior sanction needed before Bills on: forming a new State, altering State boundaries, taxation in which States are interested, and Money Bills.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • What is true about Censure Motion?It is different from the No-confidence motion; Permission of the House is not essential to present it

                                                                                                                                                                Censure Motion differs from No-Confidence Motion: reasons must be stated; no separate leave of the House needed.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following proposals is related to the Union Budget?Cut motion

                                                                                                                                                                Cut motion → linked to Union Budget (opposes/reduces a demand for grant); types: token, policy, frugality cut; Censure, Calling Attention, Adjournment are non-budget motions.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • What is the object of “cut motion” in Parliament?To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the budget proposals

                                                                                                                                                                Cut motion → proposal to reduce a demand for grant in the budget; types: Disapproval of Policy, Economy and Token cut.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • What is the object of "Cut Motion"?To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the Budget proposals

                                                                                                                                                                Cut Motion → motion to reduce the amount of a demand for grants; aims to draw the House's attention to the matter specified.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following is not correctly matched?Vote on Parliamentary sanction of all Account budgetary demands for grants in a financial year

                                                                                                                                                                Wrong pair: Vote on Account (Art 116) only draws money till budget passes, not yearly sanction; Policy cut → Re one; Economy cut → set amount; Token cut → Rs one hundred.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • The Provision for the Calling Attention Notices has restricted the scope of which of the following?Adjournment Motion

                                                                                                                                                                Calling Attention (Indian innovation) → draws a Minister's attention to an urgent public matter; it has restricted the scope of the Adjournment Motion (no censure element).

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                Parliament controls Council of Ministers through Adjournment Motion, Question Hour and Supplementary Questions; starred → oral with supplementaries; unstarred → no supplementaries.

                                                                                                                                                                • What is correct about the starred question?(i) (iii)

                                                                                                                                                                Starred question (marked *) → oral answer, supplementaries allowed, max 20 listed a day; unstarred → not answered orally, no supplementaries.

                                                                                                                                                                Memory aid Star = Spoken answer.

                                                                                                                                                                • In the Parliament of India, the purpose of an adjournment motion is –To allow a discussion on a definite matter of urgent public importance

                                                                                                                                                                Adjournment motion → allows discussion on a definite matter of urgent public importance.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Statement(A): N.D.A. Government does not like discussion under Rule 184 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha.(A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                Rule 184 (Lok Sabha) → discussion followed by voting; government avoids it as a lost vote can threaten it. A and R true, R explains A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                • Under Rule 377 of Rules and Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the maximum number of matters that can be raised by Lok Sabha members in one day are—

                                                                                                                                                                Rule 377 → matters not raisable under other rules; notice to Secretary-General; Speaker's consent needed; daily limit raised from 20 to 30 in 2015.

                                                                                                                                                                • What is meaning of Guillotine in Parliamentary Procedure?To stop the debate on the bill

                                                                                                                                                                Guillotine → a closure motion: undiscussed clauses are put to vote with discussed ones when time is over, cutting short debate on the bill.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • With reference to Indian Polity, which one of the following statements is correct?President can make ordinance only when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session

                                                                                                                                                                President can issue ordinance (Art 123) except when both Houses are in session; NDC is presided by the PM, so 'FM + CMs' is wrong.

                                                                                                                                                                • Examine the following statements and choose the correct answer from the given options1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                Right to Property → legal right (Art 300-A) by 44th Amendment, 1978; Rajya Sabha can hold a non-Money Finance Bill; 42nd Amendment, 1976 added Socialist and Secular, not Democratic.

                                                                                                                                                                • The Secretariat of Parliament of India is –Independent of the Government

                                                                                                                                                                Each House of Parliament has a separate secretariat independent of the Government (Art 98); idea mooted in January 1926 by Vithalbhai J. Patel.

                                                                                                                                                                • With reference to the post’s in Secretariate of the Parliament, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Both (1) and (2)

                                                                                                                                                                Art 98(1): separate secretariat staff for each House, but common posts allowed; Art 98(2): Parliament may by law regulate their recruitment and service conditions.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Sovereignty of Indian Parliament is restricted by –Judicial review

                                                                                                                                                                Sovereignty of Indian Parliament → restricted by judicial review; its laws cannot violate the Basic Structure of the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • The Golden Jubilee of Indian Parliament was celebrated on –13-05-2002

                                                                                                                                                                Golden Jubilee of Indian Parliament → 13 May 2002 (Parliament constituted 13 May 1952), marking 50 years.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • Which architect has designed the new building of the Indian Parliament?Bimal Patel

                                                                                                                                                                New Parliament building → designed by Bimal Patel; inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on 28 May 2023; old building by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker.

                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                • In reference to Indian Parliamentary Group, which of the following statements is/are true?—

                                                                                                                                                                Indian Parliamentary Group → autonomous body (1949, motion of 16 August 1948); open to MPs and ex-MPs; Lok Sabha Speaker is ex-officio President; IPU national group.

                                                                                                                                                                Nationalist elected Speaker of Central Legislative Assembly in 1925 → Vithalbhai Patel, first to hold it (24 August 1925 to 28 April 1930).

                                                                                                                                                                      Parliamentary Committees: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                      • The Parliament is assisted by a number of Committees in the discharge of its duties. These committees are appointed or elected by Houses of the Parliament or nominated by the Speaker / Chairman. They perform their work under the direction of the Speaker / Chairman and submit their report to the House, or to the Speaker / Chairman as applicable.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Mainly the parliamentary committees are of two kinds – Standing committees and Ad-hoc committees.
                                                                                                                                                                      • The Standing committees are permanent (constituted every year or periodically) and work on a continuous basis while the Ad-hoc committees are temporary and cease to exist on completion of the task assigned to them.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Standing Committees are-
                                                                                                                                                                      (i)Financial Committees
                                                                                                                                                                      (ii)Department-related Standing Committees. (Total 24)
                                                                                                                                                                      (iii)Committee of Enquiry
                                                                                                                                                                      (iv)Committees to Scrutinise and Control
                                                                                                                                                                      (v)Committees relating to the day-to-day business of the

                                                                                                                                                                      House.

                                                                                                                                                                      (vi) Housekeeping Committees or Service Committees.

                                                                                                                                                                      • Financial committee includes the Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee and Public Undertakings Committee.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Most of the standing committees, leaving some committees, consist of members from Lok Sabha and Rajya sabha in the ratio of 2:1.
                                                                                                                                                                      • The Public Accounts committee consist of 22 members (15 from Lok sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha). It examines various expenditure reports and accounts under the purview of the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                      • The Estimates Committee consists of 30 members elected every year by the Lok Sabha from among its members. All of its members are from Lok sabha.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Its function is to suggest alternative policies in order to bring about efficiency and economy in administration and to report improvements in organizations, efficiency or administrative reform, consistent with the policy underlying the estimates, may be effected.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Public Undertakings Committee consists of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha). It analyses the accounts and workings of the state-owned PSU firms. It also checks the disinvestment policies of the various PSUs. Committee to Inquire includes the committee on petitions, the committee on privileges and the ethics committee.
                                                                                                                                                                      • The Petition committee in Lok Sabha consists of15 members, while the petition committee in Rajya Sabha consists of 10 members.
                                                                                                                                                                      • Public Accounts Committee submits its report to the Lok Sabha Speaker. (Ordinarily Presents reports to the House; only when the House is not in session, it may present the report to the Speaker and later present it to the House). Generally, a member from the opposition in Lok Sabha is appointed as the chairperson of this committee by the speaker of Lok Sabha. There are a total of 24 Departmentally Standing Committees (DRSCs). Out of 24, 8 under Rajya Sabha and 16 under Lok Sabha.
                                                                                                                                                                      • In what way does the Indian Parliament exercise control over the administration?Through Parliamentary Committees

                                                                                                                                                                      Parliament controls the administration through Parliamentary Committees (Public Accounts, Estimates, Standing Committees).

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is/are a Financial Committee of Parliament in India?All 1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                      Financial Committees of Parliament → Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings.

                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid Financial trio 'PEP': Public Accounts, Estimates, Public Undertakings.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is the largest Committee of the Parliament?The Committee on Estimates

                                                                                                                                                                      Largest Parliamentary Committee → Estimates Committee (30 members, all Lok Sabha, first 1950, one-year term); PAC 22 (15 + 7); Public Undertakings 22; Petitions 15. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is not a tool of Parliamentary control over Public expenditures?Comptroller and Auditor General of India

                                                                                                                                                                      Not a Parliamentary tool → CAG (independent constitutional authority, Art 148); PAC, Estimates Committee and Public Undertakings Committee are Parliament's tools.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The members of Standing Committee of Parliament are taken from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in which ratio?Two and one respectively.

                                                                                                                                                                      Parliament's joint Standing Committees → Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha members roughly in ratio 2:1.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC Chairman → appointed by Lok Sabha Speaker; PAC = 22 MPs (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha), no outside experts; assisted by CAG.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • How many members are elected from the Lok Sabha for Public Account Committee?15

                                                                                                                                                                      Public Accounts Committee → formed every year, not more than 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha; scrutinises the CAG's report. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid PAC = 15 + 7 = 22.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • What is the main function of Public Accounts Committee?To examine CAG Annual Reports

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC → examines CAG's annual audit reports; financial check on the executive; first set up 1921 under Government of India Act, 1919; 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS).

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                      Estimates Committee (30) all from Lok Sabha; PAC and Public Undertakings (22 = 15 LS + 7 RS); Parliamentary Affairs Ministry under Cabinet Committee; its Minister nominates MPs to government bodies.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The main function of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament is-To examine the financial account of the government and report of Comptroller and Auditor General.

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC's main function → examine Government's accounts and CAG's report on Union accounts; exposes misuse of public expenditure.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • With reference to Public Accounts Committee, which of the following statements is / are correct?Only 1

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC → reports to Speaker, presented in Lok Sabha (copy laid in Rajya Sabha); max 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha + up to 7 from Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Don't flip the split: 15 members come from Lok Sabha, only 7 from Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Public Accounts Committee present its report to-Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC → formed every year, not more than 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha); examines CAG audit report and reports to Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The Public Accounts Committee submits its reports to-The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC submits its report to the Speaker of Lok Sabha → presented in Lok Sabha; members: 15 (Lok Sabha) + 07 (Rajya Sabha) = 22. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid PAC formula 15 + 07 = 22; the bigger share and the report both go to Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements The Parliamentary Committee on Public Accounts2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                      PAC → examines CAG report and scrutinises appropriation and finance accounts of Government; has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS), not '25 Lok Sabha members'.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Who nominates the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of Indian Parliament?The Speaker of Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                                                      Chairman of PAC → appointed by Speaker of Lok Sabha from among its members; till 1966-67 from ruling party, since 1967-68 an opposition member. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer by using the code given below the lists:3 4 1 2

                                                                                                                                                                      Public Accounts Committee → Financial Committee; Committee on Petitions → Functional Committee; Joint Committee on Stock Market Scam → Ad hoc; Departmental Committees → Standing.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Members of the Rajya Sabha are not associated with –Only 2

                                                                                                                                                                      Estimates Committee (first 1950) → 30 members, all from Lok Sabha, no Rajya Sabha member; PAC and Public Undertakings Committee → 22 (15 LS + 7 RS). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid Estimates = Exclusively Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Estimates Committee (30, Lok Sabha only) with PAC (22, both Houses).

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following are Financial Committees of Indian Parliament (A) Estimates Committee (B) Public Accounts Committee (C) Committee on Public Undertakings (D) Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowance for Members of Parliament Select the correct answer using code given below: Codes:(A), (B) and (C)

                                                                                                                                                                      Financial Committees (3) → Estimates, Public Accounts, Public Undertakings; Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs is a Housekeeping Committee.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Salaries and Allowances committee deals with money but is Housekeeping, not Financial.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is the Financial Committees of Parliament in India?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                      Three Financial Committees of Parliament → Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings.

                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid PEP: Public Accounts, Estimates, Public Undertakings.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The audit report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is examined byPublic Undertaking Committee; Public Accounts Committee

                                                                                                                                                                      CAG audit report → examined by Public Accounts Committee; Committee on Public Undertakings also examines CAG reports, so book accepts (a) and (c).

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not a Standing Committee of Parliament?—

                                                                                                                                                                      Parliamentary committees → Standing and Ad hoc; three main Standing Committees: Estimates, Public Accounts, Public Undertakings; 17 Department-related Standing Committees came in 1993.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following statements about the Ethics Committee in the Lok Sabha are correct?1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                      Lok Sabha Ethics Committee → initially ad hoc; cannot take up sub-judice matters; complaints not limited to Lok Sabha members. First Ethics Committee: Rajya Sabha, 1997.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • On which of the following, a Parliamentary Committee has not been set up?Welfare of Minorities

                                                                                                                                                                      Parliamentary Committees exist on Public Undertakings, Government Assurances (tracks ministers' promises) and Estimates; none on Welfare of Minorities.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following Committees does not come under the jurisdiction of Lok Sabha?Committee on Health and Family Welfare

                                                                                                                                                                      Department-related Standing Committees: Social Justice & Empowerment, Urban Development, Labour → under Lok Sabha; Health and Family Welfare → under Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The Consultative Committee of Members of Parliament for Railway Zones is constituted by which of the following?Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs

                                                                                                                                                                      Consultative Committees of MPs for Railway Zones → constituted by Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; MPs of the respective zones are members.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Not the Ministry of Railways, even though the committees are for railway zones.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which pair is incorrect regarding the appointment of Chairpersons of Parliamentary committees constituted by the Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha for the year 2024-25?Estimates Committee – Baijayant Panda

                                                                                                                                                                      18th Lok Sabha committees 2024-25 (Speaker Om Birla): PAC → K.C. Venugopal; Estimates → Sanjay Jaiswal; Public Undertakings → Baijayant Panda (so 'Estimates – Panda' is wrong).

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The Joint Parliamentary Committee set up for probing the 2G spectrum issue, consists of20 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha

                                                                                                                                                                      2G spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee (2011) → 30 MPs: 20 from Lok Sabha + 10 from Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • The Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the 2G Scam is headed byP.C.Chacko

                                                                                                                                                                      2G Scam Joint Parliamentary Committee → headed by P.C. Chacko; report given to Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?Committee on Subordinate Legislation

                                                                                                                                                                      Committee on Subordinate Legislation → checks whether Executive properly uses delegated power to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse With Committee on Government Assurances, which checks ministers' promises made on the floor of the House.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is a Parliamentary Committee relating to delegation of power to make rules and regulations to the Executive?Committee on Subordinate Legislation

                                                                                                                                                                      Committee on Subordinate Legislation → delegated rule-making by Executive; exists in both Houses, 15 members each, nominated by Speaker/Chairman; ministers cannot be members.

                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse The official name is 'Subordinate' Legislation, not 'Delegated', 'Executive' or 'Administrative' Legislation.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                      • In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, electricity, etc.?1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                      Independent regulators (telecom, insurance, electricity) → reviewed by Parliament's ad hoc committees and Department-related Standing Committees (24); not Finance Commission, FSLRC or NITI Aayog.

                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
