                                                                                                                                                                            Parliamentary Act

                                                                                                                                                                            88 facts · 89 questions · 4 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                            Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                            Parliamentary Act: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                            • The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was introduced in 1954 and came into force on 1 June, 1955 (Repealed w.e.f. 5 August, 2011).
                                                                                                                                                                            • All the punishable offences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are cognizable and triable summarily.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The trials of crime under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are done by a First Class Judicial Magistrate and in the case of Metropolis, it is done by Metropolitan Magistrate.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 was brought into force on 26 October, 2006.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The Criminal Tribes Act was first enacted in 1871.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been applicable in India since 30 January 1990. To implement the objectives of The Scheduled Castes and The Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the central government has the power to make rules by notification in the Official Gazette.
                                                                                                                                                                            • Section 18 of The Scheduled Castes and The Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 prohibits anticipatory bail to the accused.
                                                                                                                                                                            • According to Rule 7(1) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, an offence committed under this Act shall be investigated by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
                                                                                                                                                                            • Under section 14 of this Act, the State Government, for the purpose of providing speedy trial, is empowered to constitute a court of session, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, to be a special court for each district to try the offence under the SC & ST Act.
                                                                                                                                                                            • Hindu Marriage Act, Hindu Succession Act and The Commission of SATI (Prevention) Act were enforced in 1955, 1956 and 1988, respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                            • Right to Information came fully into force on 12 October 2005. The Right to Information is a legal right. According to the Supreme Court, it is also a fundamental right. The use of the Right to Information Act is to obtain Information from the public authority.
                                                                                                                                                                            • Namit sharma V/s Union of India case is related to the Right to Information Act 2005. The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan is an Indian social movement and grassroots organization best known for its demand for the Right to Information Act. The Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 removed the previous provision i.e., the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) and Information Commissioner (IC) at the Central and State levels will hold office for a term of five years and substituted it by term as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October, 2010, under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
                                                                                                                                                                            • The provision of the Panchayats (extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 or PESA is a law enacted by the Parliament of India ensuring self-governance through traditional gram sabhas for people living in the Scheduled Areas of India.
                                                                                                                                                                            • In which year was Prevention of Food Adulteration Act first enacted?1954

                                                                                                                                                                            Prevention of Food Adulteration Act → enacted 1954; came into effect 1 June 1955.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • All offences punishable under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are:Cognizable and Summarily Triable

                                                                                                                                                                            Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955, Section 15 → all offences are cognizable and summarily triable.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Offences are tried under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 by the Courts ofJudicial Magistrate First Class

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955 offences → tried by Judicial Magistrate First Class (special courts); in UP, Chief Judicial Magistrate/Judicial Magistrate courts are designated Special Courts.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • All the punishable offences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are:Cognizable and Triable Summarily; Cognizable and Non-Compoundable

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955 → all offences are cognizable, triable summarily and non-compoundable.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, All offences are –Cognizable; Punishment with imprisonment and fine both

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955 → Section 15(1): all offences cognizable; Section 10A(1): State Government can impose collective fine; punishment is imprisonment and fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • If any person refuses admission to any person to any hospital, dispensary or educational institution on the ground of untouchability, then under which section of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 he shall be punishable?Section - 5

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, Section 5 → refusing admission to hospital, dispensary or educational institution on ground of untouchability; jail one to six months plus fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which one of the following Sections of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 has ‘power of State Government to impose collective fine’ been provided?Section 10 A

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, Section 10A → power of State Government to impose collective fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Protection of Civil Rights Act extends to:The whole of India

                                                                                                                                                                            Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 → Section 1(2): extends to the whole of India.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 extends to?Whole of India

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955 → punishes preaching and practice of untouchability and enforcing any disability from it; extends to whole of India (Section 1(2)).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which of the following Sections of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 has ‘offences by companies’ been provided?Section 14

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955: Section 14 → offences by companies; Section 10 → abetment (public servant neglecting investigation); Section 12 → presumption by courts.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Who is held responsible for the offences committed by Companies, under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, offence by a company → person in charge of its affairs (Director, Manager or Secretary) deemed guilty and punished.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • When the court, under section 12 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, shall presume that the offence is committed on the ground of "untouchability"?When it relates to member of Scheduled Castes only

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, Section 12 → court presumes act was on ground of untouchability when victim is a member of a Scheduled Caste.

                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Presumption covers Scheduled Castes only, not Scheduled Tribes.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Untouchability will not constitute an offence when -The accused and complainant victim belong to the same social group

                                                                                                                                                                            Untouchability is not an offence when the accused and the victim belong to the same social group.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • A court can presume that any act constituting offence was committed on the ground of untouchabilliy - if such offence is committed in relation to -a member of Scheduled Castes

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, Section 12 → court can presume 'untouchability' motive when offence is against a member of the Scheduled Castes (unless contrary proved).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which one of the following Sections of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 has 'protection of action taken in good faith' been provided?Section 14 A

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Act 1955, Section 14A → protection of action taken in good faith (no suit against Central or State Government).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following Central Ministries are responsible for the implementation of Protection of Civil Right Rules, 1977?1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                            PCR Rules 1977 at Centre → Ministry of Home Affairs, Social Justice & Empowerment and Tribal Affairs (not Minority Affairs); main responsibility with States/UTs.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?73rd Constitutional Amendment - Reservation of seats for women in the election of local bodies in urban areas

                                                                                                                                                                            Women's reservation in urban local bodies → 74th Amendment, not 73rd. Hindu Marriage Act 1955; Hindu Succession Act 1956; Sati (Prevention) Act 1987.

                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse 73rd with 74th Amendment: urban local bodies come under the 74th.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below.2 1 4 3

                                                                                                                                                                            Indian High Court Act → 1861; Indian Divorce Act → 1869; Royal Title Act → 1876; Indian Arms Act → 1878.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act came into force on –26th October, 2006

                                                                                                                                                                            Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 → came into force on 26 October 2006.

                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Act year 2005, but in force from 2006.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is not a Social Act?MISA Act

                                                                                                                                                                            MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act, 1971; repealed 1977) → security law, not a social Act; Anti-Dowry, PCR, Immoral Traffic Acts are social Acts.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • When was the Criminal Tribes Act enacted for the first time?1871

                                                                                                                                                                            Criminal Tribes Act → first enacted 1871 by the British; first in northern India, later extended to Bengal.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 came into force on:30th January, 1990

                                                                                                                                                                            SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → President's assent 11 September 1989; came into force 30 January 1990. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Act year is 1989, but it came into force in 1990.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • How many Sections are there under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?23

                                                                                                                                                                            SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → has 23 Sections.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Who has/had the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Scheduled Castes and theThe Central Government

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 23(1) → Central Government makes rules by notification in the Official Gazette.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which Section of the Scheduled Castes and is 'economic boycott' defined?Section 2 (b c)

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → 'economic boycott' defined in Section 2(bc).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Offence committed by any public servant under Section provides for minimum punishment ofOne year

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989 → public servant committing an offence under Section 3 → minimum one year imprisonment.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)Act, 1989, in which section there is a provision for the arrangement of a special court?14

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989: Section 14 → Special Court and Exclusive Special Court for speedy trial; Section 15 → Special Public Prosecutor.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The State Government can specify a Court of Session to be a Special Court to try the offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 with the concurrence of the–Chief Justice of High Court

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, Section 14 → State Government, with concurrence of Chief Justice of High Court, notifies a Court of Session as Special Court for each district.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • A Court of Session specified as Special Court to try the offences under the Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for the purpose of providing –Speedy trial

                                                                                                                                                                            Court of Session made Special Court under SC/ST Atrocities Act (Section 14) → purpose: speedy trial.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • An appeal under Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 shall lie from any judgement, sentence or order to the High Court.Both on facts and law

                                                                                                                                                                            Appeal under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → lies to the High Court on both facts and law.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is a special provision for the advancement of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes which is based on which one of the following doctrines?Doctrine of Protective discrimination

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → based on Doctrine of Protective Discrimination; implements the system under Article 15(4).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Who is empowered for imposition and realization of a collective fine under SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?State Government

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 16 → State Government imposes and realises collective fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Not the District Magistrate or Special Court; the power is with the State Government.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • In a prosecution for an offence under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the court can presume which of the following?All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 8 → court may presume abetment, common intention and common object.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 provides for application of certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code?Section 6

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 6 → applies certain Indian Penal Code provisions (e.g. Sections 34, 149); IPC now replaced by Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • In how many days will the investigation officer submit his report for the offences committed under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?—

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Rules, 1995 → investigating officer to finish investigation within thirty days and report to Superintendent of Police; rule changed by Amendment Rules, 2016.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, which of the following is barred?Anticipatory Bail

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → anticipatory bail is barred.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 is anticipatory bail prohibited?Section 18

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 18 → anticipatory bail (Section 438) does not apply to arrests under this Act.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • An offence committed under the Scheduled Castes and shall be investigated by a police officer, not below the rank of –Deputy-Superintendent

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act offences → investigated by police officer not below Deputy Superintendent rank (Central rules of 1995).

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following powers is not provided to specified Special Court under Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?To authorize a person for extra investigation other than police.

                                                                                                                                                                            Special Court (SC/ST Atrocities Act) can forfeit convict's property, remove suspect from area, take measurements/photographs; cannot authorise a non-police person for extra investigation.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following powers a Special Court cannot exercise under the Scheduled Castes and ScheduledTo impose collective fine

                                                                                                                                                                            Special Court (SC/ST Atrocities Act) → can remove a person, forfeit property, take measurements; cannot impose collective fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • In a prosecution for an offence under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the accused in his defence cannot take the plea that -—

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act applies only to accused who are not SC/ST; its Section 6 applies the IPC's general exceptions (Chapter IV), such as private defence. MPPSC gave bonus marks.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under the Scheduled caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, whoever, not being a member of a Scheduled caste or a Scheduled Tribe, causes physical harm or mental agony of a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe on the allegation of practising witchcraft or being a witch shall be punishablewith imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to five years and with fine

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act → non-SC/ST person harming SC/ST member on allegation of witchcraft → jail six months to five years, plus fine.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following statement is incorrect?"Exclusive Special Court" established under Section 14 (1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is defined under section 2(d)

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST Atrocities Act: 'Exclusive Special Court' → Section 2(1)(bd), not 2(d); 'Victim' → 2(ec); 'Dependent' → 2(bb); offences are by non-SC/ST persons.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which one of the following Sections of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes Rules, 1995, Constitution of ‘District Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee’ has been provided?Section 17

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, Rule 17 → District Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee, set up by District Magistrate in each district.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Under which one of the following Sections of the Scheduled Tribes Rules, 1995 has 'Material for Annual Report' been provided?Section 18

                                                                                                                                                                            SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, Rule 18 → 'Material for Annual Report'.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Right to Information Act of Parliament received the assent of the President of India on –15th June, 2005

                                                                                                                                                                            RTI Act → passed Lok Sabha 11 May, Rajya Sabha 12 May 2005; President's assent 15 June 2005; in force 12 October 2005 (after 120 days); a legal right. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • The Right to Information is –Both (a) and (b)

                                                                                                                                                                            Right to Information → a legal right under RTI Act 2005 and, per Supreme Court decisions, also a Fundamental Right; aims: empower citizens, transparency, accountability, curb corruption.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following terminology is/are mentioned in the Preamble of the Right to Information Act, 2005? (A) Transparency of Information (B) Revelation of Information (C) Informed Citizenry (D) Paramountcy of the democratic ideal Select the correct answer using code given below: Codes:(A), (B), (C) and (D)

                                                                                                                                                                            RTI Act 2005 Preamble mentions all four → transparency of information, revelation of information, informed citizenry, paramountcy of the democratic ideal.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is not true about the objectives of the Right to Information Act?To empower the women and weaker sections of the society

                                                                                                                                                                            RTI Act 2005 objectives → empower citizens, transparency and accountability of government, contain corruption, make democracy work for people; not 'empower women and weaker sections'.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements about the ‘Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005’ and select one which has not been provided for or is specially exempted –—

                                                                                                                                                                            RTI Act 2005, Section 6(2) → applicant need not give any reason or personal details for seeking information; the other options were provisions of the Act then.

                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following sections of the Right to Information Act is not related to the functions and powers of the Central Information Commission?12

Act, 2013.
