Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                  The Supreme Court: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                  • An Integrated Judicial system has been established under the Indian Constitution in which the Supreme Court is at the top.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Below the Supreme Court there are various High Courts.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • This single system of the Judiciary has been adopted from the Government of India Act 1935.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28th January 1950.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Articles 124 to 147 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court of India consists of the Chief Justice of the India and up to 33 other judges.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Earlier there were 30 Judges and a Chief Justice. Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 increased the number of Judges including Chief Justice from 31 to 34. The President of India appoints the judges of the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The President appoints a Chief Justice after consultation with the other judges of the Supreme Court of India and the judges of the high courts.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The person to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court must be a citizen of India and he should be, for at least 5 years, a Judge of a High Court or two or more such courts in succession; or he has been for at least ten years an advocate of a High Court or of two or more such courts in succession; or he must be a distinguishedjurist in the opinion of President.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • No minimum age is prescribed for the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Parliament has the power to increase the number of Judges in Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • A person appointed as the Judge of the Supreme Court has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Judges can give their resignation in writing to the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Judges of the Supreme Court can be removed by the President after the recommendation of the Parliament (address by each House).
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Recommendation (Address) of Parliament for the removal of Judges must be passed by a special majority in each House of the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The recommendation of Parliament is presented to the President in the same session.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The grounds on which removal of judges takes place are proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • These removals can be declared unconstitutional and illegal in the state of being extraordinary.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of 65 years.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Salary and other allowances of the Supreme Court Judges are determined by Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under Article 127, the Chief Justice of India can designate a judge of a High Court as an Ad hoc Judge of the Supreme Court for a temporary period to complete the quorum of the Judges in the Supreme Court (with the previous consent of the President and after consultation with the Chief Justice of High Court concerned).
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The bench hearing a case related to the interpretation of the Constitution should have at least 5 judges.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 129, the Supreme Court is a Court of Record.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • It has the power to punish for its contempt.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Court of Record means a court whose proceedings are kept as a record and are available as an evidence of fact. Article 131 deals with the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Disputes between the Government of India and any of the States of the Union, the government of India and any State or States on one side and any other State or States on the other side or between two or more States comes under the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (only if the dispute involues a question on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends).
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Articles 132 to 136 deal with the Appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court under its extraordinary powers conferred by Article 136 can interfere to quash the decision of a quasi - Judicial tribunal when the tribunal has either exceeded its jurisdiction or has approached the question referred to in a manner likely to result in injustice.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 137 provides that the Supreme Court has the power to review any judgement pronounced or order made by itself.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The concept of Judicial review is based on the Procedure established by law and supremacy of the Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The last authority to interpret the Constitution is the Supreme Court. It is called as the Guardian of the Indian Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Aarticle 143, the President may seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance on which he thinks it is expedient to obtain such an opinion or on any dispute arising out of the pre-constitutional treaty, agreement, covenant, engagement or other similar instruments. In first case the Supreme Court may tender or refuse to answer but in second case Supreme Court is bound to tender its opinion.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court can send any case to any court of the country.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • The source of the Doctrine of Basic Structure of the Indian Constitution is Judicial interpretation.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 141 of Indian Constitution stipulates that the decision of the Supreme Court would be binding upon all courts within the territory of India.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the Keshvananda Bharati Case (1973), the Supreme Court propounded the Doctrine of the Basic Structure of the Indian Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • When was the Supreme Court inaugurated in India?28 January, 1950

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court of India → inaugurated 28 January 1950.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Supreme Court in India was established-By the Indian Constitution

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court → established by the Constitution of India; inaugurated 28 January 1950; succeeded the Federal Court (Government of India Act, 1935).

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Provisions relating to appointment of Supreme Court and High Court Judges in the Indian Constitution were incorporated on the basis of published recommendations given by ___ Committee (1945).Sapru (Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru)

                                                                                                                                                                                  Appointment of Supreme Court and High Court Judges → based on Sapru Committee Report (1945) under Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru; set up by Non-Party Conference, November 1944.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The power to increase the number of Judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in –The Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                  Power to increase number of Supreme Court Judges → Parliament; Article 124 provides for formation of the Supreme Court.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The current sanctioned strength of Judges of Supreme Court of India is –—

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court → Part V, Chapter IV, Article 124; Articles 124 to 147 cover its composition and jurisdiction; in the 1950s it had a Chief Justice and seven Judges. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court consists of a Chief Justice and—

                                                                                                                                                                                  Original Constitution (1950) → Supreme Court of a Chief Justice and 7 puisne Judges; Parliament may increase the number (Article 124). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • To become a Judge of Supreme Court, a person must be an advocate in High Court for at least how many years?10

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court Judge (Article 124(3)) → citizen of India and High Court Judge for 5 years, or High Court advocate for 10 years, or distinguished jurist; appointed by President.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Advocates need double the time: 5 years as Judge, 10 as advocate.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The resignation letter by a Judge of Supreme Court is addressed to:The President

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court Judge resigns by writing to the President; appointed by President by warrant under hand and seal; strength: CJI + up to thirty-three Judges (originally seven). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • How can a Judge of the Supreme Court be removed?By the President on the recommendation of the Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                  SC Judge removed (Article 124(4)) → President's order after address by each House (majority of total membership + two-thirds present and voting), for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:3 and 4 only

                                                                                                                                                                                  Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 → Speaker can reject a motion to remove an SC Judge; Constitution does not define 'incapacity and proved misbehaviour'; removal by President after Parliament's address.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The age of retirement in the Supreme Court is-65 Years

                                                                                                                                                                                  Retirement age → Supreme Court Judges 65 years; High Court Judges 62 years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Higher court, higher age: SC 65, HC 62.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Don't mix 65 (Supreme Court) with 62 (High Court).

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Salaries of the Judges of the Supreme Court are determined by –Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                  Salaries of Supreme Court Judges → determined by Parliament by law (Article 125(1)); until then as in the Second Schedule.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • What is the provision to safeguard the autonomy of the Supreme Court of India?1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court autonomy → President must consult CJI on appointments; Judges' salaries charged on Consolidated Fund of India; removal by President with Parliament's special majority, not by CJI.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                  Parliament can enlarge Supreme Court's jurisdiction on Union List matters (Article 138); SC administrative expenses, incl. staff salaries and pensions, charged on Consolidated Fund of India; both statements false.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Judges of the Supreme Court, after retirement, are permitted to carry on practice before –None of the Courts

                                                                                                                                                                                  Retired Supreme Court Judge → cannot plead or act in any court or authority in India (Article 124(7)); bar on retired permanent High Court Judges → Article 220.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Acting Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India is appointed by-President

                                                                                                                                                                                  Acting Chief Justice of India → appointed by President (Article 126) when CJI post is vacant or CJI cannot act; no additional judges in Supreme Court. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Judges of Supreme Court of India are appointed by the President –In consultation with the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court Judges → appointed by President after consulting such SC and HC Judges as he deems necessary (Article 124(2)); CJI always consulted for other Judges.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • In which year was the Collegium System for the appointment of Judges adopted by the Supreme Court of India?1993

                                                                                                                                                                                  Collegium System for appointing Judges → adopted by Supreme Court in 1993; origin in the Three Judges Cases.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court’s Collegium comprises the Chief Justice of India and a few Senior Judges for recommending appointee to the Supreme Court. The number of such Senior Judges, who are part of this body, is4

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court Collegium → Chief Justice of India + 4 senior-most Judges.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid CJI + 4 = a five-member collegium.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements about the collegium system:1 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                  SC Collegium → five members: CJI + four senior-most Judges; majority opinion prevails; not created by a law of Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following statements are correct regarding National Judicial Appointments Commission? It consists of: (A) The Chief Justice of India as the Ex-Officio Chairperson. (B) Two other Senior Judges of the Supreme Court next to the Chief Justice of India, as the Ex-officio Members. (C) The Union Minister of Law and Justice as the Ex officio Member. (D) Two eminent persons to be nominated by the Committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of Opposition in the House of the people or where there is no such Leader of Opposition, then, Leader of single largest opposition party in the House of the People Members. Choose the correct options.All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                  NJAC (99th Amendment, 2014) → CJI (Chair), two senior SC Judges, Union Law Minister, two eminent persons (chosen by PM, CJI, Leader of Opposition); struck down in 2015.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following has recommended that appointment of Judges to Higher Courts should be through the participation of the Executive, Legislature and Chief Justice?Second Administrative Reforms Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                  Second Administrative Reforms Commission → recommended appointing higher court Judges with participation of Executive, Legislature and Chief Justice of India. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Ad hoc Judges are appointed in the Supreme Court when–There is no quorum of the Judges available to hold.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Ad hoc Judges in Supreme Court (Article 127(1)) → when quorum is lacking; CJI requests them with President's prior consent, after consulting the High Court's Chief Justice. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • With reference to Indian judiciary, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                  Article 128 → CJI, with President's prior consent, can ask a retired SC Judge (or qualified ex-HC Judge) to sit as SC Judge; High Courts too can review own judgments.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The minimum number of Judges of the Supreme Court required for hearing any case involving interpretation of the Constitution is –Five

                                                                                                                                                                                  Cases involving interpretation of the Constitution → minimum 5 Supreme Court Judges (Constitution Bench).

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The minimum number of Supreme Court Judges who can hear a case involving a substantial question of law as to the Interpretation of the Constitution is –Five

                                                                                                                                                                                  Substantial question of law on interpreting the Constitution → minimum five SC Judges; benches kept odd (3, 5, 7, 9, 11) to avoid a tie.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the State falls under its–Original jurisdiction

                                                                                                                                                                                  Centre-State disputes → Supreme Court's original jurisdiction (Article 131), excluding other courts; covers disputes between Government of India and States, and among States. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following statements is not true about the power of Supreme Court of India?It has the exclusive power to issue writs to protect the fundamental rights of the People.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Writs for Fundamental Rights → Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226); so SC's writ power is not exclusive.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse SC's original jurisdiction in inter-governmental disputes is exclusive; its writ power is not.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Of the following statements, which one is not correct?Supreme Court can hear from any High Court/ Tribunals except Court-martial.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Supreme Court can hear appeals from Court Martial too (Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007); constituted 1950; highest court of appeal.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Supreme Court of India is a ‘Court of Record.’ It implies that –All its decisions have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned in any court.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Court of Record (Article 129) → its judgments have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned in any court; can punish for its own contempt.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following Courts in India is/are known as the Court (s) of Record?The High Courts and the Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                  Courts of Record → Supreme Court (Article 129) and High Courts (Article 215); both can punish for contempt of themselves.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following pairs (Article- provision) is not correctly matched?Article 124 - Supreme Court to be a Court of Record

                                                                                                                                                                                  Court of Record → Article 129 (not 124, which establishes SC); Article 143 → advisory; 132 → appellate; 136 → special leave to appeal.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Article 124 creates the Supreme Court; Court of Record status is Article 129.

                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                  Practise this hour: 40 questions

                                                                                                                                                                                    Spaced review: 15 questions from earlier hours

                                                                                                                                                                                      Your weak questions

                                                                                                                                                                                        Hour 32 →

                                                                                                                                                                                        Hour 32 of 72 · Learn

                                                                                                                                                                                        The Supreme Court · part 2 of 3

                                                                                                                                                                                        32 facts · 39 questions · 7 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                        • Consider the following statements:1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                        Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 → on H.N. Sanyal Committee (1961) report; SC and HCs punish contempt (Articles 129, 215); Constitution does not define civil/criminal contempt.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Under Article 32 in which case ‘Wilful non compliance’ with court order was declared as contempt of the court?M.L. Sachdev vs.Union of India

                                                                                                                                                                                        M.L. Sachdev vs Union of India → wilful non-compliance with court order treated as contempt; civil contempt = wilful disobedience (Section 2(b), Contempt of Courts Act, 1971).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Supreme Court holds its meetings in New Delhi, but it can meet elsewhere –With the approval of President.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Supreme Court sits in Delhi or other places the CJI appoints with approval of the President (Article 130).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Needs the President's approval, not Parliament's or a majority of Judges.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • In which of the following cases, the Supreme Court of India enunciated the ‘Doctrine of Basic Structure’?Keshvanand Bharti

                                                                                                                                                                                        Basic Structure doctrine → Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973), thirteen-Judge bench, 7:6; Parliament cannot damage basic structure under Article 368. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India have been declared by the Supreme Court as the ‘Inviolable basic structure’ of the Constitution: Select the correct answer from the code given below:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                        Articles 32, 226, 227 → inviolable basic structure (judicial review by SC and High Courts, Kesavananda Bharati); Article 245 not.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • The source of the ‘Basic Structure Theory of the Constitution’ in India isJudicial Interpretation

                                                                                                                                                                                        Basic Structure Theory → source: judicial interpretation (Kesavananda Bharati case), approved in Minerva Mills case, 1980; limits amending power under Article 368.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • The second largest bench Constituted by the Supreme Court till date was in the –Golaknath Case

                                                                                                                                                                                        Largest SC bench → 13 Judges, Kesavananda Bharati (1973); second largest → 11 Judges, Golaknath vs State of Punjab (1967).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • In which of the following cases, Supreme Court held that? “Fundamental Rights enable a man to chalk out his life in the manner he likes best “?Golaknath Vs. The State of Punjab

                                                                                                                                                                                        Golaknath vs State of Punjab → 'Fundamental Rights enable a man to chalk out his life in the manner he likes best'.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Identify the incorrect pair of Case and Ruling in that case by Supreme Court:Bella Banerjee Case- Right to travel abroad is a part of personal liberty.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Right to travel abroad as personal liberty → Maneka Gandhi (1978), not Bella Banerjee (land case, 1948 Act); Indira Sawhney → OBC creamy layer; Vishaka → workplace sexual harassment.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Bella Banerjee is a land development law case; travel abroad belongs to Maneka Gandhi.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Consider the following statements and state which one of them is correct?It has Original, Appellate as well as Advisory Jurisdiction

                                                                                                                                                                                        Supreme Court jurisdiction → Original (Article 131), Appellate (Articles 132-136) and Advisory (Article 143).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Numbers rise with the order: 131 original, 132-136 appeal, 143 advice.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following is concerned with the Supreme Court of India?More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                        Collegium system, appellate and original jurisdiction → all relate to Supreme Court; collegium evolved through SC judgments, not by an Act or the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Appellate Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in connection with Constitutional Cases?Article 132 read with Article 134 A

                                                                                                                                                                                        Appellate jurisdiction in constitutional cases → Article 132 read with Article 134A (appeals from High Courts); Article 131 → original jurisdiction. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • All the cases regarding interpretation of the Constitution can be brought to the Supreme Court under its–Appellate Jurisdiction

                                                                                                                                                                                        Cases on interpretation of the Constitution reach the Supreme Court under its Appellate Jurisdiction (appeals from High Courts in civil, criminal or other cases).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Curative Petition in India can be filed in Supreme Court under Article –142

                                                                                                                                                                                        Curative Petition → evolved in Rupa Ashok Hurra vs Ashok Hurra (2002); filed in Supreme Court under Article 142.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which Article of the Constitution permits the Supreme Court to review its judgement or order?Article 137

                                                                                                                                                                                        Article 137 → Supreme Court can review its own judgment or order, subject to law made by Parliament and rules under Article 145. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following is correct about the Supreme Court regarding its Judgment?It can change the Judgment

                                                                                                                                                                                        Supreme Court can change (review) its own judgment under Article 137, subject to law by Parliament and rules under Article 145.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • With reference to the constitution of India, prohibitions or limitations or provisions contained in ordinary laws cannot act as prohibitions or limitations on the constitutional powers under Article 142. It could mean which one of the following?The Supreme Court of India is not constrained in the exercise of its powers by laws made by the Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Article 142 → SC can pass any decree or order for complete justice, enforceable across India; ordinary laws cannot limit it, so SC is not constrained by Parliament's laws.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • In India, Judicial Review impliesthe power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial Review → power of Judiciary to interpret the Constitution and declare laws or executive orders void if they conflict with it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                        Constitution doesn't define 'basic structure' (doctrine first recognised in Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973); it does provide judicial review to protect rights (Article 13 voids laws violating Part III).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • In India, the power of Judicial Review is enjoyed by?The Supreme Court as well as High Courts

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial Review in India → both Supreme Court and High Courts; originated in USA, Marbury vs Madison (1803), CJ John Marshall; declared part of basic structure.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                        42nd Amendment (1976) barred High Courts from judging validity of Central laws; 43rd Amendment (1977) restored it; SC can examine constitutional amendments; both statements false.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • The system of Judicial Review, is prevalent inBoth in India and U.S.A.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial Review → exists in both India (Article 13) and USA; not in UK, where Parliament is supreme and its laws cannot be challenged in court.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Assertion (A): The scope of Judicial review is limited in India.Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial review in India is limited (mainly checks laws touching basic structure); Constitution is a 'bag of borrowings'; both true, but R does not explain A.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • In essence, what does 'Due Process of Law' mean?The principle of natural justice

                                                                                                                                                                                        Due Process of Law → in essence the principle of natural justice (fairness, no arbitrariness); natural justice includes 'Nemo judex in causa sua' (no one judges own cause).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Don't pick 'procedure established by law'; due process is about fairness, i.e. natural justice.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Judicial review in the Indian Constitution is based on –Procedure established by Law

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial review in India → based on 'Procedure established by Law'; found in Articles 13, 32, 136, 137, 226, 227.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Don't pick 'Due Process of Law'; Indian judicial review rests on procedure established by law.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Judicial process in India is based onNone of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                        Judicial process in India → based on the Constitution, procedure established by law, conventions and due process of routine law; so 'more than one' is correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • A Constitution (Amendment) Act may be declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court of India if it –Removes Right of Equality before the law from Part III and places it elsewhere in the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Amendment moving Right to Equality before law out of Part III → can be struck down (Article 13(2): no law may take away or abridge Part III rights).

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Supreme Court is aNone of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                        Supreme Court → highest court, guarantor of Fundamental Rights and guardian of the Constitution; so 'more than one of the above' is correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who has the last authority to explain the Constitution?Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                        Final authority to interpret the Constitution → Supreme Court; it is the Guardian or Custodian of the Constitution. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following is the custodian of the Constitution of India?The Supreme Court of India

                                                                                                                                                                                        Custodian / Guardian of the Constitution of India → Supreme Court (not President, PM or Lok Sabha Secretariat). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).(A) is false, but (R) is true.

                                                                                                                                                                                        SC has no exclusive jurisdiction on validity of Central laws (High Courts too; writs under Articles 32 and 226); SC is Guardian of the Constitution → A false, R true.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following cases comes under the Jurisdiction of High Court and Supreme Court?Enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Enforcement of Fundamental Rights → both Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226); HC writ power is wider (also other rights). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)
