                                                                                                                                                                                            Your weak questions

                                                                                                                                                                                              Hour 33 →

                                                                                                                                                                                              Hour 33 of 72 · Learn

                                                                                                                                                                                              The Supreme Court · part 3 of 3

                                                                                                                                                                                              40 facts · 43 questions · 4 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • Under which Article of the Constitution of India Supreme Court safeguards the Fundamental Rights of the Indian citizens?32

                                                                                                                                                                                              Article 32 → Right to Constitutional Remedies; Supreme Court issues directions, orders, writs to enforce Fundamental Rights (Part III).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The power to enlarge the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India with respect to any matter included in the Union List of Legislative Powers rests with –The Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                              Enlarging Supreme Court's jurisdiction on Union List matters → Parliament by law (Article 138(1)).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • By whom the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India can be enlarged?Parliament by making a law

                                                                                                                                                                                              Supreme Court's jurisdiction can be enlarged by Parliament by making a law (Article 138).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse It needs a law, not a mere resolution of Parliament or a Presidential order.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who has the right to seek advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law –President

                                                                                                                                                                                              Advisory opinion of Supreme Court on a question of law → sought by the President (Article 143), not PM or High Courts. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Under which Article, the President of India refer to the Supreme Court regarding the process of appointment and transfer of Judges in the Supreme Court and High Courts?Article 143 sub clause (1)

                                                                                                                                                                                              Article 143(1) → President can refer to Supreme Court a question of law or fact of public importance, e.g. appointment and transfer of Judges.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following statements regarding the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is correct?2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                              Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143) → heard by a bench of 5; opinion not binding on government; SC must answer only references on old treaties/agreements, not other questions. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The Supreme Court of India tenders advice to the President on a matter of law or fact:Only if he seeks such advice

                                                                                                                                                                                              Supreme Court advises the President on law or fact of public importance only when he seeks it (Article 143(1)), never on its own.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President make a reference to the Supreme Court to seek the Court’s opinion on the Constitutional validity of the Election Commission’s decision on deferring the Gujarat Assembly Elections (in the year 2002)?Article 143

                                                                                                                                                                                              Gujarat Assembly election deferment (2002) → President Abdul Kalam sought SC's advice under Article 143 on Election Commission powers (Articles 324, 174).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • “I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India.....uphold the Sovereignty and Integrity of India..... Perform the duties of my office... uphold the Constitution and Law.” it is the form of Oath taken by –The Chief Justice of India

                                                                                                                                                                                              Oath to 'bear true faith and allegiance... uphold the Constitution and the laws' → Chief Justice of India; Third Schedule has 10 forms of oaths/affirmations.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who has the right to transfer any case anywhere in India?Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                              Article 139A → Supreme Court can transfer cases anywhere in India (e.g. same question of law pending in several High Courts).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Match List-I with List-II and identify the correct answer from the code given below:—

                                                                                                                                                                                              A.K. Gopalan → preventive detention procedure; Romesh Thapar → restrictions on free speech; Shankari Prasad → Parliament's power to amend; Champakam Dorairajan → equal admission to educational institutions.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following case is related to zamindari system?1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                              Kameshwar Singh vs State of Bihar → zamindari abolition case. The book's key counts all four listed cases, though Romesh Thapar vs State of Madras was a free-speech case.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Supreme Court's judgement of Indra Sawhney Vs Union of India Case is related to which issue?Regarding the issue of OBC reservation in Government employment

                                                                                                                                                                                              Indra Sawhney vs Union of India (1992) → OBC reservation in government jobs; reservation under Articles 15(4), 16(4) not to exceed 50 per cent.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Indra Sawhney = the 50% ceiling case.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Under which article, Supreme Court recently declared Migrants (Determination by Tribunal) Act, 1983 as unconstitutional for violation of the sacred duty of centre?Article - 355

                                                                                                                                                                                              Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 → struck down by SC (13 July 2005) under Article 355; migration from Bangladesh called aggression on Assam.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • TDSAT judgments can be challenged in the:High Court and Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                              TDSAT (set up 2000 by amending TRAI Act, 1997) → its judgments can be challenged in High Court and Supreme Court.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who was the Chief Justice of India for the shortest duration?Kamal Narain Singh

                                                                                                                                                                                              Shortest CJI tenure → Kamal Narain Singh (25.11.1991 to 12.12.1991), shorter than G.B. Pattanaik, S. Rajendra Babu, R.M. Lodha.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The correct sequence of Chief Justice of Supreme Court of India is -H.L. Dattu, T.S. Thakur, Jagdish Singh Khehar

                                                                                                                                                                                              CJI sequence → H.L. Dattu → T.S. Thakur → Jagdish Singh Khehar; earlier S.R. Das → B.P. Sinha → P.B. Gajendragadkar; K.G. Balakrishnan → S.H. Kapadia.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following statements is/are true about previous Chief Justice of India, Yashwant Vishnu Chandrachud?I, II and III

                                                                                                                                                                                              Y.V. Chandrachud → 16th Chief Justice of India (22 February 1978 to 11 July 1985), longest-serving CJI; appointed by President Neelam Sanjiva Reddy.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Fathima Beevi died recently. Consider the following statements regarding her:1 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                              Justice M. Fathima Beevi (died 23 November 2023) → first woman SC Judge (1989); first Muslim woman in higher judiciary; Governor of Tamil Nadu 1997-2001.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse She was Governor of Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following posts was held by A.S. Anand in late 1990's?Chief Justice of India

                                                                                                                                                                                              A.S. Anand (Adarsh Sein Anand) → 29th Chief Justice of India, 10 October 1998 to 31 October 2001.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Fathima Beevi, who recently passes away, she is the India's first:Woman Judge of Supreme Court

                                                                                                                                                                                              Justice Fathima Beevi → India's first woman Judge of the Supreme Court; also first Muslim woman Governor (Tamil Nadu).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which one of the following is appointed as the fourth female Judge of Supreme Court in April 2010?Justice Gyan Sudha Misra

                                                                                                                                                                                              Justice Gyan Sudha Misra → fourth woman SC Judge (30 April 2010), earlier Patna HC Chief Justice; before her Fathima Beevi, Sujata Manohar, Ruma Pal; fifth: Ranjana Prakash Desai.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Order of women SC Judges: Fathima, Sujata, Ruma, Gyan, Ranjana.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who amongst the following, recently appointed as Supreme Court judge, was not earlier judge of a High Court?L. Nageshwara Rao

                                                                                                                                                                                              L. Nageshwara Rao → elevated directly from the Bar to Supreme Court (7th such person), sworn in 13 May 2016; never a High Court judge.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Before his appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court of India in July 2024, Justice N. Kotiswar Singh was the Chief Justice of which High Court?Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court

                                                                                                                                                                                              Justice N. Kotiswar Singh → Chief Justice of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court before SC (oath 18 July 2024); Justice Manmohan (ex-Delhi HC CJ) sworn 5 December 2024.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who among the following chief justice of Madhya Pradesh High Court has not been the judge at Supreme Court of India?Justice S.K. Jha

                                                                                                                                                                                              Among MP High Court Chief Justices, S.K. Jha never became a Supreme Court Judge; A.K. Patnaik, R.V. Raveendran, A.K. Mathur did.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which one of the following judges of Supreme Court of India has not worked in Rajasthan High Court as judge?Justice R.C. Lahoti

                                                                                                                                                                                              R.C. Lahoti (35th CJI, 1 June 2004 to 1 November 2005) → never a Rajasthan High Court judge; joined the Bar at Guna (MP) in 1960.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who was the Chief Justice of India when Public Interest litigation was introduced in the Indian Judicial System?—

                                                                                                                                                                                              First PIL → Hussainara Khatoon vs State of Bihar (1979), taken up by Justice P.N. Bhagwati; CJI then was Y.V. Chandrachud; Bhagwati later 17th CJI.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Public Interest Litigations was introduced by –Judicial initiative

                                                                                                                                                                                              Public Interest Litigation → introduced by judicial initiative after the Emergency era; in line with Article 39A (social justice); any public person or NGO can approach court.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                              V.R. Krishna Iyer → SC judge, never Chief Justice of India; with P.N. Bhagwati, pioneer of PIL (Public Interest Litigation), which lies in both High Courts and Supreme Court. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse PIL = Public Interest Litigation, not Public Inquiry or Public Investment Litigation.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).(A) is false, but (R) is true.

                                                                                                                                                                                              PIL → judge-made process that widened locus standi, giving weaker sections access to justice (R true); calling it 'essential for rule of law' is treated as false (A false).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements and choose the correct answer from the code given below:Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                              PIL → public-minded citizens can approach court for those unable to reach it themselves; A and R true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in:The United States

                                                                                                                                                                                              Public Interest Litigation → originated in the United States (legal aid movement; first legal aid office in New York, 1876). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Don't confuse Not India or UK: the PIL concept began in the United States.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • ‘Judicial Activism’ in India is related to –Public Interest Litigation

                                                                                                                                                                                              Judicial Activism in India → linked to Public Interest Litigation; began in the mid 1970s on the Supreme Court's initiative.

Anand; adventurism is an extreme form of activism.

Shah) glorified women's status: preferring women as Principal of Government Girls' College does not violate Articles 14, 15, 16.

State of Rajasthan and others is related to -Prevention of sexual harassment of women at work place

                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Governor: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Constitution of India envisages the same pattern of government in the states as that for the centre, that is, a parliamentary system. Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the Government of the state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Governor is the executive head of the state. Generally, a person is the governor of only one state and after the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956, the same person can be appointed as the governor of two or more States.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Governor is appointed by the President of India (Article 155).
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • He holds office for a term of 5 years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • However, his tenure is subject to the pleasure of the President [Article 156(1)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Further he can resign at any time by addressing a resignation letter to the President [Article 156(2)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • According to Article 157, the qualifications for the post of the Governor are - (i) He should be a citizen of India, and (ii) age over 35 years. Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act 2019 reorganised the state of Jammu & Kashmir into: (i) the Union territory of Jammu & Kashmir with a legislature, and (ii) the Union Territory of Ladakh without a legislature. Both the newly created Union Territories will be administered by the President through a Lieutenant Governor appointed by him.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • All the executive works of the state is formally done in the name of the Governor.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Chief Minister of the National Capital Territory of Delhi is appointed by the President (Article 239 AA).
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The salary, allowances and other expenditures related to the Governor are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of each state [Article 202(3)(a)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Governor has the power to appoint the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister [Article 164(1)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • He is an integral part of State Legislative Assembly and has the right to address and send messages and of summoning/proroguing and dissolving the State Legislative Assembly.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Governor has the right to nominate one-sixth of the members of the legislative council. Governor of a state, if he is of the opinion that the Anglo-Indian community needs representation in the Legislative Assembly of the state and is not adequately represented therein, could nominate one member of that community to the Assembly. It is noteworthy that the arrangements of nominating representatives of the Anglo-Indian community in the state Legislative Assemblies have not been extended beyond the stipulated date (25 January, 2020) by 'The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019. Thus, the arrangements of nomination of one member of the Anglo-Indian Community in the Legislative Assemblies has ended.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • A person who has the qualification required for the judge of a High Court can be appointed as the Advocate General by the Governor (Art. 165).
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • When a bill is sent to the Governor after it is passed by State Legislature, he can give his assent to the bill, or return the bill (if it is not money bill) for reconsideration, or reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • However if the bill is passed again by the state legislature the governor may give his assent to the bill or reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • According to Article 201, if a bill is reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President, then the President will declare whether to give assent to the bill or not.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Article 202 (3) (a) the emoluments and allowances of the Governor and other expenditure relating to office are charged on the consolidated fund of the state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Governor can promulgate an ordinance when the state legislature is not in session (Article 213), and only if the circumstances require immediate action.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • He can grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remission of punishment or suspend, remit and commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the state extends (Article 161).
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Sarojini Naidu was the first woman to be appointed as the Governor of any state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • She was the governor of Uttar Pradesh (United Provinces) from 15th August, 1947 to 2 March, 1949.
                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The original plan in the draft Constitution for having elected Governors was dropped because1, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Elected Governor plan dropped → it meant another election; elected Governor might feel superior to CM; Governor works under Parliamentary System. Governor is appointed by President. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                    • To whom is the Governor of a State responsible?President

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Governor → responsible to the President; holds office at President's pleasure (Article 156(1)), in effect the Union Government; term five years (Article 156(3)).                                                                                                                                                                                                     Union Territories → administered by the President through an administrator appointed by him (Article 239(1)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Same Governor for two or more States → emoluments shared among States in proportion fixed by President's order (Article 158(3A)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The State Legislature · part 1 of 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                          28 facts · 39 questions · 6 Must know
