Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          The State Legislature: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Legislative Council

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • As per Article 169, the Parliament has power of the abolition and the creation of the Legislative Council in a state, if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect, by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by a majority of not less-than two-thirds of the members of the Assembly, present and voting.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Article 171 of the Indian Constitution makes provision for the Composition of Legislative Councils in the states.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Only 6 States have Legislative Councils at present, these are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh. It is a permanent House.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The tenure of its members is 6 years.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 171 (1) the maximum strength of the Legislative Council shall not be more than one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, but not less than 40.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Uttar Pradesh with 100 members in the Legislative Council is the largest Legislative Council.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 171

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (4) the elected members of Legislative Council are elected in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and by secret ballot.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A person to be elected a member of the Legislative Council must not be less than 30 years of age.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If the question arises as to whether a member of the house of the legislature of a state has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) of the Article 191, the question shall be referred for the decision of the governor and his decision shall be final. Before giving any decision on any such question, the Governor shall obtain the opinion of the Election Commission and shall act according to such opinion. Article 171 (3) Provides for the election of the nearest 5/6 members of the legislative council and the remaining members to be nominated by the Governor. However, the composition of the Legislative councils in the states is under the provisions of Section 10 and Schedule 3 of 'The Representation of the People Act, 1950' (as amended from time to time) made by the Parliament under Article 171 (2).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The State Legislative Council has the power to remove its Chairman or Deputy Chairman from their post by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Article 191 of the Constitution of India deals with the disqualification of the members of the State Legislature. Legislative Assembly
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 168 the State legislature, in specified States, consists of Legislative Council, Legislative Assembly and governor of the state, and in the other States it consists of Legislative Assembly and the Governor of the State.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Legislative Assembly of each state shall be composed of Members elected by direct election on the basis of Universal Adult Suffrage from territorial constituencies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The maximum number of members of the Assembly shall not be more than 500 nor less than 60 members, generally.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The smallest assembly among Union territories is Puducherry (33) and in states it is Sikkim (32).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly with 403 members.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Election Commission of India conducts the elections for the state legislatures.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 170 (2) Each state shall be divided into territorial constituencies in such a manner that the ratio between the Population of each constituency and the number of seats allotted to it shall, so far as practicable, be the same throughout the state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Speaker of the assembly exercises a casting vote in case of equality of votes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The speaker establishes the contact between the house and the Governor.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In the absence of a speaker, the deputy speaker works as the speaker of the Assembly.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001, the number of members in State Assemblies will remain the same until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Under section 14(3) of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 the number of assembly members in Jammu & Kashmir UT is 90 elected and 5 nominated [plus 24 vacant election constituencies fall in areas occupied by Pakistan (POK)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Only three Union Territories (Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir) have legislative assemblies. Article 173 lays down the qualifications of a person to be a member of the legislative assembly (a) He must be a citizen of India, and (b) He must not be less than 25 years of age.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 332 the Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the legislative assembly in proportion to their population.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Rights and Functions of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly are the same as those of the Speaker of the lower House of the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • As per Indian Constitution, Legislature of States consists3 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Legislature (Article 168) → Governor + Legislative Assembly (+ Legislative Council where it exists); bicameral: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which is the Upper Chamber of State Legislatures in India?Legislative Council

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Upper House of a State Legislature → Legislative Council; lower → Legislative Assembly; with only one House it is the Legislative Assembly (Article 168(2)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides the provision of Vidhan Parishad in the State?Article 171

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Article 171 → composition of Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad); Article 169 → its creation and abolition.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Don't mix 169 (create/abolish the Council) with 171 (its composition).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the right method to establish or cancel the second chamber in states?Proposal in Legislative Assembly with full majority along with law passed by Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Create/abolish State Legislative Council (Article 169) → Assembly resolution by majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting, then a law by Parliament. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following statement about resolution adopted by a State Legislative Assembly under Article 169 of the Constitution of India for the abolition of the State Legislative Council is correct?It does not impose an obligation on the Union Government to take action for initiating legislative in Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Article 169 resolution to abolish a State Legislative Council → Union Government is not obliged to start legislation in Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the composition of the Legislative Council in a state of India, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Both (1) and (2)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Legislative Council size (Article 171) → not more than one-third of Assembly's total membership, and never less than forty.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Ceiling one-third of Assembly, floor forty.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Legislative Council → max one-third of Assembly strength, so never larger than half; Governor does not nominate its Chairman; Assembly: 60 to 500 members (Article 170(1)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How many members are nominated in the Legislative Council of Uttar Pradesh by the State Governor?1/10 of the total members

                                                                                                                                                                                                          UP Legislative Council → Governor nominates 1/10 of members (per book); nominees have special knowledge of literature, science, arts, co-operative movement, social service (Article 171(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is correct about State Legislative Council?(ii) (iii) (vi) (viii)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Legislative Council → permanent House, cannot be dissolved; members serve six years, one-third retire every second year; elects own Chairman; one-third elected by Assembly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Industrialists are not a category that elects Council members.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following cannot be dissolved but can be abolished?State Legislative Councils

                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Legislative Council → cannot be dissolved but can be abolished (Article 169); member's tenure 6 years. Rajya Sabha: neither; Lok Sabha and Assemblies: dissolved, not abolished. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Council: abolish yes, dissolve no; Rajya Sabha: neither.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following States of India does not have a Legislative Council so for even though the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 provides for it?Madhya Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Madhya Pradesh has no Legislative Council though Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 provides for it; 6 bicameral States: UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following States does not have Bicameral Legislature?Tamil Nadu

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh → unicameral; Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Bihar, Maharashtra → bicameral (have Legislative Council). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How many re-organised States had Bicameral Legislatures in 1956?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                          After 1956 reorganisation, 7 of 14 States were bicameral: UP, Bihar, Bombay, Madras, Mysore, Punjab, West Bengal; Councils abolished: West Bengal 1969, Punjab 1970, Tamil Nadu 1986.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 170 of the Indian Constitution, the minimum and maximum strength of members of Legislative Assembly in a state can be respectively:60 and 500

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Article 170 → State Legislative Assembly: minimum 60, maximum 500 members, directly elected; Sikkim is an exception. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Assembly size: 60 to 500.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements: The Constitution of India provides that2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Assembly → not more than 500 members, not 450 (Article 170(1)); minimum age to be chosen to the Assembly → 25 years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution consists the provision of the election of Legislative Assemblies of States–Article 170

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Article 170 → composition and direct election of Legislative Assemblies; Article 176 → Governor's special address; Article 178 → Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the minimum age limit prescribed for the membership of Legislative Assembly?25 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Minimum age → Legislative Assembly member 25 years (Article 173(b)); Legislative Council member 30 years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Upper House, higher age: Council 30, Assembly 25.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The provision for the representation of Anglo-Indian Community in the Legislative Assemblies of the States has been made in the Constitution of India under –—

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Anglo-Indian representation in State Assemblies → was under Article 333 (Governor could nominate one member); this arrangement was later discontinued.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which state among the following has the maximum number of members in Legislative Assembly?Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly (403 members), more than Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following Indian States has the largest number of members in its State Legislature?Himachal Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Himachal Pradesh Assembly → 68 seats; Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya → 60 each.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?Manipur — 62

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Manipur Assembly → 60 members (not 62); Goa → 40; Uttarakhand → 70; Uttar Pradesh → 403.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which Union Territory formed after division of Jammu and Kashmir State does not have a legislature of its own?Ladakh

                                                                                                                                                                                                          J&K split (5 August 2019): Jammu & Kashmir → UT with legislature; Ladakh → UT without legislature; separate Lieutenant Governors.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who conducts the State Assembly Elections?Election Commission of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Assembly elections → conducted by Election Commission of India (Article 324).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Not the State Election Commission, even though these are State elections.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who among the following is the final authority to decide any question relating to disqualification of a Member of a House of Legislature of a State?Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Disqualification of a State legislator (grounds in Article 191(1)) → Governor's decision is final (Article 192), acting on Election Commission's opinion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Final decision on question as to disqualification of members of a Legislative Assembly is taken by –Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Final decision on disqualification of an MLA → Governor (Article 192), who must obtain and follow the Election Commission's opinion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who decides the disqualification of members of State Legislative Assembly, for matters other than those in the tenth schedule of the Constitution?Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Disqualification of MLAs for reasons other than the Tenth Schedule → decided by Governor, according to Election Commission's opinion (Article 192).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Tenth Schedule cases are not decided by the Governor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If the Speaker of Legislative Assembly of a State wants to resign, he will give his resignation to –Deputy Speaker

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker (Article 179(b)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Not the Governor or CM: the Speaker's resignation goes to the Deputy Speaker.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Speaker vacates office if he ceases to be Assembly member, resigns (to Deputy Speaker) or is removed by resolution; not immediately on dissolution (Article 179).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Speaker continues to be the Speaker even after the dissolution of the Assembly until:Immediately before the first sitting of the new Assembly constituted after dissolution

                                                                                                                                                                                                                After Assembly dissolution, Speaker stays in office until immediately before the first sitting of the new Assembly (Article 179).

Satyabrat → Manipur; Ritu Khandari → Uttarakhand.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Ramkishore Shukla → has held Protem Speaker, Speaker and Deputy Speaker posts in Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Who prorogues the Vidhan Sabha of a State?Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Vidhan Sabha of a State is prorogued by the Governor (Article 174(2)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Governor addresses the Assembly at the first session after each general election and first session of each year; where State has no rule, Lok Sabha rules apply.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Select the correct order of proceedings of madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly.3, 2, 4, 1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Order of MP Assembly proceedings → oath or affirmation → Governor's address → introduction of Ministers → mention of death.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following statements are correct in reference to rule of procedure for 'Motion For Adjournment on a matter of Public importance in Rajasthan Legislative Assembly? (A) Speaker's consent necessary to make motion. (B) The motion shall raise a question of privilege. (C) The motion shall be restricted to a specific matter of recent occurrence. (D) Not more than one such motion shall be made at the same sitting. Select the correct answer using code given below: Codes:(A), (C) & (D)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Rajasthan Assembly adjournment motion → needs Speaker's consent; specific matter of recent occurrence; only one per sitting; cannot raise a question of privilege.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding subordinate legislation in Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?Speaker refers Bills containing provisions for delegation of legislative powers to the Committee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Rajasthan Assembly Committee on Subordinate Legislation → examines 'orders' and Bill provisions delegating powers (Rules 240, 241); Speaker does not refer such Bills to it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • What is the 'quorum' required in the State Legislature to hold a meeting?Ten members or one tenth of the total members of the House, whichever is greater.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Quorum of a House of State Legislature → ten members or one-tenth of total members, whichever is greater (Article 189(3)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse It is 'whichever is greater', not 'whichever is less'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to the 'Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajasthan Legislative Assembly'. which of the follwing department's estimates do not comes under the control of Estimates Committee 'A'?Home Department

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Rajasthan Assembly rules → Home Department's estimates do not come under Estimates Committee 'A'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • State Legislative Assembly can participate in the election of which of the following: I. President of India II. Vice-President of India III. Members of Rajya Sabha IV. Members of Legislative Council Select the correct answer:I, III and IV

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Legislative Assembly takes part in electing the President, Rajya Sabha members and Legislative Council members; not the Vice-President.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse MLAs vote for the President but not for the Vice-President.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature?Business in the legislature shall be transacted only inofficial language of the state or in Hindior in English.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Legislature business → in State official language(s), Hindi or English (Article 210(1)); Advocate General cannot vote; conduct of SC/HC Judges cannot be discussed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The ‘Contingency Fund’ of the State is operated byThe Governor of the State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Contingency Fund of the State → placed at the disposal of the Governor for urgent or unforeseen expenditure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following is responsible for establishing ‘the Contingency Fund of the State’?The Legislature of the State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Contingency Fund of the State → established by the State Legislature by law; placed at Governor's disposal for advances on unforeseen expenditure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following is correct about the heading of the Article 162 of the Constitution of India?Extension of Executive Power of State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Article 162 → Extent of executive power of State: covers matters on which the State Legislature can make laws.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Match the articles related to State Legislature:(iii) (i) (iv) (ii)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Legislature Articles: 168 → constitution of Legislature; 178 → Speaker and Deputy Speaker; 195 → salaries of members; 199 → definition of Money Bills.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • A bill other than Money Bill which is passed by Legislative Assembly for the first time, may remain pending in the legislative council for how many months?For not more than three months

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Ordinary bill passed by Assembly → Legislative Council can hold it 3 months first time (Article 197), about 4 months in all; Vidhan Sabha Speaker decides Money Bill. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • In which assembly of States, money Bills are proposed?Only in Legislative Assembly

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Money Bills → introduced only in Legislative Assembly; Council returns it within 14 days with recommendations (Article 198(2)), which Assembly may accept or reject.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • If budget is disclosed before introducing in the Legislative Assembly, what will happen?Finance Minister will have to resign

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Budget leaked before presentation in Assembly → Finance Minister must take individual responsibility and resign (oath of secrecy; Official Secrecy Act, 1923).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • No money Bill can be introduced in Assembly of a State, except on the recommendations of –The Governor of the State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Money Bill → introduced only on Governor's recommendation (Article 207(1)), never in Legislative Council; matters listed in Article 199(1)(a)-(f).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to which Article of Constitution of India, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor of a State?Article 164

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Chief Minister → appointed by the Governor under Article 164(1).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following statements about the Chief Minister of a State is not correct?The Governor has to exercise all his functions on the advice of the Chief Minister

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Governor acts on advice of Council of Ministers headed by CM, except where Constitution requires his discretion (Article 163(1)); so 'all functions on CM's advice' is wrong.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which of the following Constitutional Amendment in India has decided the maximum strength of the Council of Minister with Chief Minister in a State?91st Constitutional Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                91st Amendment Act, 2003 → Article 164(1A): State Council of Ministers, including CM, cannot exceed 15% of Assembly members.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • What can be the minimum strength of Council of Ministers including Chief Minister in the States?12

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Council of Ministers including CM → minimum 12, maximum fifteen per cent of Assembly members (Article 164(1A)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Memory aid Floor 12 ministers, ceiling fifteen per cent.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Which one of the following statements about the Chief Minister is not correct?He is normally selected by the Governor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Chief Minister → formally appointed by Governor (Article 164(1)) but chosen by majority party members in Assembly; not selected by the Governor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • How long can a Minister continue without being elected to the State Assembly?Six Months

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Non-member Minister in a State → may continue six consecutive months; ceases to be Minister if not elected to State Legislature by then (Article 164(4)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Art 173: legislator must be citizen, twenty-five+ (Assembly)/thirty+ (Council), so voter eligibility alone can't make one minister; RPA 1951: two+ years' jail → disqualified till six years after release.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse The six-year bar runs from release; it is not a permanent disqualification.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Pay and allowances of the Ministers of a State Government are determined by the –State Legislative Assembly

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Salaries and allowances of State Ministers → fixed by State Legislature by law (Article 164(5)); until then as in the Second Schedule.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Courts cannot inquire into ministers' advice to the Governor (Article 163(3)); State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Legislative Assembly (Article 164(2)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to:the Legislative Assembly

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Council of Ministers → collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly (Article 164(2)); Ministers hold office during Governor's pleasure (Article 164(1)).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The tenure of Jammu and Kashmir’s Chief Minister is:—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                J&K Chief Minister's tenure → earlier 6 years (Assembly term), not fixed, lasts while he has majority; J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 fixed Assembly term at 5 years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                First CM of Madhya Pradesh → Pt. Ravishankar Shukla (1 November to 31 December 1956); State executive: Articles 153 to 167, Part VI.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Who among the following Chief Ministers of Madhya Pradesh has not held the office of the leader of the house in Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly during his tenure?Govind Narayan Singh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Govind Narayan Singh (fifth CM of Madhya Pradesh) → never Leader of the House in MP Legislative Assembly during his tenure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The main force forming the principles of the procedure for the work of State Government is:Secretariat

                                                                                                                                                                                                                State Secretariat → apex wing of State administration; main force forming the principles of procedure for State Government's work.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Chief Secretary → chosen by Chief Minister, appointed by Governor; head of the State's administrative machinery; has no fixed tenure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • In the administration of the State Secretariat every file have to be sent to the Cabinet through?Chief Secretary

                                                                                                                                                                                                                In the State Secretariat, every file goes to the Cabinet through the Chief Secretary.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                • After the Ayodhya incident in 1992, Vidhan Sabha in some States was dissolved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 After Ayodhya incident (1992), Assemblies of UP, MP, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan were dissolved; Bihar's was not (it came under President's rule in 1995).
