                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Emergency Provisions: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Emergency provisions are contained in Part XVIII of the Constitution from Articles 352 to 360. These provisions enable the Central Government to meet any abnormal situations effectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Constitution stipulates three types of emergencies –

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  (i) An emergency due to war, external aggression or armed rebellion (Art. -352).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  (ii) An Emergency due to failure of Constitutional machinery in the state (Art. - 356).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  (iii) Financial Emergency due to a threat to the financial stability or credit of India (Art. - 360).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • During an Emergency, the Central government becomes all powerful and the executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to any State as to the manner in which the executive power of the State is to be exercised.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under Article 352, the President can declare a national emergency when the security of India or a part of it is threatened by war or external aggression or armed rebellion.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Proclamation of Emergency must be approved by both the Houses of Parliament by the special majority required by Article 352(6) within one month from the date of its issue.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If the proclamation of emergency is issued at a time when the Lok Sabha has been dissolved or the dissolution of the Lok Sabha takes place during the period of1 month without approving the proclamation, then the proclamation survives for 30 days from the first sitting of the Lok Sabha after its reconstitution and ceases unless Lok Sabha also approves it within those 30 days, provided that the Rajya Sabha has in the meantime approved it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If approved by both the Houses of Parliament the emergency continues for 6 months from the date of passing of the Second approving resolution and may be extended for further six-month periods by resolutions of both Houses passed with the special majority under Article 352 (6).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • During a National Emergency, the Parliament becomes empowered to make laws on any subject mentioned in the State list.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The laws made by Parliament on State subjects become inoperative six months after the emergency has ceased to operate. The President can issue an ordinance on state subjects also, if the Parliament is not in session.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 354 (1) while the proclamation of National Emergency is in operation, the President can modify the Constitutional distribution of revenues between the Centre and the States. This modification operates only for a period not extending beyond the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases, and every such order must be laid before each House of Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 83 (2), while a proclamation of National Emergency is in place, the life of the Lok Sabha may be extended beyond its normal term (5 years) by a law of Parliament for one year at a time (for any number of times).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • However this extension cannot continue beyond a period of six months, after the emergency has ceased to operate.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Articles 358 and 359 describe the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights. Article 358 deals with the suspension of enforcement of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Article 19 due to war or external aggression. No separate order for their suspension is required.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 359 deals with the suspension of enforcement of other Fundamental Rights (Except those guaranteed by Articles 20 & 21).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 359 authorises the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The National Emergency has been proclaimed 3 times so far – in 1962, 1971 and 1975.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The President Rule under Article 356 is imposed in case of failure of the Constitutional machinery in the State.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Notably in the case of the President’s Rule the President can act either on a report of the Governor or otherwise too (i.e even without the Governor's report).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under this arrangement the President may acquire all or any of the powers of the state government concerned.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The President (actually on behalf of him, the Governor)dismisses the state council of ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • During this time the Parliament passes the state legislative bills and the state budget.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A Proclamation imposing Presidential Rule must be approved by both the Houses of the Parliament within two months from the date of its issue.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If approved by both the Houses of the Parliament the President's rule continues for 6 months.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • It can be extended for a maximum period of 3 years with the approval of the Parliament, every six months.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Every resolution approving the proclamation of President’s Rule or its continuance can be passed by either house of the Parliament only by a simple majority. For any extension beyond 1 year, Article 356(5) imposes conditions that must also be met: a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission of India certifies difficulty in holding State Legislative Assembly elections.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 360 of the Indian Constitution deals with Financial Emergency.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency ifhe is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A proclamation of financial emergency must be approved by both the Houses of Parliament within two months from the date of its issue.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Once approved by both the Houses of the Parliament, the financial emergency continues indefinitely till it is revoked.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • During a financial emergency, the centre acquires full direction-based control over the States in financial matters.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No financial emergency has been declared so far.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • K.M. Nambiar, while criticising the emergency powers of the President, called it is “ a fraud on the Constitution.”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The phrase ‘armed rebellion’ was inserted by the 44th Amendment Act of1978, replacing the original phrase ‘internal disturbance.’
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 355, it is the Duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbances and to ensure that the Government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The Finance Commission: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Article 280 of the Constitution provides for a Finance Commission which is constituted by the President of India every fifth year or at an earlier time that he considers necessary.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Finance Commission is required to make recommendations regarding the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and States, the allocation between the States of the respective shares and the principle that should govern the grants-in-aid to the States by the Centre, measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities and any other matter referred by the President in the interest of sound finance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • First Finance Commission was constituted vide presidential order dated 22 November, 1951 under the chairmanship of Shri K.C. Neogy on 6th April, 1952.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The chairman of the 14th Finance Commission was Shri Y.V. Reddy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • 14th Finance Commission recommended an increase in the share of states in the net proceeds of taxes to 42 percent from the then existing 32 percent.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The recommendations of the 14th Finance Commission were enforced for the period of five years (2015-20).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The 15th Finance Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of N.K. Singh.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The tenure for the enforcement of recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission was from the year 2020-21 to the year 2025-26 but the commission submitted two reports - the first report consisted of recommendations for the financial year 2020-21 and the final report with recommendations for 2021-26.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31st December, 2023 under Arvind Panagariya former Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The State Finance Commission is a constitutional body.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Finance Commission constituted under Article 280(1) consists of a chairman and four other members appointed by the president.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • How many types of emergencies have been envisaged under the Indian Constitution?Three

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Three emergencies → National Emergency (Art 352), President's Rule on failure of state constitutional machinery (Art 356), Financial Emergency (Art 360).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 352, 356, 360 → Nation, State, Money: each four apart.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under which Article of the Constitution it is the responsibility of the Indian Government to protect States from external aggression and internal disturbance?Article 355

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art 355 → Union's duty to protect States from external aggression and internal disturbance; Art 352 → National Emergency. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Art 355 (Union's duty to protect States) with Art 356 (President's Rule).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The President of India may declare the National Emergency if there is the threat of:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Emergency (Art 352) grounds → war, external aggression, armed rebellion; 'internal disturbance' replaced by 'armed rebellion' (44th Amendment, 1978). Communal clashes not a ground. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under which of the following circumstances can the President declare Emergency?1, 3, and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President can declare Emergency for external aggression (Art 352), failure of state constitutional machinery (Art 356) and financial crisis (Art 360); internal disturbance no longer a ground. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under whose advice can the President of India declare Emergency under Article 352?Union Cabinet

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Emergency (Art 352) → President acts only on Union Cabinet's decision communicated in writing [Art 352(3)].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Not 'Prime Minister' or 'Council of Ministers': the written advice must come from the Union Cabinet.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A: Art 352 deals with declaring Emergency (true). R: emergency can arise any time, even on imminent danger (true), but R does not explain A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation of Emergency?Article 352

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Proclamation of (National) Emergency → Article 352 (war, external aggression, armed rebellion, or imminent danger); Art 356 → failure of constitutional machinery in a state.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • What is correct about external emergency as per Article 352?i iii v vi

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Emergency (Art 352) → proclaimed by President; approved by Parliament within 1 month (earlier two months, cut by 44th Amendment 1978); special majority (2/3); revoked by simple majority.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is the time limit for the ratification of an Emergency period by the Parliament?1 month

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Emergency proclamation (Art 352) → must be approved by both Houses within one month, or it ceases to operate. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Provisions regarding division of taxes between the Union and the States –Can be suspended during National Emergency

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Tax-sharing provisions (Arts 268 to 281) → President's order can suspend or modify them during National Emergency [Art 354(1)].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under which of the following articles the President of India can suspend the enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20, 21)?Article 359

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art 359 → President can suspend enforcement of Fundamental Rights except Arts 20 and 21. Art 358 → Art 19 suspended on war or external aggression (after 44th Amendment).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Art 358 (Art 19 suspended automatically) with Art 359 (President's order suspending enforcement of FRs).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The President of India has the power to suspend the—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Emergency → Art 19 auto-suspended (Art 358, war/external aggression); President can suspend other FRs incl. Art 21A (Art 359); Arts 20 and 21 never suspended. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • During National Emergency the term of the House of People –Can be extended till Emergency lasts but only by one year at a time.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  During National Emergency, Lok Sabha term → extendable by Parliament by law, one year at a time, not beyond six months after Emergency ends [Art 83(2)].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The term of a State Legislative Assembly can be extended during Emergency by–The Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  During Emergency, State Legislative Assembly term → extended by Parliament by law [Art 172(1)], one year at a time, up to six months after Emergency ends.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • On which of the following dates President of India, using his powers, declared by proclamation that a grave emergency existed where the security of India was threatened by internal disturbance?25 June, 1975

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Emergency on 'internal disturbance' → 25 June 1975 by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed (Art 352); withdrawn 21 March 1977; 44th Amendment 1978 replaced it with 'armed rebellion'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Statement: Constitution of India is basically Federal in nature.The statement is correct, but Reason is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Indian Constitution → federal with unitary elements (statement true). Failure of state constitutional machinery → Art 356, not Art 352 (reason false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Art 352 (National Emergency) with Art 356 (President's Rule in a State).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Mainly on whose advice the President’s Rule is imposed in the State?Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule in a State → Article 356; imposed mainly on the Governor's report, though the President can act otherwise too.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In which of the following States there is no provision for the imposition of Governor’s Rule?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Governor's Rule → only in old Jammu and Kashmir (Section 92 of its own Constitution; Art 370 status), besides President's Rule (Art 356). Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya had none.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular State, thenThe powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule (Art 356) → State Legislature's powers exercised by or under authority of Parliament; Assembly suspended or dissolved, not automatically dissolved; Fundamental Rights (Art 19) unaffected.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State?1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule → State Council of Ministers is removed; dissolution of the Assembly and of local bodies are not necessary consequences (Assembly may be suspended).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements regarding Article 356 of the Constitution:(i), (ii), and (iv) only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994) → Art 356 proclamation open to judicial review; failure must be real; Assembly not dissolved until both Houses approve within two months.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • President’s Rule can be imposed for a maximum period of –3 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule → maximum three years by successive Parliament resolutions; beyond one year only if National Emergency operates and Election Commission certifies polls impossible (44th Amendment, 1978).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer from the codes given below:(ii) (iii) (i) (iv)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule imposed till 2019 → Manipur 10, Uttar Pradesh 9, Bihar 8, Odisha 6 times.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid M-U-B count down 10-9-8, then Odisha 6.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under Article 356 of the Constitution of India, President’s Rule was imposed for the first time in –PEPSU

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  President's Rule (Art 356) → first used in Punjab in 1951; then PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) in 1953, the earliest among the options.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements in respect of financial emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution of India:1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Financial Emergency (Art 360) → lapses after 2 months unless both Houses approve; President can order salary cuts for Union and State staff, including Supreme Court and High Court judges.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Statement 2 was wrong only because it excluded the judges; their salaries can also be cut.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is/are the consequence (s) of invoking Article 360, declaration of a financial emergency?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Financial Emergency (Art 360) → President can order salary cuts for State employees and Union employees incl. SC/HC judges; State money bills reserved for President only if he so directs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has not so far been used?Article 360

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Article 360 (Financial Emergency) → never used so far; Articles 352 and 356 have been used. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Art 360, like 360 degrees, brings you back to zero: zero uses.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • How many times has Financial Emergency been declared in India so far?Never

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Financial Emergency (Art 360) → never declared in India so far.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who said, “The emergency power of the President is a fraud with the Constitution”?K.M. Nambiar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  "Emergency power of the President is a fraud with the Constitution" → K.M. Nambiar, while opposing President's Rule provisions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Generally, in India Finance Commission is appointed for every five years-To determine the share of the States in the grants and revenues of the Central Government.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission (Art 280) → set up by President every fifth year; recommends sharing of net tax proceeds between Union and States; first one 6 April 1952 under K.C. Neogy. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following recommends the principles for sharing of revenues among the Union and the States?Finance Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Principles for sharing revenue between Union and States → Finance Commission, constituted every 5 years. Inter-State Council → coordination; Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) → resource allocation. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Given below are two statements one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R):(A) is false, but (R) is true

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Qualifications of Finance Commission members → fixed by Parliament (Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951), not the President (A false); President appoints Chairman and members (R true).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who among the following determines the qualification which shall be requisite for appointment as member of the finance commission?Parliament by Act

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Qualifications and manner of selection of Finance Commission members → determined by Parliament by law [Art 280(2)].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse President appoints the members, but Parliament fixes their qualifications.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • With reference to Union Finance Commission, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Neither (1) nor (2)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission → Chairman + four other members (not six); reports to the President [Art 280(3)], not to NITI Aayog → neither statement correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements: The function (s) of the Finance Commission is/are –2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission → divides net tax proceeds among States; sets principles for grants-in-aid. Not its job: withdrawal from Consolidated Fund (Parliament) or checking tax collection (Finance Ministry). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • With reference to the Finance Commission of India, which of the following statements is correct?None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct in this context.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission [Art 280(3)] → tax sharing, grants-in-aid (Art 275), funds for Panchayats and municipalities, matters referred by President; not foreign capital, PSU finances or transparency.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Federal Finance Commission in India relates to –Finances between States and the Centre

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Federal Finance Commission → finances between the Centre and the States; it recommends distribution of finance between Union and States. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who was the Chairman of the Twelfth Finance Commission?C. Rangarajan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  12th Finance Commission (2005 to 2010) → Dr. C. Rangarajan, former RBI Governor. 13th → Vijay Kelkar; 14th (2015-2020) → Y.V. Reddy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 12th → Rangarajan, the RBI Governor: R for Rangarajan and Reserve Bank.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • After the commencement of the Constitution how many Finance Commissions have been constituted?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission chairmen: 13th → Vijay Kelkar; 14th → Y.V. Reddy (formed January 2013); 15th → N.K. Singh (constituted 27 November 2017). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who has been nominated as the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission.N.K. Singh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  15th Finance Commission → Chairman N.K. Singh; constituted 27 November 2017 under Art 280; two reports: for 2020-21 and for 2021-26.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman andFour other members

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Finance Commission → a Chairman and four other members [Art 280(1)], appointed by the President.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 1 + 4 = a five-member body, set up every five years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who of the following shall causes every recommendation made by the Finance Commission to be laid before each House of the Parliament?The President of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Article 281 → the President causes every Finance Commission recommendation to be laid before each House of Parliament.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:(A) is true, but (R) is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  State Finance Commission → constitutional (Art 243-I; set up by Governor every fifth year; Seventy-Third Amendment, 1992) (A true). Union Finance Commission does cover Panchayats [Art 280(3)(bb)] (R false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following statements about a State Finance Commission is true?It is a Constitutional body.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  State Finance Commission → a constitutional body, constituted by the Governor under Article 243-I. Must know
