                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Lokpal and Important Commissions · part 2 of 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    51 facts · 57 questions · 6 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • A Sitting Judge of the High Court or a Sitting District Judge can be appointed as a member of the State Human Rights Commission after consultation with?the Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Sitting High Court Judge or sitting District Judge → made SHRC member only after consulting the Chief Justice of that State's High Court.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • In the event of occurrence of any vacancy in the Office of the Chairperson of the State Commission, who can authorize one of the members to act as Chairperson?The Governor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Vacancy or absence of SHRC Chairperson → Governor authorises one member to act as Chairperson.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Analyze the statements with reference to National Human Rights Commission:Both Statements (i) and (ii) are true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    NHRC functions (Section 12, Act 1993) → promote research in human rights and encourage NGOs working in the field; both statements true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is not the function of the State Human Rights Commission?To punish for the violation of Human Rights

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    State Human Rights Commission → can inquire suo motu, visit jails, review human-rights protection; cannot punish violators.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Human Rights Commissions only recommend; they have no power to punish.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The State Commission submits its annual report to the?State Government

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    SHRC annual report → to the State Government; laid before State Legislature with action-taken memorandum and reasons for non-acceptance.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Not the Governor: SHRC reports go to the State Government.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Every member of the Commission, Sate Commission and every officer appointed or authorized by the Commission or State Commission to exercise functions under the Protection of Human Rights Act is to be deemedPublic Servant

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Members and officers of NHRC/SHRC acting under Protection of Human Rights Act → deemed Public Servants (Section 21 IPC).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • An advocate may be specified by the State Government for the purpose of conducting of cases in Human Rights courts as Special Public Prosecutor who has been in practice for not less than:Seven years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court → advocate with at least 7 years' practice, specified by State Government (Section 31, Act 1993).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • In relation to offences described under Section 175, Section 178, Section 179, Section 180 or Section 228 of the Indian Penal Code, the Human Rights Commission is to be deemedCivil Court

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    For offences under IPC Sections 175, 178, 179, 180 and 228 → Human Rights Commission deemed a Civil Court; it has all powers of a civil court.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • While dealing with complaints of violation of Human Rights by the members of the armed forces, the Commission either on its own motion or on receipt of a petition will?seek a report from the Central Government

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Human rights complaints against armed forces → Commission only seeks a report from the Central Government and makes recommendations (limited role).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Articles 369 to 392 in Part XXI of the Constitution deal with the temporary, transitional and special provisions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Article 370 was related to the temporary provisions of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The State of Jammu and Kashmir had its own separate Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir was adopted on 17 November 1956 and came into force on 26 January, 1957.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The State of Jammu and Kashmir was excluded from the Article 152 of the Chapter 1 of Part VI (provision related to states) in which the definition of state is provided. Article 370, granting temporary special provision to the state of Jammu and Kashmir, was declared inoperative through a notification issued by the President on the recommendation of the Parliament on 6 August, 2019. The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019 bifurcates the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two union territories (Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The states of Maharashtra and Gujarat are given special provisions under Article 371.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Nagaland under Article 371 A, Assam under Article 371 B, Manipur under Article 371 C, Andhra Pradesh/Telangana under Article 371D, Sikkim under Article 371 F, Mizoram under Article 371 G, Arunachal Pradesh under Article 371 H, Goa under Article 371 I and Karnataka under Article 371 J are granted special provisions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Election Commission: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Articles 324 to 329 in Part XV of the Constitution deal with the provisions related to the electoral system.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to Article 324, there shall be an election commission, which is a permanent and independent body.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • This commission is responsible for superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Parliament, the Legislature of every State, the President and the Vice-President.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The election commission consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners (the number being decided by the President from time to time) [Art. 324(2)]. The Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners are appointed by the president.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Till 15 October, 1989 there was only a Chief Election Commissioner, but on 16 October, 1989 two additional election commissioners were appointed for the first time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • But these posts were in effect upto the 1st of January 1990.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • On 1st October 1993, again two additional election commissioners were appointed and since then the election commission has three members. At present, there are two Election Commissioners and one Chief Election Commissioner in the Election Commission. They have equal power and their salary and perks are the same as those of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Their tenure is for 6 years or up to the age of 65 years (whichever is earlier).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The chief election commissioner can be removed from his office only in a manner and on the grounds prescribed for the removal of Judges of the Supreme Court [Article 324(5)].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Other Election Commissioner or the Regional Commissioner can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The notifications for the elections to the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are issued by the President and for the state legislative assemblies by the Governor.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Article 326 mentions the provision of Adult Suffrage. The right to vote in India is a Statutory Right.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • As per the Representation of the People Act 1951, there is right to vote and to be elected in India.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The age for the right to vote was decreased from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act 1988 which came into effect from 28 March 1989.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The elections to the local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) is being conducted by the State Election Commissions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Delimitation Commission is a commission established by the Government of India. Its main task is to redraw the boundaries of various assemblies and lok sabha constituencies based on the recent census. Till now, the Delimitation commission has been set up for five times (1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002) and the latest in March 2020. The March 2020, Delimitation Commission was constituted via notification for delimitation of the UT of Jammu & Kashmir.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with special provisions with respect to different States?Art. 371

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Special provisions for different States → Articles 371 to 371-J (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The status of the Chief Election Commissioner of India is equal to the –—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Chief Election Commissioner → ranks 9(A) in Table of Precedence, with UPSC Chairperson and CAG. CJI and Lok Sabha Speaker → 6th; Governor → 4th.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Given below are two statements:Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Elections entrusted to independent Election Commission (Art 324) (A true); CEC removed like SC Judge, other ECs by President with CEC's advice (R true); R doesn't explain A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Election Commissioner can be removed by thePresident on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          An Election Commissioner → removed by the President only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge; other Election Commissioners only on CEC's recommendation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The functions of Election Commission of India are-I, II and IV

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Election Commission [Art 324(1)] → electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, Vice-President; it does not recommend President's Rule or make election laws. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following elections is not conducted by the Election Commission?Local bodies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Local body (Panchayat, municipality) elections → State Election Commission (Arts 243K, 243ZA), not the Election Commission of India.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following are the functions of the Election Commissioner of India?None of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Not ECI's work: electing Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman (done by House members); municipal polls (State Election Commission, Art 243ZA); election disputes (judiciary) → none. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ECI → three-member body (CEC + two ECs), not five; ECI (not Home Ministry) fixes election schedules; ECI resolves split/merger disputes of recognised parties → only 3 true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is not related to Election Commission?To issue notification of election

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Election notification → issued by President (Parliament) and Governor (State Legislature), not by Election Commission; EC allots symbols and conducts polls.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is correct in respect of the commencement of the election process in India?The recommendation for election is made by the Election Commission, and the notification for election is issued by the President and Governors of the States concerned.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Start of election process → Election Commission recommends; President or Governor issues notification; then EC announces dates and timings.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the election system have been adopted for different elections in India?1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Election systems in India → direct election on adult suffrage (Lok Sabha, Assemblies) and proportional representation by single transferable vote (President, VP, Rajya Sabha, Councils); no list or cumulative system.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who decides disputes regarding disqualification of Members of Parliament?The President in consultation with the Election Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Disqualification of MPs → decided by the President after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion and acting on it (Article 103). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Under Article 103 of the Constitution of India, the President shall obtain the opinion of which of the following authority before giving any decision on any question regarding the disqualification of the members of the Lok Sabha?Election Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Article 103 → before deciding disqualification of an MP [Art 102(1) grounds], the President must obtain the Election Commission's opinion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If in an election to a State Legislative Assembly the candidate who is declared elected loses his deposit, it means that –A very large number of candidates contested.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Winner losing his deposit → a very large number of candidates contested; deposit is lost if a candidate gets no more than one-sixth of valid votes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The decision to disqualify the person declared convict by the Court to contest the elections has been made by-The Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Disqualification of convicted persons → by Parliament: Section 8(3), RPA 1951: jailed 2 years or more → disqualified from conviction until 6 years after release.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Given below are two statements:(A) is true but (R) is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Model Code of Conduct → applies once Election Commission announces schedule (A true); framed by Election Commission, not enacted by Parliament (R false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Right to Vote and to be Elected in India is a-Legal Right

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Right to vote and to be elected in India → a legal right (not fundamental, constitutional or natural). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Right to Vote and Right to be elected in India is a –Legal Right under an Act

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Right to vote and right to be elected → legal rights under an Act (ordinary law), not Fundamental or Constitutional Rights.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Right to Vote in India is aLegal Right

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Right to vote → merely a statutory (legal) right; Kuldip Nayar vs Union of India: neither fundamental nor constitutional right.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Don't pick 'Constitutional Right': the Court called voting a statutory right.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Voting right by the youths at the age of 18 years was exercised for the first time in the General Election of1989

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Voting age 21 → 18 by 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force 28 March 1989); first used in the November 1989 Lok Sabha general election. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Law in 1988, first vote in 1989.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 9 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In which article of the constitution the Adult Suffrage is recognised?Article 326

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Adult suffrage → Article 326: elections to Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides right to vote i.e. adult suffrage for electing representatives of Lok Saba and Vidhan Sabha?Article 326

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Right to vote (adult suffrage) for electing Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha → Article 326.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the Law enacted by Parliament in December 1989, the legal age for a citizen to become major is:18 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Voting age → 18 years: 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Art 326 (from 21); Representation of the People Act, 1951 amended too.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the eligibility age, after the changes made in March 2024, for senior citizens to vote by postal ballot?85 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Postal ballot from home for senior citizens → age raised from 80 to 85 years (Rule 27A, Conduct of Elections Rules 1961, amended 1 March 2024); also 40% disabled.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Principles for election to the State Legislatures include:All the four

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          State Legislature elections → adult suffrage; one electoral roll per territorial constituency; no bar of religion, race, sex on roll; parties free to have norms → all four.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If 'One Nation One Election' is to be realized in India, which Article of the Indian Constitution will require an amendment?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          'One Nation One Election' → needs amendment of Articles 83, 85, 172, 174 and 356 → more than one option.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who among the following is not a member of a high level committee constituted on simultaneous elections?Sri Tushar Mehta

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Simultaneous Elections committee (2 September 2023) → chair Ram Nath Kovind; members incl. Amit Shah, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap, Harish Salve; Niten Chandra Secretary; Tushar Mehta not on it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following statements regarding Exit Poll is correct?Exit Poll is a term used to denote a post-election survey of voters regarding the candidates in whose favour they had exercised their franchise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Exit Poll → survey of voters after voting on whom they voted for. Opinion Poll → survey before the election.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Exit poll (after voting) with opinion poll (before the election).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the total number of electors in Lok Sabha elections of 2009 in Million ?(1 million = 10 Lakh).714

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha elections 2009 → total electors 714 million.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          RPA 1951 (Section 33) → max two Lok Sabha constituencies (1 false). Devi Lal contested three in 1991 (2 true). No rule makes party pay bypoll costs (3 false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements about the recent amendments to the elections law by the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act 1996.1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          RPA (Amendment) Act 1996 → insulting National Flag/Constitution: six-year disqualification; higher security deposit; no countermanding on a candidate's death; max two constituencies, not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Statement 3 was wrong: the limit is two constituencies, not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended:Government funding of parliamentary elections

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Dinesh Goswami Committee (electoral reforms; Goswami was Law Minister, 1989) → recommended government funding of parliamentary elections; basis of RPA Amendment, 1996.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Read the following statements in relation to reservation of seats in Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly, and choose the correct option:Statement I and III are false, but Statement II is true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha → 84 SC and 47 ST seats of 543 (Delimitation 2008), not 44 ST. Delimitation Commission picks reserved seats; Central Government constitutes it, not Speaker.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to the Delimitation Commission, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Delimitation Commission orders → cannot be challenged in court; laid before Lok Sabha or State Assembly but cannot be modified → both true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023?Four

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Delimitation Commissions under Delimitation Acts → four: 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002; the 2020 one (J&K and NE States) is technically a fifth.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Proportional representation → represents all groups (ethnicity, gender, interests, ideologies), so it eases minority representation; A and R true, R explains A.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           • Proportional representation is not necessary for a country where:a two-party system has developed

Course of action:Neither (I) nor (II) follow.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lower turnout than last time → neither re-election nor cancelling non-voters' rights follows; voting is a statutory right and EC uses awareness campaigns.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following Election Reforms in India and arrange them in correct chronological order starting from earliest to the last.2, 1, 3, 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Order → EVM (19 May 1982, Parur, Kerala) → Voter photo ID card (1993) → VVPAT (4 September 2013, Nagaland) → NOTA (SC order 27 September 2013).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the version of the machine VVPAT used for voting in India?M3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          VVPAT/EVM version used in India → M3, third-generation; holds data of 384 candidates; tamper detection and self-diagnostics.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Election Commission was converted into a ‘Three members Commission’ in the following year:1989

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Election Commission first made three-member in 1989 (two extra ECs, 16 October 1989 to 1 January 1990); three members again since 1 October 1993.

Lohani

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Not an ECI member → N.B. Ramadevi → both statements correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          First woman Chief Election Commissioner → V.S.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           National Voters' Day → 25 January (Election Commission's foundation day), celebrated since 25 January 2011 to draw young voters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Political Parties: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Party system is a part of the political system.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Formation and working of the government in the Democratic political system is done with the help of the Party system.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Under the Representation of the People Act 1951, there is a provision for the registration of political parties.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Election Commission of India registers the Political Parties.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • By the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985, Political Parties, for the first time, were given the Constitutional status. This Act came into force on 1 March, 1985.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Tenth Schedule which is related to the Anti-defection law, was added to the Indian Constitution by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Internal party democracy is used for internal elections in the political parties.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • It occurs periodically to elect the officials of the political parties.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Election Commission is empowered to grant status to different political parties as national and state parties.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Presently 6 political parties are recognised as National-level parties in our country.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • These are Indian National Congress (INC), Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Bahujan Samaj Party, Communist Party of India - Marxist (CPI-M), Aam Aadmi Party and National People's Party.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • In India, elections are held on the basis of Universal Adult Franchise.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Political parties have the freedom to establish their own standards, subject to mandatory legal/registration conditions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 and its first president was W.C. Banerjee.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The word 'National' in Indian National Congress reflects its all-India character and intent to speak for people across India, it was also influenced by the reaction against British Rule.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Bharatiya Janata Party was founded in 1980 and its first president was Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Independent Labour Party was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1936.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Communist Party of India was found ed in 1925 and C.P.I. (Marxist) was founded in 1964.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements regarding the political parties in India:1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Parties registered under RPA 1951 by Election Commission; National party → recognised in four or more states (among other tests); 1999 polls: six national, 48 state parties → all correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Who is empowered to recognize various political parties in India as National or Regional Parties?The Election Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Recognition as National or State party → Election Commission, under Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Who recognises the political parties in India?Election Commission of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Political parties are registered and recognised by the Election Commission of India (Election Symbols Order, 1968).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • A party gets recognition as a national party when –—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                National party → any one: 2% Lok Sabha seats from three states; or 6% votes in four states + four Lok Sabha seats; or State party in four states. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • A political party is recognized as a regional party, ifIt gets 8% votes in the State either in Lok Sabha or the Assembly election.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                State party (Symbols Order 1968) → any one: 3 Assembly seats or 3%; 1 Lok Sabha seat per 25; 6% votes + seats; or 8% of total State votes. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Don't confuse UPPSC's key said 'None of the above'; the book holds 8% (option c).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The word ‘National’ in Indian National Congress was influenced by-Reaction against British rule

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                'National' in the name Indian National Congress → influenced by reaction against British rule.

Sangma, Tariq Anwar after expulsion from Congress over Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin.
