                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Constitutional Amendment: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Any constitution, even ifit is made wisely, needs amendments in time and circumstances.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Indian Constitution is a mixture of rigidity and flexibility.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • It contains the provision of Amendments in Article 368 of Part-XX of the Indian Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Indian Constitution can be amended in three different ways.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1.Simple majority
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2.Special majority
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3.Special majority and by the ratification of not less
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • than one-half of the state legislatures. A Constitutional Amendment bill can be introduced in either House of the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Constitutional Amendment bill needs to be passed by both the Houses of the Parliament separately with a special majority and there is no provision for the joint sitting of the Houses for the Constitutional Amendment bill.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Election of President, Representation of States in the Parliament, Supreme and High Court, power of Parliament to amend the constitution etc, are the subjects that require a special majority of the Parliament and ratification by at least half of the state legislatures for the Amendment.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Any amendment in the provision of the Constitution by a simple majority in both the Houses is not included in the amendment under Article 368.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • These include the provisions regarding admission or establishment of new states, alteration of names, areas, boundaries, etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 added two new Articles i.e. Article 31A and 31B and also the 9th Schedule.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is known as a mini-constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 52nd Amendment Act is related to the Anti-defection law.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 61st Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 69th Amendment Act, 1991 gave Delhi the status of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 21A, i.e. Right to Education, Provision for Free and compulsory education for children from the age of 6 years to 14 years.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 amended Articles 75 and 164 and Schedule 10.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • It inserted a new Article 361B.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • This Amendment restricts the size of the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • That cannot be more than 15% of the total number of members of the House of the People at the Union level and the total number of members of the state legislative assembly at the level of the State.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 97th Amendment Act 2011 gave constitutional status to the co-operative societies (Part IX B inserted by the 97th Amendment is now operative only for multi-State Co-operative Societies).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 100th Constitutional Amendment Act is related to the India-Bangladesh boundary st
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • treaty.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • 101 Amendment Act is related to the GST (Goods and Services Tax). The National Commission for Backward Classes has been given constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment Act. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 deals with providing 10 percent reservation in government Jobs and education to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of citizens. This EWS category includes citizens other than the classes mentioned in clauses (4) and (5) of Article 15 and clause (4) of Article 16.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Doctrine of basic structure of the Constitution refers to the features of the Constitution which are inviolable and cannot be amended or altered by the Parliament.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The doctrine of basic structure was given by the Supreme Court in the famous Keshavananda Bharati case of 1973. The 105th Constitutional amendment amends clauses 1 and 2 of Article 342A and also introduces a new clause 3. It also amends Articles 366 (26C) and 338B(9). It is designed to clarify that states can maintain the 'state list' of OBCs. The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 is the Latest amendment in the Indian Constitution. It reserves one third of all seats for women in Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, including those reserved for SCs and STs. This reservation for women shall come into effect after the next delimitation exercise following the first census conducted after the Act's commencement, and shall remain in effect for 15 years from such commencement.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Assertion (A): Under Article 368, the Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution.Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Art 368 → Parliament can amend any part by addition, variation or repeal, except basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973); Parliament is supreme elected body → R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Article 368(1) → Parliament may amend any provision by addition, variation or repeal → all three.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid Amend = A-V-R: Add, Vary, Repeal.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following Bills must be passed by each House of the Indian Parliament separately by the special majority?Constitution Amendment Bill

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Constitution Amendment Bill (Article 368) → must be passed by each House separately by special majority, then presented to the President for assent. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Amendments to the Constitution may be initiated-Either House of the Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Amendment Bill → introduced in either House of Parliament [Art 368(2)], not in State legislatures; special majority in each House; procedure taken from South Africa. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Under the provisions of the Article 368(2) of the Constitution of India, If a bill comes to Rajasthan Legislative Assembly after passing by parliament of India for resolution to rectify, then (A) Resolution can be passed by Assembly. (B) Resolution can be rejected by Assembly. (C) No Amendment shall be proposed to such a reso lation Select the correct answer using code given below: Code -(A), (B) and (C)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Amendment sent to States for ratification [Art 368(2)] → a State Assembly may pass or reject the resolution but cannot propose amendments to it → all three.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to the Indian Constitution, the Constitutional amendment of the following topics requires consent of at least half of State legislatures1, 2, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Ratification by half the States needed for → federal provisions, Supreme Court and High Courts, Art 368 itself. New States, boundaries, names → simple majority of Parliament. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • An amendment of the Constitution shall require to be ratified by the legislatures of not less than one-half of the states:If such amendment seeks to make changes in Article 279A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Half-States ratification needed for Art 279A (GST Council), also Arts 54, 55, 73, 162, 241, Seventh Schedule lists, States' representation; not Arts 53, 239A, 243A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following subjects underthe Constitution of India: I. List I-Union List, in the Seventh Schedule II. Extent of the executive power of a State III. Conditions of the Governor's office For a constitutional amendment with respect to which of the above, ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States is required before presenting the bill to the President of India for assent?I and II only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Half-States ratification → needed for Union List (Seventh Schedule) and extent of State executive power (Art 162); not for conditions of Governor's office (Art 158).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which is unmatched in the context of Constitutional Amendment Procedure?iv v vi

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Outside the Art 368 State-ratification list → President's qualification, conditions of office and tenure; executive powers, courts, President's election, legislative powers, States' representation are inside.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following Constitution Amendments was the first Constitution Amendment, which was ratified by the State Legislatures according to the requirements of the provision of the Article 368(2) of the Constitution?Third Constitutional Amendment, 1954

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      First amendment ratified by State legislatures under Art 368(2) → Third Amendment, 1954 (re-enacted entry 33 of Concurrent List).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the event of the Upper House rejecting a Constitutional Amendment Bill passed by the Lower HouseThe Bill will have to be dropped

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Rajya Sabha rejects a Constitution Amendment Bill passed by Lok Sabha → Bill is dropped; there is no joint sitting for amendment bills.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Joint sitting applies to ordinary bills, never to Constitution Amendment Bills.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Cooperatives under Art 19(1)(c) → 97th (2011); SC/ST backlog vacancies → 81st (2000); NJAC → 99th (2014, struck down 16 October 2015); Council of Ministers size → 91st (2003).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Match the Amendments with their year of implementation:3 1 4 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      42nd Amendment → 1976; 52nd → 1985; 86th → 2002; 96th → 2011.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts was termed as Mini Constitution?42

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      'Mini Constitution' → 42nd Amendment (1976); it sought to overcome the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) ruling on essential features.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution of India:2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      42nd Amendment (1976) → added 'socialist, secular, integrity' to Preamble and 10 Fundamental Duties (not eight). Incorrect: statements 2 and 3 (the new Directive Principles list).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following Constitutional Amendment is related to the Fundamental Duties?42

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment, 1976 (Swaran Singh Committee); Part IV-A, Art 51A; first 10, now 11; idea from the Soviet Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • What is not true about the 44th Constitutional Amendment?Through this amendment first time it was made clear in Constitution that President cannot act against the advice of Council of Ministers; As per this amendment President can return the advice of Council of Ministers for reconsideration as many times as he want till he is satisfied

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      44th Amendment (1978, Janata Govt) → undid 42nd changes; President can return ministers' advice for reconsideration only once. 42nd had bound President to ministers' advice (Art 74).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      PM's election beyond judicial review → 39th Amendment (1975), undone by 44th (1978): 1 false. SC struck down 99th Amendment (NJAC, 2014) for judicial independence: 2 true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which Constitutional Amendment Act dealing with National Judicial Appointments Commission, was declared unconstitutional by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court?99th Constitutional Amendment Act

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014 → National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC); struck down by a five-judge Constitution Bench on October 15, 2015 to protect judicial independence.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following has banned floor crossing by the member elected on a party ticket to the legislature?52nd Constitutional Amendment Act

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      52nd Amendment Act, 1985 → Anti-Defection Law (ban on floor crossing); added the 10th Schedule; later amended by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse 52nd (1985, brought anti-defection law) with 91st (2003, which only amended it).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The authoritative text of the Indian Constitution in Hindi was authorized to be published by which of the following constitutional amendments?58th Amendment, 1987

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      58th Amendment Act, 1987 → authorised publication of the authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution, with all later amendments.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following Amendments to the Constitution is related to the Lowering of the age of voters?61 Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      61st Amendment Act, 1988 → voting age lowered from 21 to 18 years; came into force on March 28, 1989.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which Constitution Amendment Act reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?61st Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      61st Amendment → voting age for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections cut from 21 years to 18 years.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             • By Which one of the following Constitutional Amendments Delhi became ‘National Capital Region’?69th Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            69th Amendment Act, 1991 → Delhi got the status of National Capital Territory (NCT). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The 79 Amendment of the Indian Constitution is related to –Reservation of SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            79th Amendment (1999) → extended SC/ST and Anglo-Indian seat reservation in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by 10 years; 95th Amendment (2009) extended it another 10 years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The 93rd Constitution Amendment Bill deals with the:Free and compulsory education for all children between the age of 6 and 14 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            93rd Amendment Bill → free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14; enacted as the 86th Amendment: added Art 21-A, amended Art 45, added Art 51-A(k).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Bill number and Act number differ: the 93rd Bill became the 86th Amendment Act.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • ‘Right to Education’ introduced through 86 Amendment came into force:In 2010

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            86th Amendment Act, 2002 → Art 21A (Right to Education); RTE Act passed 2009; both came into force on 1 April 2010. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Three dates: amendment 2002, RTE Act 2009, in force 2010 — 'came into force' means 2010.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which Amendment to the Constitution inserted a new Article 21 A in the Constitution providing Right to Education?86th Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            86th Amendment Act, 2002 → new Article 21-A: free and compulsory education for all children aged 6-14 as a Fundamental Right. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Memory aid 21-A sits right after Art 21 (life): education grows out of the right to life.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements about ‘Right to Education’ and choose the correct answer:Only 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Right to Education aims at 'Education for All'; earlier only a DPSP in Part IV (Art 45); became a Fundamental Right (Art 21A) by the Eighty-sixth, not 91st, Amendment, 2002.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which Constitutional Amendment bifurcated the Combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate bodies?89th Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            89th Amendment Act, 2003 → split the combined SC-ST Commission into National Commission for SCs (Art 338) and National Commission for STs (Art 338A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Memory aid 338 = SCs; 338A = STs — the 'A' came later for the second commission.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts seeks that the size of the Councils of Ministers at the Centre and in a State must not exceed 15 percent of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha and the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State, respectively?91

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            91st Amendment Act, 2003 → amended Arts 75 and 164: total ministers (incl. PM/CM) capped at 15% of Lok Sabha / State Assembly strength.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The size of the Council of Ministers was fixed up to 15 percent of the total members of Lok Sabha by which of the following Constitutional Amendments?91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            91st Amendment Act, 2003 → inserted Art 75(1A): Council of Ministers incl. PM not more than 15% of Lok Sabha strength; in force from 1 January 2004.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Option traps: 92nd (2004), 74th (1992), 86th (2002) — the ministry-size cap is only the 91st (2003).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The 91 Amendment of the Indian Constitution providesceiling of the size of Council of Ministers

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            91st Amendment (2003) → ceiling on the size of the Council of Ministers (15% of the House) via Art 75(1A), to strengthen the anti-defection law. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • By which Constitutional Amendment OBCs have been given 27 percent reservation in the admission to educational institutions?93rd

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            93rd Amendment Act (2006) → 27% reservation for OBCs in admission to educational institutions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of2012 is concerned with……….Organization and working of co-operative societies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            97th Amendment (notified 12 January 2012) → cooperative societies: added to Art 19(1)(c), new Art 43B and Part IX-B (Arts 243ZH to 243ZT). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • According to Article 243(ZJ) of the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of directors of a cooperative society can be –21

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Art 243ZJ → board of a cooperative society: number of directors set by State Legislature, but maximum 21.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015 was brought for exchange of territories between India and Bangladesh. What is not true in reference to this?Under this, India transferred 51 enclaves to Bangladesh whereas Bangladesh transferred 111 enclaves to India.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            100th Amendment Act, 2015 → ratified 1974 India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement: India gave 111 enclaves to Bangladesh and got 51; option (a) reverses this.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Don't reverse the numbers: India → Bangladesh 111 enclaves; Bangladesh → India 51.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following constitution (Amendment) Act provides for goods and Services Tax (G.S.T.)?The Constitutions (One Hundred and First)Amendment Act. 2016

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            101st Amendment Act, 2016 → Goods and Services Tax (GST); national GST introduced on 1st July 2017.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            105th Amendment Act, 2021 (assent by President Ram Nath Kovind, 18 August 2021) → States/UTs may keep their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC).

Golak Nath Case II. Keshavanand Bharti Case III. 24th Constitution Amendment Act IV. 42nd Constitution Amendment Act Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes:I, III, II, IV

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Chronology: Golak Nath case (1967) → 24th Amendment (1971) → Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) → 42nd Amendment (1976).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In which of the following cases the Supreme Court limited the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution for the first time?Golaknath Vs.The State of Punjab

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Golaknath vs State of Punjab, 1967 → Supreme Court first limited Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Golaknath (first limit, 1967) with the later Kesavananda Bharati or Minerva Mills cases.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Keshavananda Bharati Case is important because-The Supreme Court interpreted the basic features of the Constitution

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala, 1973 → Basic Structure Doctrine: Parliament may amend even Fundamental Rights under Art 368, but not the basic structure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In which case(s) did the Supreme Court of India give for the first time the doctrine of ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution?Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Basic structure doctrine first given in Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973); it reversed Golak Nath and upheld the 24th Amendment. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Memory aid K for Kesavananda = K for 'Keystone': the basic structure holds up the arch.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The basic structure theory of the Constitution of India implies that –Certain features of the Constitution are so essential to it that they cannot be abrogated.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Basic structure theory → certain features of the Constitution are so essential that they cannot be abrogated even by amendment (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which Amendment of the Constitution provides that no law passed to give effect to Directive Principles of State Policy contained in Articles 39(b) & (c) shall be deemed to be void on the ground that it abridges the rights conferred by Articles 14 and 19?25th Amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            25th Amendment, 1971 → laws giving effect to DPSP Arts 39(b) and (c) cannot be void for abridging Arts 14, 19 (or 31).

Supreme Court has laid down in its verdict in Minerva Mills Case, 1980 that the preference given only to Directive Principles of State Policy mentioned in Article 39(b) and 39(c) over Fundamental Rights mentioned in Articles 14 and 19 is Constitutional.Only II is correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Statement I false: the 42nd Amendment (1976), not 44th, gave DPSP priority over Arts 14, 19. II true: Minerva Mills (1980) kept only Art 39(b), (c) priority.

Raj Narain (1975) → 39th Amendment; Minerva Mills (1980) → 42nd; Kihoto Hollohan (1993) → 52nd; P. Sambamurthy (1987) → 32nd.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment, 2023) → one-third seats for women in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, Delhi Assembly, incl. within SC/ST quota; valid 15 years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Statement 1 is false: it does not take effect from the 18th Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Constitution (98 Amendment) Bill is related to:Constitution of the National Judicial Commission

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Constitution (98th Amendment) Bill → National Judicial Commission; presented by Law Minister Arun Jaitley in the NDA Government.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            101st Amendment Act (2016) → GST: Art 246A (power to make GST law), Art 269A (inter-State GST), Art 279A (GST Council).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            By May 2013, 98 Constitutional Amendments had been made; by January 2020, the 104th.
