                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Official Language

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  19 facts · 22 questions · 4 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Official Language: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Official language is mentioned in Part-XVII (Art. 343- 351) of the Indian Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Art. 343, the official language of the union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script and the digits used for official purposes shall be an international form of Indian numerals.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under Article 344, the president has the power to form a commission related to the official language. According to Article 344, the President shall at the expiration of five years from the Commencement of the Constitution and there after at the expiration often years from such commencement, by order constitute a commission on official language.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The First official language commission under the chairmanship of B.G. Kher was constituted in 1955.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Art. 344 (4), there is a provision to form a 30- member joint parliamentary committee on official language. The committee consists of20 members from Lok Sabha and 10 members from Rajya Sabha.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Any language can be added in the Indian Constitution under the 8th Schedule.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Initially only 14 languages were added to the Indian Constitution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • 'Sindhi' language was added to the Indian Constitution by the 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali were added by 71st Constitutional Amendment Act 1992 in 8th Schedule.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In 2003, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment. At present, a total 22 languages are there in 8th Schedule. According to Article 345, the legislature of a State may by law adopt any one or more of the languages in use in the State or Hindi as the language or languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of that State; till such adoption English language shall continue to be used for official purposes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • There is a description of official language for communication between two states or between a state and the union in Article 346.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 347, there is a special provision relating to language spoken by a section of population of a state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Hindi was accepted by the Constituent Assembly as the official language on 14th September 1949.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • 14 September is celebrated as the Hindi Diwas. According to Article 348 (1)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • (a), all proceedings in the Supreme Court and every High Court shall be done in English language. Under Article 348(2), with the previous consent of the President, the Governor of a State may authorise the use of Hindi or any other language used for any official purposes of the State, in proceedings in the High Court, having its principal seat in that States.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to Article 350 A, there is a provision of facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at primary stage. Article 350B provides for the establishment of a special officer for linguistic minorities. The officer shall be appointed by president and shall investigate all matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities, reporting directly to the President.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Constitution of India initially permitted the use of English language for all official purposes for a period of:15 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art 343(1) → Hindi in Devanagari is the Union's official language; Art 343(2) → English allowed for all official purposes for 15 years from commencement.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which Article of Indian Constitution provides the procedure for adoption of official Language or Languages of the State?345

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art 345 → State Legislature may by law adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as its official language(s) (subject to Arts 346, 347).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Parliament can amend the provision on official language of India under the Constitution by—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Official language (Part XVII, Articles 343 to 351): Articles 343, 344, 346, 348 amended only by Article 368(2) special majority; Official Language Act 1963 (English use) by simple majority. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is correct about the languages mentioned in the Constitution of India?Bodo is a recognized language in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Bodo is in the 8th Schedule (added by 92nd Amendment, 2003); Hindi is the Union's official language (Art 343), not the national language.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Don't call Hindi the 'national language' — Art 343 makes it only the official language of the Union.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which Article of the Constitution provides that every state shall endeavour to provide an adequate facility for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage of education?Article 350-A

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art 350A → every State and local authority to provide mother-tongue teaching at primary stage for linguistic-minority children; President may issue directions (added by 7th Amendment). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under Article 344 of Indian Constitution, the first ‘Official Language Commission’ was established-In 1955 Under the Chairmanship of B.G. Kher

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  First Official Language Commission (Art 344) → appointed 7 June 1955 under B.G. Kher, report 1956; reviewed by Parliamentary Committee under Govind Ballabh Pant (1957).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following languages was added in the eighth schedule of the Constitution in 2003?Santhali

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali; Schedule now 22 (Sindhi by 21st, 1967; Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali by 71st, 1992); Bhojpuri not included. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 2003 four: 'Bo-Do-Ma-San' — Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following languages is / are NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of Indian Constitution?Only 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Bhojpuri is NOT in the Eighth Schedule; Nepali, Dogri and Bodo are among its 22 languages.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Constitution (71 Amendment) Act, 1992 amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  71st Amendment Act, 1992 → Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali added to the Eighth Schedule (not Maithili); 14 languages originally, 22 now.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 71st = 'KoMaNe': Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the language is not included in the VIII Schedule of the constitution?English

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  English is NOT in the Eighth Schedule; the Schedule had 14 languages initially and has 22 now (Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu are in it).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The number of official languages recognised by the constitution in the eight schedule is………—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Eighth Schedule languages: 18 before the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003; 22 after it (none of the printed options fits today). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following states has given the Sanskrit language the status of second official language?Uttarakhand

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Uttarakhand → made Sanskrit its second official language on January 1, 2010; Rishikesh declared a Sanskrit city (CM Ramesh Pokhariyal 'Nishank').

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following languages included in the VIII Schedule of the Constitution is spoken by the largest number of people?Bengali

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Among Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Telugu → Bengali has most speakers (Census 1991, 2001), Telugu second; Census 2011: Hindi first, Bengali second, Marathi third.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is the correct sequence in descending order of the Indian languages, being used as mother tongue?1, 4, 2, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Mother-tongue order, Census 2001: Bengali > Telugu > Marathi > Tamil. Census 2011: Hindi > Bengali > Marathi > Telugu > Tamil.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse Telugu was 2nd in 2001 but Marathi moved ahead of it in 2011 — check which census is meant.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Percentage of Hindi speaking Indians is about:—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Hindi speakers: 41.03% (Census 2001) and 43.63% (Census 2011) — the largest language group in India.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is a language of Baluchistan but from philological aspect it is a language of Dravidian family?Brahui

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Brahui → spoken in Baluchistan but belongs to the Dravidian language family.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Recently the Government of India has approved inclusion of some of the languages in the list of classical languages. Now, how many languages in total are having the status of classical languages?11

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Classical languages now total 11: Tamil first (12 October 2004), Sanskrit 2005, Telugu 2008…; Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali added October 2024.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 2024's five: 'MAPP-B' — Marathi, Assamese, Pali, Prakrit, Bengali.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which Indian languages are accorded the status of Classical Language?More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  11 classical languages: Tamil, Sanskrit, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Odia (earlier) + Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali (3 October 2024).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following languages:2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Classical languages till 2014 (6): Tamil 2004, Sanskrit 2005, Telugu and Kannada 2008, Malayalam 2013, Odia 2014; Gujarati is not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
