                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Fundamental Rights (Part III, Arts 12-35) → from USA: Equality 14-18, Freedom 19-22, Against Exploitation 23-24, Religion 25-28, Culture and Education 29-30. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • From which country, the Indian Constitution has taken reference for the idea of the Fundamental Rights?United States of America

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Idea of Fundamental Rights (Part III) → taken from the Constitution of the USA. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Indian Constitution is divided into –22 Parts

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Original Constitution → 22 Parts, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is not correctly matched under the Constitution of India?Tribunals - Part X

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Panchayats → Part IX; Municipalities → Part IX-A; Co-operative Societies → Part IX-B; Tribunals → Part XIV-A, not Part X (Scheduled and Tribal Areas). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid IX family: IX villages, IX-A towns, IX-B co-operatives.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Indian Constitution consists of –More than 400 Articles

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Original Constitution: 22 Parts, 395 Articles, 8 Schedules; now about 468 Articles (added as 21A, 43B etc.) and 12 Schedules → 'more than 400 Articles'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides for All-Indian Services?Article 312

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  All India Services → Art. 312; Parliament creates them after a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by two-thirds of members present and voting. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:1 2 3 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art. 54 → election of President; Art. 75 → appointment of PM and ministers; Art. 155 → appointment of Governor; Art. 164 → appointment of CM and State ministers. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is matched correctly-Article 352 - Proclamation of Emergency

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Art. 352 → Proclamation of Emergency; Art. 17 → abolition of untouchability; Art. 78 → PM's duty to inform President; Art. 192 → disqualification of State legislators. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following Schedules of the Indian Constitution lists the names of states and specifies their territories?First

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  First Schedule → States and Union Territories; Second → salaries of public officials, Judges, CAG; Third → oaths and affirmations; Fourth → Rajya Sabha seats. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Ifa new state of the Indian Union is to be created, which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution must be amended?First

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Creating a new State or UT → amend the First Schedule (list of States and Union Territories). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists:3 1 4 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  7th Schedule → distribution of legislative powers (three lists); 8th → languages; 9th → validation of certain Acts; 10th → disqualification on defection. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid 7-8-9-10: Lists, Languages, Land laws, Leaving party (defection).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Under the Constitution of India, Economic Planning is a subject:In the Concurrent List

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List, Entry 20; the Planning Commission was set up under this entry. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is the subject of Concurrent List?Criminal Matters

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Criminal law (IPC, now BNS 2023) → Concurrent List; Police → State List; Foreign Affairs, Radio and Television → Union List. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following Subject lies in the Concurrent List?Education

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Education → moved from State List (Entry 11) to Concurrent List by 42nd Amendment, 1976; Concurrent List now has 52 subjects. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Must-know questions: 38

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Hour 56 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Hour 56 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Revise: Schedules to The Citizenship

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    38 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India have a bearing on Education?1, 2, 3, 4 and 5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Education links to all five: DPSP (Art. 45, 86th Amendment 2002), local bodies (Arts 243G, 243W), Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules. Tenth Schedule → anti-defection. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following subject is in List-III Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India?Criminal Procedure

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Criminal Procedure → Concurrent List; Public Order, Prisons, Police → State List. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding Anti-defection law?Tenth Schedule

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Anti-defection law → Tenth Schedule, added by 52nd Amendment Act, 1985; lays down disqualification of legislators on grounds of defection. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Provisions of Schedule sixth of the Constitution does not apply to which of these state?Manipur

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram; Manipur is not covered. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Manipur is a North-East State but not a Sixth Schedule State.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution is related to which of the following?Panchayati Raj

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Eleventh Schedule → Panchayati Raj; added by 73rd Amendment, 1992; 29 subjects. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Memory aid Panchayat trio: 73rd Amendment, Eleventh Schedule, 29 subjects.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The list of powers, authority and responsibilities which may be entrusted to the Panchayats is given in the:Eleventh Schedule

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats → Eleventh Schedule (Art. 243G), added by 73rd Amendment Act 1992; 29 entries. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • What was the exact Constitutional Status of the Indian Republic on 26-1-1950 when the Constitution came into force?A Sovereign Democratic Republic

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    On 26 January 1950 India was 'A Sovereign Democratic Republic'; 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' were added by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which among the following is the correct order mentioned in Preamble of the Indian Constitution?Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble order: Sovereign → Socialist → Secular → Democratic → Republic; then Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The expression "Socialist" was introduced in the Preamble of Indian Constitution by which amendment?42nd amendment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    'Socialist' → added to the Preamble by 42nd Amendment Act (1976), along with 'secular' and 'integrity'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following words was not included in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution in 1975?Integrity

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    'Integrity' was not in the Preamble in 1975; added in 1976 by 42nd Amendment; Fraternity, Sovereign, Equality were original words. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Consider the following statements in regards to the Preamble of Constitution and select the correct one using the code given below -Only 1,2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble: grew from Nehru's Objectives Resolution; non-justiciable; can be amended (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973); cannot override specific provisions of the Constitution. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which of the following words were not present in the preamble of the Indian Constitution adopted on November 26, 1949?(2), (3), (4)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Original Preamble (26 November 1949): Sovereign, Democratic, Republic. 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' added by 42nd Amendment, 1976; 'Reliable', 'Non-religious' never in it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 9 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following liberty is not embodied in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?Economic Liberty

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble liberty → thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; economic liberty is not included. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which part of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘Soul’ of the Constitution?The Preamble

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble → 'Soul of the Constitution'; K.M. Munshi called it the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The ideals and objectives outlined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution have been further elaborated in –The Chapter on Directive Principles of State Policy, Fundamental Rights, and Fundamental Duties

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble's ideals are elaborated in Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties; the Preamble reflects the Constitution's objectives. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • How many types of justice has been enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?Three

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Preamble → 3 types of justice: social, economic and political. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Parliamentary form of Government was first introduced in which country?Great Britain (UK)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Parliamentary form of government first emerged in Great Britain (UK). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The cardinal features of political system in India are –1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Indian political system: democratic republic, parliamentary government, supreme power with the people; no unified authority, as powers are separated between Union and States. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The Central and State governments get authority from?Indian Constitution

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Central and State governments both get their authority from the Constitution, which sets up the parliamentary (Westminster) system at Centre and in States. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is not the Philosophy of the Constitution of India?Communist State

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Constitution's philosophy (Preamble): welfare state, socialist state, political equality through adult franchise; a Communist State is not part of it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ‘India is a Republic’ means -There are no hereditary rulers in India.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    'India is a Republic' → no hereditary ruler; Head of State (President) is elected, indirectly, through people's representatives. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Assertion (A): Indian Constitution is quasi-federal.Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Indian Constitution → quasi-federal (K.C. Wheare), neither purely federal nor unitary; 'federal in nature, unitary in spirit'; Granville Austin → 'Co-operative Federalism'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which of the following critics used the term “Quasi Federal” for the Indian system of government?K.C. Wheare

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    'Quasi-federal' → Prof. K.C. Wheare, in 'Federal Government': India is 'a unitary state with subsidiary federal features'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Memory aid Wheare asks 'where' is the full federation? Answer: only quasi.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • On which of the following dates, Constituent Assembly of India adopted the National Flag?22 July, 1947

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    National Flag's present design adopted by Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947; rectangular, three colours, length to width 3:2. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • India’s National Animal is –Tiger

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    National animal → Tiger (Panthera tigris); Tiger Conservation Project started April 1973. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The power to carve out a new State is vested in –The Parliament

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Power to create new States and alter boundaries, area or names → Parliament (Art. 2: admit or establish; Art. 3: form, alter). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Not the President or a States Reorganisation Commission: only Parliament, by law.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Creation of a new state requires a ....... majority for Constitutional Amendment.Simple

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Creating a new State → simple majority in Parliament, ordinary legislative process; not an amendment under Art. 368. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • How many States and UTs did the States Reorganisation Commission create in 1956?14 States and 6 UTs

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    States Reorganisation (Fazal Ali Commission) → 14 States and 6 UTs on 1 November 1956; Andhra Pradesh, first linguistic State, 1 October 1953. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • How many States and Union Territories are there in India?None of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In 2002: 28 States, 7 UTs; Telangana became 29th State on 2 June 2014; J&K and Ladakh UTs, then Dadra-Daman merger → now 28 States, 8 UTs. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Delhi is a/an –Union territory

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Delhi → Union Territory (First Schedule), the National Capital; special status by 69th Amendment Act, 1991. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Union of India in:1975

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Sikkim → full-fledged State (22nd) in 1975 by the 36th Amendment Act; its Assembly of 32 members was elected in April 1974. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the formation of the following Indian States? Use the code given below to select the correct answer:4, 2, 1, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Order: Sikkim (16 May 1975) → Arunachal Pradesh (1987) → Chhattisgarh (1 November 2000) → Jharkhand (15 November 2000). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Uttarakhand State was created in –the year 2000

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Uttarakhand → formed 9 November 2000 as the 27th State; Jharkhand also came into existence in 2000. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The following States were created after 1960. Arrange them in ascending chronological order of their formation:3, 1, 4, 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Order: Nagaland 1963 → Haryana 1966 → Meghalaya 1972 → Sikkim 1975. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • After Independence, in which year were the Indian States reorganized on the linguistic basis?1956

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    First linguistic State: Andhra Pradesh, October 1953; large-scale reorganisation of States on linguistic basis in 1956. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which of the following is the first State in India formed on the basis of Languages?Andhra Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Andhra Pradesh (October 1953) → first State formed on language basis, by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Memory aid Andhra = 'A' for first; Telugu areas cut from Madras.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Read the following statements with reference to State Reorganization Commission, 1953 and choose the correct option:I and III

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    SRC (Fazal Ali, Panikkar, Kunzru; report September 1955) did not support splitting Bombay and Punjab. States Reorganisation Act 1956 → 14 States and 6 centrally administered territories. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Statement II is false: the SRC did not back splitting Bombay or Punjab.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • In which Part of the Constitution of India we find the provisions relating to citizenship?PART II

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Citizenship → Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Must-know questions: 38

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Hour 57 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Hour 57 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Revise: The Citizenship to Directive Principles of State Policy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      38 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The citizenship provided by the Constitution of India is:Single citizenship

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India → single citizenship for the whole country; USA → dual citizenship (of the federation and of a state). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • When was the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2019 passed by Parliament?11 December, 2019

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2019: Lok Sabha 9 December; Rajya Sabha 11 December 2019 (passed by Parliament); President's assent 12 December 2019. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse 11 December (Parliament passed) with 12 December (President's assent).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Under which Article of the Constitution of India, Fundamental Rights have been provided to citizens?Article 12 to 35

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Fundamental Rights → Part III, Articles 12 to 35; six Fundamental Rights for citizens. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which Article of the Constitution gives precedence to Constitutional provisions over the laws made by the Union Parliament/State Legislatures?13

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Article 13 → pre- or post-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void to that extent; secures paramountcy of the Constitution on Fundamental Rights. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Article 245 = extent of laws by Parliament and States; Article 326 = elections to Lok Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the Indian Constitution, the right to equality is granted by five Articles, They are:Article 14 to Article 18

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Right to Equality → Articles 14 to 18: 14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 public employment; 17 untouchability abolished; 18 titles abolished. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)
