                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Both true, R explains A: Parliament = President + both Houses (Article 79); a Bill becomes law only with the President's assent (Article 111). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution, the President of India enjoys the power to withhold his assent to any Bill passed by both the Houses of the Parliament?Article 111

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Article 111 → President declares assent to, or withholds assent from, a Bill passed by both Houses. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President give his assent to the Ordinance on electoral reforms when it was sent back to him by the Union Cabinet without making any changes (in the year 2002)?Article 123

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2002 electoral reforms ordinance: President assented under Article 123 (ordinance power during Parliament's recess) after the Cabinet sent it back unchanged; ordinance has force of an Act. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the issuance of Ordinance by the President?President can never repeal it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Article 123 ordinances: same force as an Act of Parliament; must be approved within six weeks of reassembly; President can withdraw them any time ('can never repeal' is false). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which among the following is/are appointed by the President of India?1 and 3 are correct

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        President appoints Finance Commission Chairman (Article 280(1)) and UT Chief Ministers (Article 239AA(5)); Planning Commission Vice-Chairman was appointed by the PM (now NITI Aayog). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to consult the Supreme Court?Article 143

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Article 143 → President may consult the Supreme Court on a question of law or fact; its advice is not binding on him. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who of the following was elected President of India unanimously?N. Sanjiva Reddy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Neelam Sanjiva Reddy → the only President elected unanimously (unopposed); tenure 1977 to 1982. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who of the following before becoming the President of India did not hold the office of Vice-President?Neelam Sanjiva Reddy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Neelam Sanjiva Reddy did not serve as Vice-President before becoming President; Radhakrishnan, Zakir Hussain and R. Venkataraman did. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who among the following Chief Justices of India also acted as the President of India?Justice M. Hidayatullah

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah served as acting President from 20 July 1969 to 24 August 1969. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • What is the sequence number of Ms. Pratibha Patil as the President of the Republic of India?12t

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Pratibha Patil → 12th President (25 July 2007 to 25 July 2012), first woman President; 14th by tenure order. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • How is Vice-President of India elected?through election by the MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Vice-President → elected by MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Article 66(1)); not directly, not nominated. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Vice-President may be removed from his office by a resolution of –Council of States

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Vice-President removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution (majority of all members) agreed to by Lok Sabha, after 14 days' notice (Article 67(b)); it starts only in Rajya Sabha. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid VP removal starts in his own House, the Rajya Sabha.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Cabinet means –Ministers with Cabinet Rank

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Cabinet = PM plus Cabinet-rank ministers only; a senior body within the Council of Ministers and the supreme decision-making body. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following statements is correct about the Prime Minister of India?He has full discretion in the choice of persons who are to serve as ministers in his cabinet.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        PM has full discretion in choosing ministers (Art 75(1)); a non-member minister must enter either House within 6 consecutive months, else ceases (Art 75(5)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid 75(5) → '5' looks like 'S' for Six months.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Must-know questions: 38

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Hour 59 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Hour 59 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Revise: The Council of Ministers to The Parliament (1)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          38 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Council of Ministers is responsible to the –—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Council of Ministers → collectively responsible to Lok Sabha; when Lok Sabha is not an option, the nearest answer is Parliament. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to–Only to Lok Sabha

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Union Council of Ministers → collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Don't pick 'Parliament' when 'Only to Lok Sabha' is offered; Rajya Sabha cannot remove the ministry.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Assertion (A): The Council of Ministers in the Union of India is collectively responsible both to the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.(A) is false, but (R) is true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (A) false: Council responsible only to Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)); (R) true: members of either House can be Union Ministers, but vote only in own House. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following motions, the Council of Ministers in India can move?Confidence Motion

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Council of Ministers can move a Confidence Motion; No-Confidence Motion only in Lok Sabha; if passed by Lok Sabha majority → Council must resign. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Confidence Motion (moved by the government) with No-Confidence/Censure Motion (moved against it).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The number of Lok Sabha members required to table a ‘No Confidence Motion’ against the Council of Ministers is50

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          No-Confidence Motion against the Council of Ministers in Lok Sabha → needs at least 50 members to table it. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who advises the Government of India on legal matters?Attorney General

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Art 76 → Attorney General advises Government of India on legal matters; first law officer; appointed by President, holds office during President's pleasure. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Attorney General of India is appointed bythe President of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Attorney General (Art 76) → appointed by the President, holds office at his pleasure (no security of tenure); highest/first law officer of India. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Not appointed by the Law Minister or PM; only the President appoints and removes him.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The chief legal advisor to government of india is:Attorney General of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Chief legal adviser to Government of India → Attorney General (Art 76), part of Union Executive; has right of audience in all courts of India. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse With Solicitor General (second law officer) or Advocate General (State).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          AG: appointed by President; same qualifications as SC judge; need not be an MP; removed by President, not impeached; speaks in Parliament (Art 88) but no vote. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements with reference to Attorney General of India:Only 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Attorney General (Art 76) → holds office at President's pleasure, not PM's; speaks in both Houses but cannot vote; Constitution doesn't require him to resign with the government. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who among the following official can be invited to give his opinion in the Parliament?Attorney General

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Attorney General → can speak and take part in either House, joint sitting and Parliamentary committees (Art 88), but cannot vote; CAG reports laid before Parliament (Art 151). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid AG = Allowed to talk, not Granted a vote.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which officer of the Government of India has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament of India even though he is not a member?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Non-members in Parliament's proceedings → Attorney General (both Houses) and Vice-President (Rajya Sabha only) → 'more than one'; for 'both Houses' the answer is AG. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Solicitor General of India is ……..?Legal Advisor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Solicitor General → legal adviser; second law officer, subordinate to and assists the Attorney General; helped by Additional Solicitor Generals. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who advises the State Government on legal matters?Advocate-General

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          State's legal adviser → Advocate General (Art 165): appointed by Governor, qualified as HC judge (165(1)); advises State (165(2)); holds office at Governor's pleasure (165(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by-President

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          CAG → appointed by President by warrant (Art 148(1)); removed like SC judge; Union audit reports → President; State audit reports → Governor. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The tenure of Comptroller and Auditor General of India is –6 Years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          CAG term → 6 years or age 65, whichever earlier (CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971); service conditions set by Parliament (Art 148(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid CAG: '6 or 65', whichever comes first.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is not true about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?He can be removed by the President.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Not true: 'CAG removed by the President' at will; removed only like an SC judge (Art 148(1)); salary equals SC judge; no further government office (148(4)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Removal order is signed by the President, but only after Parliament's address, as for an SC judge.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Assertion (A): The Duty of Comptroller and AuditorBoth (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          CAG checks not just legality but also propriety of expenditure, as he upholds the Constitution and Parliament's laws in financial administration; he does NOT control issue of public money. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who amongst the following attends the meetings of the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament?Comptroller and Auditor General of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          CAG attends meetings of Parliament's Public Accounts Committee; CAG's duties and powers → Article 149. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the minimum age laid down for a person to seek election to the Lok Sabha?25 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Minimum age: Lok Sabha member → 25 years; Rajya Sabha (Council of States) → 30 years (Article 84(b)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Upper House, older members: Lok 25, Rajya 30.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The state wise seat allocation in Lok Sabha is based on -Population

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          State-wise Lok Sabha seats → allotted by Population (Art 81), on the 1971 Census; equal-ratio rule not applied to States with population up to six million. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The state-wise allocation of seats in Lok Sabha is based on the 1971 Census. Up to which year does this remain intact?2026

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha seat allocation on 1971 Census → frozen till 2026 by 84th Amendment Act, 2001 (Art 81(3) proviso); delimitation of constituencies also frozen. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid 1971 census, frozen till 2026.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The maximum number of members in Lok Sabha can be -550

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Maximum Lok Sabha strength (Art 81) → 550 (530 States + 20 UTs); present strength → 543 (524 States + 19 UTs). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Don't mix 550 (maximum) with 543 (present); 2 Anglo-Indian nominations ended 25 January 2020.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What can be the maximum representation from the Union Territories to the Lok Sabha??20

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Art 81 → not more than 530 members from States and not more than 20 from Union Territories; of 543 seats in 2009, 530 were from States. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How many seats are reserved for UTs in Lok Sabha?20

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha seats for UTs → up to 20 (Art 81); now 19 (Delhi 7, J&K 5, Dadra-Daman 2, others 1 each); UT seats in Rajya Sabha → 8. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If the number of seats allocated to a state in the Lok Sabha is 42, then the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Castes in that state will be:—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          SC/ST seats in a State (Art 330(2)) → in proportion to their population share; e.g. 42-seat West Bengal SC 8 → 10, Andhra 6 → 7 after 2008. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following States has the highest number of reserve seats for the Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?Madhya Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Most ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats → Madhya Pradesh (6); Jharkhand, Odisha 5 each; Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra 4 each; none in UP and Bihar. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who holds power to appoint the nominees from Anglo Indian Community in the Lok Sabha?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Anglo-Indian nominees to Lok Sabha → President could nominate up to 2 (Art 331); provision not extended beyond 25 January 2020 (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment, 2019). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:Only 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Summoning = convocation; Prorogation ends a session; Dissolution ends the House; prorogation is by the President (Art 85(2)), not the leader of the House. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the quorum of Lok Sabha in relation to its strength?1/10

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Quorum of Lok Sabha (and Rajya Sabha) → 1/10 of total members of the House (Art 100(3)). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In India which State has the largest representation in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Largest representation in both Houses → Uttar Pradesh: 80 Lok Sabha seats, 31 Rajya Sabha seats. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid UP = 80 + 31.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • So long as the representation in Lok Sabha is concerned, which states rank second and third?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha seats now: UP 80, Maharashtra 48 (second), West Bengal 42 (third), Bihar 40, Tamil Nadu 39, Madhya Pradesh 29. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following pair of States has equal seats in Lok Sabha?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Equal Lok Sabha seats (before 2014) → Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal, 42 each; Telangana took 17, Andhra now 25; Punjab 13, Assam 14, Gujarat 26, Rajasthan 25. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • First General Election of Lok Sabha was held in-1952

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          First Lok Sabha general election → 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952, for 489 seats; first session began 13 May 1952. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha submits his resignation to?The Deputy Speaker

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Lok Sabha Speaker resigns by writing addressed to the Deputy Speaker (Article 94). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Not to the President; the Speaker's resignation letter goes to the Deputy Speaker.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How can the speaker of the Lok Sabha be removed?By a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a majority of all the members of the House.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Speaker removed by a Lok Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all the then members (Art 94(c)), after at least 14 days' notice. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Speaker of the Lok Sabha makes use of his casting vote only –In case of a tie when votes are equally divided

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Speaker uses his casting vote only in case of a tie (equality of votes), under Article 100(1). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha of India?Shri Ganesh Vasudev Mavlankar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          First Lok Sabha Speaker → G.V. Mavalankar (1952-1956); then M. Ananthasayanam Iyengar (1956-1962), Hukum Singh (1962-1967); Om Birla since 2019. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Must-know questions: 33

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Hour 60 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Hour 60 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Revise: The Parliament (1) to Parliamentary Committees

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            38 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha?G.V. Mavalankar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            First Speaker of Lok Sabha → G.V. Mavalankar (15 May 1952 till his death, 27 February 1956); called 'Father of the Lok Sabha' by Nehru. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The first Speaker against whom a Motion of No confidence was moved in the Lok Sabha was –G.V. Mavalankar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            First Speaker to face a no-confidence motion → G.V. Mavalankar; moved by Vigneshwar Missir and J.B. Kripalani, 15 December 1954; rejected 18 December 1954. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The first female Speaker of Lok Sabha isMeira Kumar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            First woman Speaker of Lok Sabha → Meira Kumar, chosen unopposed; served June 2009 to June 2014. Must know
